evidence_detail: Weblate-managed application locales translate user-facing controls and use ICU for locale-specific plural/number/date messages. Inspected French catalogue covers account settings, albums, tags, uploads and actions; this is UI localization, not multilingual CLIP search. Translation completeness varies and was not measured.
Server manages owned uploads and mounted media without requiring a third-party photo-storage account.
Documented server/ML containers and volume mounts support split workers and optional remote ML.
Browser upload/view, administration, people, tags and sharing are explicitly in the client matrix.
Android mobile app offers backup, viewing and platform-specific charging/delay controls.
iOS app supports selective/background backup subject to OS scheduling and Background App Refresh.
Web/mobile/CLI originals are copied into managed upload storage with separate derivatives.
Choose included/excluded device albums, upload on app open/resume and background opportunities; Wi-Fi-only is default, configurable. Individual local-only assets can be uploaded manually.
Creates/merges same-named server albums and backfills existing uploads. Later local deletes/reordering do not propagate; matching already-shared server albums share the newly added media.
Selected iOS albums can pull missing iCloud assets into temporary device cache for hashing/upload, then clear temporary files; requires extra data and device space.
Mobile/CLI hashes avoid re-uploading known content across upload methods/devices; server still hashes if CLI prehash is skipped. Upload-library scope is not global across accounts/external libraries.
External files appear in normal timeline/maps/albums after scanning without managed-copy import; modified source files require rescan.
One external library can recursively scan multiple mounted roots, adding a path only once when roots overlap.
Nightly scans and manually triggered scans refresh libraries; admin can select presets or a cron schedule.
Advanced-user watcher auto-imports changes but may fail on network drives and requires sufficient OS watcher capacity.
Per-library full-path patterns exclude extensions/subtrees; matching existing assets are offlined on later scan. CLI also accepts ignore globs.
Enable folder view to navigate external directory trees or template-organized managed assets.
Admin templates control directory/filename pattern using date/name/album and conditional fields; migration jobs apply changes retroactively. Date variables use server timezone.
Default UUID names avoid filename collisions; template collisions append a sequence number rather than overwrite.
Clients download photos/videos; edited assets default to edited output but original version can be selected.
Official CLI documentation recommends separate community-maintained immich-go for Google Photos Takeout rather than claiming native CLI Takeout parsing.
Mobile/web matrix documents draggable timeline scrollbars, with external and uploaded media appearing together.
README explicitly lists virtual scroll on both mobile and web; this is stronger evidence than ordinary lazy image loading.
Both clients view uploaded videos and use separately generated compatibility transcodes; originals remain unchanged.
README marks 360-degree display available on web, not mobile.
Both clients show past-date memories; scheduled generation defaults to nightly tasks.
Both clients support stacked photos; duplicate review can stack multiple retained candidates.
Favorites are available on both clients, usable as filters and merged when resolving a duplicate group to one keeper.
Archive hides media from main timeline/folder view but retains it in search and a dedicated archive view; not a privacy vault.
View EXIF/GPS and filter camera make/model/lens; extracted metadata drives location/date behavior.
Reads supported description/rating/date/GPS/tag fields; filename.ext.xmp wins over filename.xmp. Other sidecar fields remain stored but are not searchable.
Tags can be imported from IPTC Keywords as well as XMP hierarchical tag fields; not a claim of full IPTC coverage.

Selected edited metadata is written to XMP without replacing unrelated fields; managed imports copy sidecars, and external write-back requires a writable mount. Discover/Sync jobs handle later sidecars.
Enable Tags view, create/assign tags to photos/videos and navigate by tag; README limits Tags UI to web.
Assign searchable star ratings and read/write XMP Rating; duplicate resolution preserves highest group rating.
Descriptions are editable/searchable and written to dc:description/tiff:ImageDescription sidecar fields.
Timestamp edits are supported and XMP DateTimeOriginal/DateCreated fields are written; read-only external mounts prevent editing.
Location edits persist in database/XMP GPS latitude/longitude, not original file bytes; read-only external mounts cannot accept edits.
PostgreSQL/VectorChord searches image embeddings against freeform text without requiring explicit keywords; supported model choices trade accuracy, latency and memory.
Choose supported multilingual models; nllb uses the user's language setting while xlm/siglip2 understand language independently. Changing models requires rerunning Smart Search.
Full/partial filenames, extensions, folder names and original path fragments are searchable.
Filter descriptions, camera/lens, albums and archive/favorite/not-in-album state alongside other search criteria.
Search with start/end time bucket dates.
Restrict search to images, videos or both and filename extensions.
Search city/state/country generated by local reverse geocoding.
Filter assets containing one or more recognized faces and browse a named person's media.
Filter assigned/imported tags and open tag-specific media views.
Advanced search explicitly includes user-assigned star ratings.
Search text inside images; background pipeline explicitly includes an OCR job after thumbnail generation.
OCR is a first-class background processing task; optional supported acceleration also covers OCR model processing.
ML service processes generated previews into scored boxes and face embeddings; configurable detection score filters false positives.
Recognition compares saved face embeddings and assigns identities; on videos this is only faces visible in the generated thumbnail, not full-video analysis.
DBSCAN-derived clustering uses recognition distance/core-point minimums, preserves prior people incrementally and revisits unassigned candidates nightly.
Name groups, change feature photo, hide people and favorite/pin them; set birthdate to show age when an image was taken.
Merge detected people, manually assign unassigned faces and requeue missing/all recognition after tuning; existing results may need reprocessing.
FAQ says embedded asset face/person metadata creates faces and people on import; not limited to new ML discovery.
Default ML container processes previews on the self-hosted system and downloads missing models; inference is not synonymous with a guaranteed air-gapped first run.
Send preview images to another ML container, optionally retaining local fallback. URLs are tried sequentially, not load-balanced; recognition clustering remains server/database-side.
Experimental ARM NN, CUDA, ROCm, OpenVINO and RKNN backends have model/device/driver limits; ARM NN does not accelerate query-time text search.
Enabled-by-default ML utility groups visually similar assets for review; distinct from exact upload checksum deduplication.
Choose which candidates to retain/trash; suggested keeper preference uses larger byte size then richer EXIF count, not a measured aesthetic-quality score.
More than one asset can be retained and optionally stacked; retained assets then keep their own metadata rather than merging it.

Only exactly one keeper plus at least one trashed asset triggers merge: union albums/tags, any favorite, highest rating, combined descriptions, most restrictive visibility and GPS only when nonempty coordinates agree.
Create albums and add uploaded/external assets; albums are independent of physical storage unless optional template behavior uses album names.
CLI --album creates albums from each uploaded file's containing folder or --album-name targets one album. External-library scans do not natively create matching albums.
Explore people and view all assets containing a selected person's face.
Client matrix and supported-format table establish RAW/RW2 support; full decoder/extension list is maintained separately.
Both HEIC and HEIF are explicitly supported image formats.
AVIF is explicitly supported.
JPEG XL .jxl is explicitly supported.
Supported-format table includes SVG.
README explicitly lists Apple Live Photo backup and playback on mobile and web.
Motion Photo backup/playback appears in both client columns.
Crop creates an edited version and can be reverted to the original.
Photo edit controls include rotation and mirroring.
Image edits create another version; metadata writes use sidecars/database. Original bytes are retained, though emptying trash can delete originals.
Transcode policy generates web-compatible derivatives without replacing originals; changing policy and rerunning jobs can delete unnecessary transcodes.
NVENC/QSV/RKMPP/VAAPI can accelerate encoding, with optional decoding. Hardware, codec, Linux/WSL and quality/size tradeoffs apply; Raspberry Pi is unsupported in this guide.
Both clients display geotagged assets on a global map; map tile/style services are distinct from local reverse geocoding.
GeoNames data is loaded into PostgreSQL on minor upgrades; city/state/country queries then run locally.
Set separate light/dark style JSON URLs and choose another tile provider rather than the default tiles.immich.cloud styles. Offline basemap provisioning is not established.
Multiple users own assets and libraries, with admin-managed passwords and per-user settings; accounts are not counted as selectable multiple catalogues.
Assign shared users read-write editor or read-only viewer permissions on albums.
Instance users can contribute their own photos/videos to shared albums when given editor permission.
Random-secret URLs share selected photos/videos or albums with non-users and configurable permitted actions.
Public links can require a password.
Public-link configuration includes an expiration date.
Permit non-account visitors to contribute photos/videos into the owner's account using a configured public share.
Grant broad asset/metadata/download/resharing access with optional per-partner timeline inclusion. Person data and favorites are not shared; both parties must grant separately for reciprocity.
Admins set GiB quotas that block further upload when exceeded; external libraries do not count against the quota.

Locked Folder hides assets until session unlock; access initially lasts 15 minutes and can extend with activity. While unlocked, locked assets may appear in search/utilities; Lock/sign-out revokes access.
README marks offline support on mobile, not web. Inspected docs do not specify guarantees that all remote originals/search/models are available offline.
Docker :ro protects external original files; metadata edits also cannot persist, and files trashed in UI can return after trash-empty/rescan because disk deletion is denied.
Trash delays permanent deletion. Missing external files move to trash on rescan and restoration requires restoring the source; their metadata is discarded after documented 30-day removal.
Review/delete only device assets already backed up and not in server trash, with cutoff date, keep favorites/albums and keep photo/video options; iCloud Shared Album items are excluded.
Free Up Space confirms a reviewed list then moves assets to native trash in batches (Android 2000/iOS 10000); manually empty OS trash to reclaim space immediately.
Read-only app mode permits timeline viewing while preventing accidental device photo deletion; not an encrypted vault.

Default daily 2am dumps retain 14 copies; manual backups and UI restore are supported. Restore creates a rollback point, migrates/checks health and rolls back on failure. Media is not in database dumps.
Scheduled checks compare stored/actual checksums and detect missing/untracked paths; checks default nightly at 3am with configurable time/progress budgets and refresh-only-reported options.
Read/write marker checks validate expected storage mounts and permissions; failed checks normally prevent server startup.
Job pipeline covers metadata, template migration, thumbnails, smart search, faces, OCR, video and duplicates, plus separately configurable nightly jobs; admin views job state.
Include/exclude worker settings let containers isolate web/API work from background processing and distribute resources.
Maintains blurred thumbhash, WebP previews, JPEG thumbnails and person face thumbnails in derivative storage.
Queue missing/all thumbnail/transcode jobs separately from originals; policy changes can remove unnecessary encoded video without deleting original media.
Notify new users, users added to shared albums and collaborators about new assets; per-user controls and custom HTML templates are documented.
Account settings show usage and admins can see per-user quota percentages in Server Stats.
Documented OpenAPI with generated TypeScript/Dart clients; web users create API keys with restricted permissions and can manage logged-in devices.
CLI supports recursive paths, globs, albums, visibility, dry run, JSON output, upload concurrency, filesystem watching and explicit local-delete/delete-duplicate options.

Configure third-party provider, mobile/web redirects, auto-registration/launch and backchannel logout. Role/quota claims can synchronize on login; default storage label is registration-only unless changed.
Experimental photo/video Cast requires Google scripts, public HTTPS/reachable Google DNS and Cast-compatible video formats.
Cast manual explicitly reserves Android/iOS support for future development.
FAQ limits current video face recognition to a generated thumbnail and mentions possible future whole-video scanning.
FAQ explicitly says NSFW image filtering is unavailable; an open request is not an implemented feature.
FAQ says manual reordering is not yet available and links a planned-feature discussion.

PhotoPrism provides its library browsing, metadata editing, organization and sharing interface through a web browser. PWA installation is optional and is not a native Windows/macOS or mobile application distribution.

Official tar packages can run the PhotoPrism server directly on compatible Linux distributions without Docker. They require manual configuration, updates and installation of system dependencies; this is a native server distribution with a browser interface, not a Linux desktop GUI package.

Official documentation offers fully managed hosting through selected partners, and the personal-edition comparison lists PikaPods as a paid managed deployment. Provider plans and feature availability differ from a self-hosted installation.

The October 2026 release explicitly discusses missing user-interface translations, fixes the sign-in language picker and invites native-speaker translation improvements. Account roles can retain a personal language preference; this is UI localization, not multilingual image search.

Places can switch to a globe that rotates, zooms and tilts; the guide says it works with all map styles and can combine with terrain mode. Paid satellite/terrain map services remain a separate capability.

The edition comparison lists OpenID Connect SSO for self-hosted Community, Essentials and Plus. WebDAV documentation explains that OIDC-authenticated accounts use app passwords instead of their account password for WebDAV; provider-specific configuration was not inspected.
Runs server under owner control with web UI; Docker supports AMD64/ARM64 on multiple host OSes, not native desktop installers.
Stable and preview images include converters/dependencies; CE and standard extension-bundled images have distinct licensing terms.
Browser app can be installed on phone/tablet/desktop home screen; this does not establish a native mobile background-backup service.
SQLite and MariaDB supported; October release adds explicitly experimental PostgreSQL and database-transfer CLI. MySQL 8 support is discontinued.
Indexing leaves existing file/folder names unchanged, reads metadata and writes derived data outside originals by default.
Host folders/drives can be mounted as subfolders below one originals tree; this is one catalogue over multiple mounts, not isolated per-user libraries.
Folders and hierarchical Originals views reflect source organization; next index updates paths after media is moved within originals.
Copies by default or moves from import to originals; unsupported files remain in import. Web uploads follow import semantics rather than direct originals upload.
Imports assign unique filenames and year/month directories while preserving original name as indexed property; advanced destination patterns can be configured but do not rename existing imports.
Index all or selected subfolder; Complete Rescan includes unchanged files and preserves manually entered labels/people/titles/captions.
Optional scheduled rescans and default five-minute safety delay after WebDAV changes; concurrent scans and slow transfers can produce load or incomplete sets.
Automatic hidden-prefix exclusions plus directory-scoped .ppignore wildcard rules; rules do not retroactively remove already indexed items/stacks.
Reads Google Photos JSON sidecars and Apple XMP during indexing; this establishes metadata ingestion, not authenticated cloud sync or complete Takeout repair.
Compatible apps such as PhotoSync can back up iOS/Android media in background via WebDAV; companion licensing/OS behavior is external to PhotoPrism.
Duplicates are skipped; Move import also deletes duplicate sources as though successfully moved, so it is a destructive source-cleanup choice.
Index detects/skips matching SHA-1+size files so they appear once in results/albums; no byte-confirmation claim is documented.
Manual explicitly says browsing and deleting duplicates in web UI is future work; automatic suppression is already present.
Same-folder basename companions always stack, including RAW/JPEG and hybrid image/video; this mandatory rule cannot be disabled.
XMP/JSON and other same-origin sidecars remain associated with media stack; permanent deletion removes related sidecars as well.
Optional sequential-name, same-second/position and Unique Image/XMP Instance ID grouping; choose primary preview or unstack nonprimary image. Changing rules does not auto-unstack old groups.
Cards show title/time/location, mosaic emphasizes imagery, list shows metadata; selectable light/dark themes.
Calendar organizes media by time taken, complemented by regions, people, labels, folders and favorites navigation.
Fullscreen viewing supports caption/sidebar toggles, editing and direct export/download.
Viewer starts/pauses slideshows; Live Photos play when viewed in slideshow or hovered.
Shortcuts include fullscreen, slideshow, info/caption/mute/favorite, edit, archive/restore and download/export.
Result-view manual explicitly offers multiple light/dark themes; paid premium theme availability is not conflated with baseline theme switching.
Space combines filters with AND; supported fields permit & or |, label groups permit leading !, and names/captions accept escaped operators/wildcards. Not universal arbitrary boolean syntax.
Separate name, filename, original and path filters support wildcards. Searches operate on files, so narrowly matching extensions can exclude a stack's companion video.
Filter camera, lens, aperture, focal length, ISO, codec, captions/titles, hashes and source IDs, along with flags for private/archive/review/errors.
Year/month/day and taken/before/after plus added/edited/updated timestamps can be combined.
Filter image/RAW/live/video/animated/audio/vector/document and stacked/unstacked/primary/unsorted states; filter presence alone does not establish each format's full playback semantics.
Resolution ranges plus portrait/landscape/square/panorama conditions are documented.
Search standard dominant colors, chroma and monochrome flag; file-level results distinguish color/monochrome variants in stacks.
Country/state/city/category, coordinates with distance, bounding boxes, altitude, Open Location Code, S2 cell and nearby-photo UID filters.
Exact person or partial people names with conjunction/disjunction, face IDs/new faces and minimum face counts; can combine with date/place filters.
Search manual/generated labels, category expansion and keywords with supported boolean combinations.
Built-in EXIF parser plus optional ExifTool normalizes and merges camera/time/location data; changed files are reread when mtime changes.
ExifTool extracts IPTC together with embedded EXIF/XMP into JSON sidecars; disabling it reduces metadata support.
Standalone XMP fields take precedence, including documented GPS/altitude/subject multiword keywords; embedded XMP requires ExifTool. Support is selective, not all XMP schemas.
Enable Import Faces from XMP to reuse names/regions from Bridge, Lightroom, digiKam, ACDSee or Windows rather than reentering them.
Indexer/editor creates human-readable YAML sidecars unless disabled and ExifTool JSON extracts; manual YAML edits are not synchronized back to overwrite existing index.
Add/rename/remove labels; renaming affects all assigned pictures. Removing generated label sets confidence zero for reactivation; globally deleting prevents reapplication until deliberately restored.
Generated labels belong to searchable broader groups such as vehicle; category grouping is not user-editable hierarchy.
Edit title, caption, copyright, camera/lens and private notes; title/caption/keywords searchable, Notes ignored. Manual changes survive rescans.
Details editor changes dates while preserving user overrides through indexing; release fixes timezone adjustment behavior. General embedded timestamp writing is not provided.
Paste decimal coordinate pair or use built-in map/place search in Details. This is catalogue geotagging, not a claim that GPS is written into original EXIF.
When enabled, edits up to 999 selected pictures or a subset. Mixed values indicate replacement scope; partially assigned chips can add to all or remove from all.
Like media for Favorites view and quality review; starring people/labels sorts them first.
Except image orientation, PhotoPrism explicitly does not write changed metadata back into originals to avoid conflicts/data loss.
Choose correct orientation in Files tab; writes original metadata and is unavailable in read-only mode.
Current built-in YuNet detects faces; only primary stack image is scanned, and small/rotated/low-contrast faces may be missed.
Current SFace embeddings compare faces; legacy libraries keep FaceNet until migration. Recognition starts after full library scan and can be CPU-intensive.
Groups similar faces, updates clusters after new data/corrections and can auto-name a consistent cluster when enough recognized members agree; New Faces shows clusters, not every unknown face.
Name in People, photo editor or info sidebar, rename person globally and select a representative face cover.
Bad matches remove or replace identity and update cluster thresholds in background; false positives can be removed with undo only before reload.
Info Sidebar permits manual region marking missed by detection; 360-degree content explicitly does not support manual marking yet.
Private/hidden people withhold names/regions from viewers/guests/visitors and remove names from generated titles after maintenance; pictures remain visible, so this is not redaction/encryption.
Default ONNX classification generates labels/categories; model can be replaced or set to none without removing existing labels.
ONNX label/NSFW/face models run locally without model-service setup; maps and optional hosted AI are separate network dependencies.
Configure Ollama or OpenAI for natural-language captions and labels; self-hosted Ollama recommends GPU, OpenAI needs API key/network. Not an established native semantic-search engine.
OpenAI/Ollama Cloud send images to configured service endpoints with API keys; configurable prompts/models/thresholds and service credentials, no requests to these hosts without key.
vision.yml supports auto/manual/on-index/newly-indexed/on-demand/on-schedule/always/never modes; on-index limited to built-in local models to avoid blocking ingestion.
Built-in ONNX models can use NVIDIA GPU; Ollama model/GPU/thread options are configurable. Documented timings are project claims, not benchmarks performed here.
NSFW detector can mark potentially objectionable images private; docs call it only partly reliable and older indexed images need rescan.

Review score uses known date/GPS, resolution, non-screenshot classification and favorite/edit/approval; low scores are withheld until approved unless disabled. Not blur/aesthetic scoring; manual says 1–5 while filter reference permits 1–7.
Create/edit albums, add selection to multiple albums, remove membership and choose cover; album deletion differs from file deletion.
Moments are continuously updated time/place or content-label collections such as country/year or pets; no arbitrary user-defined smart-query builder is claimed.
Regions group images by location; time/place Moments supplement map navigation.
View/download all a person's photos and add that selection to manual albums.
All users receive hosted high-resolution OSM-based vector map; Places plots GPS media, supports search and requires WebGL 2.
Click grouped map markers for overlay and open associated photos in search; map can be restricted with most normal search filters.
PhotoPrism location service resolves coordinates to places; disabling Places retains indexed GPS but disables lookups/map UI. Community geocoding is rate-limited.
Essentials/Plus provide additional MapTiler satellite/outdoor/3D styles and enhanced geocoding; standard hosted vector map remains free. Globe viewer works across styles.
Docker includes Darktable/RawTherapee; generated JPEG/PNG previews serve browser/ML use, outside originals by default. Camera support depends on converters.
Supported with converted browser previews; heif-convert may not honor JPEG resolution limit.
Format table includes AVIF/sequences; preview conversion is distinct from browser-native display and converter resolution constraints.
JPEG XL generates JPEG/PNG preview sidecars for thumbnail/recognition where browsers cannot render original.
Plus edition includes vector graphics support, with SVG/AI/EPS/PS listed in format reference; not attributed to free core merely because format table lists them.
GIF animation plays natively; ExifTool should remain enabled to extract duration/resolution.
Still/video companions stack and play on hover/slideshow; live search filters and dedicated navigation.
Live filter explicitly includes Motion and Live Photos; detailed phone-specific extraction matrix not established.
FFmpeg is required for video indexing stills; ExifTool supplies duration/resolution/codec. Supported browser codecs stream directly under documented bitrate rules.
Converts unsupported codecs to MPEG-4 AVC on first play or convert CLI; first-play latency/storage can be large. Existing AVC is not re-encoded even above bitrate limit.
Video guide explicitly supports configured hardware transcoding; exact device/driver matrix was not inspected.
Equirectangular content opens sphere viewer with pan/zoom/playback. Metadata identifies still projections; panorama flag plus roughly 2:1 frame identifies video; other projections stay flat.
INSV/INSP/fisheye DNG become equirectangular derivatives using known camera FOV or configured fallback; dual-lens video/proxy files stack and originals stay unchanged.
Download selected photos, individual Files-tab items or whole albums/moments/person collections; configure which stack files are included.
Admins/Users export originals, full-size previews, resized JPEGs or playable video renditions with per-download retry; Viewers/Guests/Visitors may download but not use Export.
Share manual albums, Moments, Months, Regions or Folders; visitors view/download only nonprivate media and cannot edit. Reusing secret can share multiple albums.
Each collection can have different secret/expiry links; links can be deleted independently.
Share manual explicitly describes optional password protection as planned, distinct from existing secret URLs and authenticated guest accounts.
All editions have account CLI; Community includes Admin, Guest and Visitor, with full library or shared-only scope. Accounts are not separate selectable libraries.
Admins have unrestricted library/settings access; guests read shared content; anonymous visitors only shared resources. Superadmin flag prevents accidental role lockout and controls global flags.
Essentials/Plus add editable-library User without global settings and read-only Viewer excluding private/archive and uploads/indexing.
Plus adds UI for accounts/sessions; account deletion disables/signs out but retains account record and uploaded pictures. CLI remains in all editions.
Account 2FA uses compatible authenticator, one-time recovery code disabling 2FA, and administrator reset path.
App passwords support WebDAV-only scope; even Full Access app credentials cannot change account password or manage users.
Mount originals/import to open/edit/delete remotely and sync external WebDAV servers; auth required, disabled in public mode, HTTPS required outside trusted local network.

October release adds search/browse and metadata/format/command lookups, enabled for eligible roles with per-account/global disable options; external assistants can access authorized library information.
Release adds authorization-code app/remote-MCP connections; PHOTOPRISM_OAUTH_APPS=none can block external app authorization.
CLI provides index/import/convert/cleanup/thumb regeneration, backup, account management and database transfer; reset is destructive to index and requires backup.
Disables original-writing features including import/upload/delete/WebDAV; optional Docker :ro mounts enforce OS-level protection. Derivative conversion remains possible outside originals.

Archive hides without deleting, and restore returns media; album membership is removed on archive and not automatically restored. This is reversible catalogue archive, not OS trash or retained deleted bytes.
Delete must be enabled; archived files can be selected or all removed with confirmation. Originals and sidecars are removed permanently, cached derivatives on later cleanup.
Default daily database dumps retain up to three; album/YAML backup switches and manual commands available. Full recovery also needs originals and preferably storage/config, copied separately.
Can pause index/import/upload below configured free-space percentage with 100 MB floor; disabled by default because network/FUSE/container probes may be unreliable.
JPEG thumbnail matrix is hash-addressed outside originals, with Lanczos3 rendering and up to 16K previews; static minimum 720 px supports ML.
Independent static/dynamic size limits and Dynamic Previews reduce disk use at cost of latency/CPU; smaller/lower-quality analysis thumbnails can impair recognition.
Face clusters update after indexing/corrections, optional AI has scheduled metadata-worker modes, and fisheye originals convert asynchronously.
Still/document/RAW conversion defaults to ten-minute timeout; -1 disables it. Video uses a separate timeout disabled by default.

Cleanup deletes unused thumbnails/orphan index entries when requested with indexing/CLI, not on schedule, and skips empty originals; thumbnail regeneration and full index reset are distinct operations.
Debug mode exposes logs under Library > Logs after restart; advanced configuration changes require restart.
People manual lists automatic YAML backup of tagged people as upcoming; general metadata sidecars must not be assumed to fully back up face identities.
Krokiet has prebuilt portable Windows 10/11 desktop binaries; release notes distinguish current Krokiet from legacy GTK packages.
Release distribution includes Krokiet macOS x86_64 and ARM64 desktop builds; this is a native frontend, not a browser served from a container.
Krokiet supplies prebuilt Linux desktop executables; the manual documents glibc 2.17+ and optional ffmpeg requirements for relevant video tools.

README explicitly documents multiple interface languages including Polish, English and Italian. Krokiet's Language setting changes the UI immediately without restart; this is interface translation, not multilingual content search.
Included paths accepts multiple directories with recursive traversal and optional other-filesystem exclusion; scans operate on existing files without import.
Groups by size, then first/last 4 KB prehash, then full-file hash. Blake3 is default; CRC32 and XXH3 are alternatives with different collision characteristics.
Name, size and combined name+size modes avoid content reads; case sensitivity is configurable and docs explicitly warn these methods produce false positives.
Krokiet manual explicitly says hash duplicate matching does not perform byte-by-byte comparison.

BK-tree/Hamming-distance matching with six hash algorithms, 8/16/32/64 hash sizes, resize filters and distance threshold; optionally ignores same-size or same-resolution groups. EXIF orientation is applied before hashing.
Optional comparison setting adds mirror/flip and 90-degree rotation variants; changed invariance/hash/filter parameters create distinct cached signatures.

Requires ffmpeg/ffprobe. Compares perceptual frame sequences in temporal windows with duration tolerance, minimum matching-window fraction, letterbox detection and shorter-clip containment thresholds; presets include near-identical, similar and long-skip movie scans.

Separate audio comparison mode uses similarity, shorter/longer duration ratio, minimum duration and maximum audio difference; Krokiet manual says this mode itself does not require ffmpeg, unlike visual hashing/thumbnails.

Match selected title/artist/bitrate/genre/year/length tags, optionally approximate title/artist; alternatively compare content fingerprints with minimum matching segment and difference thresholds. Empty selected tags are not grouped.
Ref paths participate as keeper references but are protected from selection/removal; all-reference scans are refused. Link actions target a group's reference file where present.
Excluded directories, whole-path glob patterns, include/exclude extensions and image/video/music/text extension groups restrict scans; default exclusions cover common system/cache locations.
Global minimum/maximum size filters apply to appropriate tools; empty files, temporary files and largest/smallest scans explicitly ignore these bounds.

Select one or all except oldest/newest/biggest/smallest, shortest/longest path, and for images resolution; custom selection and group inversion are available. Highlighting and action checkboxes are deliberately distinct.
Select-all/inversion may check every member; deletion popup reports how many groups have every file checked rather than silently treating all actions as keep-one.
Unselect-all or removing rows only from displayed results leaves files on disk; result hiding is not documented as a persistent review decision.
CLI and Krokiet share full/prehash, perceptual image/video, music and scan caches; binary caches have JSON fallback and optional JSON export, with image parameters in cache keys.

Group action keeps the reference or first checked file and links other checked members; requires at least two checked members without a reference. Applicable even to similar-media groups, so user judgment matters.
Softlink action follows the same reference/first-checked keeper rule as hardlink; release notes explicitly mention surfacing rollback rename failures.
Save creates text, pretty JSON and compact JSON files; results cannot be loaded back into the GUI.
Preview pane displays a highlighted image; Similar Images has a side-by-side Compare overlay. Video preview uses separately enabled thumbnails or thumbnail grids.
Returns configurable N biggest or smallest files, default 50, excluding zero-byte files.
Finds zero-byte files, with extra checks for all-null content and non-visible-ASCII-only content; the latter can match non-Latin text, an explicit caution in the GUI manual.
Reports topmost all-empty branches. Excluded/unreadable folders, symlinks or entries on another filesystem prevent a directory being declared empty.
Case-insensitive suffix matching includes download remnants, backups, cache/dump files and OS artifacts; users can replace/reset the suffix list.
Flags nonexistent targets and excessive/circular link chains; deletion removes the link, not its target.
Parses images, audio, PDFs, archives, fonts and markup using type-specific libraries; errors are candidates for manual verification, not guaranteed corruption.
Off-by-default ffprobe header checks and slow ffmpeg full-decode checks require external ffmpeg; videos are otherwise not checked by Broken Files.
Magic-byte detection produces compatible-extension suggestions; Rename applies fixes and skips collisions with a warning.

Configurable rules cover uppercase extensions, emoji, edge whitespace, non-ASCII/transliteration, restricted character sets and repeated punctuation; results show proposed names and collision failures are reported.

Finds metadata-bearing images and strips non-ignored tags; default preserved tag is Orientation. Cleaning supports library-dependent JPEG/PNG/TIFF/WebP/JXL/HEIF formats and creates a named cleaned copy unless overwrite is enabled.
Requires ffmpeg; excludes configurable already-efficient codecs and offers target codec, CRF, denoising, frame-size/fps limits, fail-if-bigger, overwrite and custom commands.
ffmpeg-backed optimization detects black bars or static edge content using thresholds/sample limits and applies the proposed crop to selected files.
Optimizer offers NVENC, VAAPI, QSV, VideoToolbox and AMF, contingent on ffmpeg and the platform encoder.
Current manual documents built-in rawler RAW decoding; optional libraw replaces the decoder rather than being mandatory.
Similar-image support requires a build with the heif feature and relevant system libraries; not inferred from EXIF-cleaning format support.
Requires the libavif build feature and associated libraries.
JXL is listed among supported similar-image extensions in the current Krokiet manual.

Treemap and sunburst views provide file-type toggles, folder drilldown, type detection choices and detail thresholds. Uses file sizes rather than allocated space, counts hardlinks per name and does not follow symlinks.
Move popup can copy instead, preserve folder structure and either skip conflicts or rename to avoid them.

Separate Trash action for checked scan results is recoverable through the OS, while Delete is permanent; trash may fail on network shares. Disk-usage chart's similarly named action is explicitly not functional.
Checkboxes determine actions independently of highlighted preview rows, and delete popup flags groups with all members selected; reference rows are protected.
EXIF cleaning defaults to writing a .czkawka_cleaned_exif copy; overwrite is an explicit popup option.
Thread count can be set, with zero meaning all CPU threads; changing it requires restart. Speed claims are project claims, not tested benchmarks.
Action bar switches between Scan and Stop during work.
With ffmpeg, generate a single position-based thumbnail or tiled grid; CLI pre-scanning populates GUI cache, and unused thumbnails older than seven days can be cleaned at startup.
Automatic stale-record cleanup and a manual Clean outdated cache action remove entries for changed/missing files; separate global and per-preset settings are stored as JSON.
General settings include completion sound and desktop notification switches.
Ten user presets save roots, filters and tool parameters, plus a reserved command-line-path slot; custom selection rules are separately persisted.
Separate command-line frontend shares the core and caches; release 12.0.2 also adds starting a Krokiet scan through command-line arguments.
UI-independent czkawka_core exposes scan configuration, typed results and shared functionality for other applications.
README explicitly states no Internet access and no collection of user information/statistics.
Arrow/page/home/end navigation, shift-range highlighting, Space check/uncheck, Enter open and Ctrl+A highlight are documented.
Dark theme and UI language settings apply without restarting.
Prebuilt Windows 10/11, macOS and Linux binaries require no installation; optional media builds/runtime dependencies remain separate.
Repository supplies a touch-oriented Cedinia frontend; its supported tools differ from Krokiet and GTK.

Photos mobile v1.3.66 explicitly adds Korean UI language support and updates translations across sharing, account recovery, cleanup and onboarding; v1.3.67 restores missing translations. This is interface localization, separate from Magic Search query-language support; equal language coverage across clients is not asserted.
Encrypts original media and metadata on the client; security FAQ identifies XChaCha20/XSalsa20, Poly1305 and Argon2id. Server operators do not receive plaintext library data or encryption keys.
Gallery mode on iOS/Android browses device photos/videos and runs optional local face/semantic analysis without uploading; desktop does not have this mode.
Device media and already-indexed face/Magic Search work offline; remote originals must first download, and account sharing/backups/maps are separate network-dependent functions.
Photos app supports Android and alternative distribution channels including F-Droid, with local gallery and encrypted backup modes.
iOS app supports gallery/backup, editors and local AI, subject to mobile permission/background constraints.
Native desktop client supports watch folders, local AI and continuous export; it is not the independent Auth client.
Desktop Photos supports local AI/watch/export and macOS device-authentication app lock.
Native Photos desktop release supports Linux, including documented RAW-preview improvements and export/ML workflows.
Web client supports uploads, basic search, metadata and sharing; public album viewers do not need an account. Web ML/face recognition is not available.
Open-source production server can be deployed with configurable endpoints/buckets, Photos web and a separate public Albums application; clients can connect to it.
Quickstart provisions containers; documented minimum is one CPU core and 1 GB RAM. Production configuration/backup is the operator's responsibility.
Mobile gallery mode reads native Camera/Screenshots/other device albums without an import copy; cloud mode is a separate backup workflow.
Selected device folders/albums back up originals without compression, use Wi-Fi by default with a cellular override, resume interrupted uploads and map into Ente albums.
Onboarding new-only mode starts at seven days ago; enabling later uses the current moment. Already queued uploads are not cancelled and manual older uploads still work.

Monitors additions/deletions while the desktop client runs; new files upload and local deletions move cloud membership to Uncategorized instead of permanent removal. Edits to already-uploaded files are not tracked.
Multiple desktop watch folders have independent album-mapping choices and sync concurrently; these are roots feeding one account, not separate catalogues.
Upload/watch chooses one flattened album or separate albums named by leaf folders. Equal leaf names can merge into one album and empty folders are ignored.
Matches media with Takeout JSON dates/location/captions. Extract all archive parts into one parent while preserving album subfolders; reimporting skipped assets does not repair their stored dates.
Same-album duplicates skip; cross-album matches add logical references without re-upload. Mobile uses content hash; web/desktop require matching hash and filename.
Manual mobile/desktop cleanup recognizes content hashes and retains one underlying file with references in each album; independently generated thumbnails can differ without changing identity.
ML Similar images groups visually related but nonidentical photos for mobile review; desktop lacks this dedicated cleanup feature.
Review can override deletion choices. Favorites are never auto-selected; other files favor the largest size, with filename as tie-breaker, not resolution or EXIF completeness.
Mobile Similar images requires reviewing groups and confirming which copies to keep/delete; logical album references help avoid removing every representation of a scene from albums.
Shows reclaimable size and removes backed-up local copies after confirmation, retaining Ente originals; the automated action covers all backed-up items rather than an arbitrary selective subset.
Desktop/CLI export preserves original file bytes and album folders; files in several albums appear in each exported folder, potentially increasing local space.
Desktop continuous export downloads new items while running; CLI repeated/scheduled exports incrementally update a disk or mounted NAS. Local edits do not upload back.
Exports edits into metadata/filename.ext.json with canonical photoTakenTime, description and geoData; originals remain unchanged. Legacy creationTime field is deprecated.
Cloud deletion moves exported files into an export Trash folder; subsequently emptying cloud Trash does not automatically delete those local copies.
Interrupted backup resumes with connectivity and repeated CLI export continues previous work; retained encrypted upload staging can temporarily increase device storage.
Mobile gallery chooses square tiles or original-proportion mosaic; pinch adjusts density and crosses into mosaic without modifying images.
Device gallery presents photos chronologically; cloud metadata date selection uses embedded metadata, Takeout sidecar, filename inference then upload-time fallback.
Local and signed-in mobile modes provide a full-screen photo/video viewer with swiping and pinch zoom.
Gallery-mode comparison explicitly includes pinch-to-zoom and swiping between media; collage framing also uses pinch/drag.

Mobile and desktop play photos/Live Photos, not videos, with 5-second through 10-minute intervals, ordered/shuffled playback and black/blurred backgrounds. Mobile can combine albums; desktop plays one album.
Search focus, range/additive/select-all selection and delete shortcuts are documented; slideshow uses arrows and Space.
Clients view videos, but browser-unsupported codecs may require original-file download instead of streaming.

Optional stream generation creates 720p H.264 at 2 Mbps in encrypted HLS with encrypted playlist, enabling seeking without downloading whole originals. Stream storage is quota-exempt only during beta.

Optional beta streaming generates 720p H.264 at 2 Mbps with an HLS playlist so mobile and web/desktop clients can begin playback and seek without first downloading the complete original. A stream must have been generated; unsupported or failed streams can fall back to original-file playback/download. Streams are encrypted and quota-exempt only during beta.
Signed-in users create albums with covers/descriptions and reuse one original across albums through references; local account-free mode does not provide Ente albums.
FAQ explicitly states albums are flat and cannot be nested, even when uploaded folders are nested.
FAQ explicitly says photos/videos cannot currently be dragged into a custom album order; available Sort by options must be used instead.
Removing the last album membership or watched-folder file retains the asset in Uncategorized. Cleaning removes only entries also present in an album the user owns.

Mobile config adds existing/new owned uploads containing selected named people after local face indexing, including editable collaborative albums; Favorites/Uncategorized are excluded and disabling ML pauses updates.
Favorites are account-backed organization, used by widgets and protected by similar-image auto-selection; unavailable in account-free gallery mode.
Archive removes items from home timeline/memories while retaining search and album visibility; no extra authentication is required.
Hide removes owned media from ordinary timeline/albums/search and requires device authentication for Hidden; a still-local copy may remain visible in On device views.
Web/basic search includes filename alongside date, description and album; no semantic model is required for these fields.
Only fields parsed at import are searchable; raw EXIF can still be displayed separately. Captions/descriptions are searchable and encrypted.
Magic Search documentation combines semantic results with date filters and specific time periods; web supports basic date search.

Opt-in local CLIP matches natural-language objects/scenes/colors/activities and relationships; combine with dates, people, albums or locations. English typically works best; not available in the web client.
Face and semantic indexing runs on mobile/desktop. Signed-in mode indexes backed-up media only, whereas signed-out gallery mode can index permitted local files.
Opt-in analysis detects face regions as the first stage of recognizing people; web does not support this feature.
Automatically groups similar faces after indexing. Mobile mixed-group re-evaluation applies stricter settings for difficult cases such as babies.
Face groups find all photos containing the same people across albums; identity naming and corrective operations remain local and encrypted on sync.
Mobile/desktop assign names to groups and make them searchable; selecting an existing named identity merges groups.
Mobile supports de-merge, Not this person, ignored-group restore and cover selection; desktop has naming/merge-history undo/ignore but not individual incorrect-face editing or cover selection.
Named identities can be searched across albums using the local face index; no unencrypted face data or search queries need reach the service.

Index on desktop, sync encrypted results to mobile and disable mobile local indexing to reduce memory load. Concurrent clients avoid duplicate indexing but documentation says this does not accelerate the overall job.

Mobile Memory Lane requires at least two years with four eligible person photos per year; known ages below three, hidden items and ignored faces are excluded. Timelines include age/year captions and public-link presentation.
Mobile memories/widgets show On This Day, Past Years and smart curated moments; notifications can exclude a person by hiding them from memories.
Mobile long-press recognizes/copies text in photos/Live Photos using on-device OCR. Android downloads models on first use; supported languages vary, and Trash/guest views and video are excluded.
OCR guide explicitly states Detect Text builds no searchable library index; occasional CLIP matches to prominent text are not dedicated OCR search.
Mobile detects multiple QR codes on-device and offers open/copy/share plus supported UPI payment actions; scanning alone does not upload QR contents.
Reads capture time/camera/GPS for import and exposes View all EXIF on mobile/web/desktop; not every raw field is searchable.
Imports embedded IPTC alongside other standards, including date information; original bytes remain preserved.
Reads embedded XMP for metadata/date extraction without implying arbitrary XMP sidecar editing.
Edit searchable descriptions in the info panel on mobile/web/desktop; values sync encrypted and are separate from originals.
Desktop bulk Edit/Fix time can use original/digitized/metadata EXIF dates, parsed filename or custom time. Corrections sync but never rewrite original EXIF.
Desktop supports bulk creation-time changes; mobile/web/desktop allow location edits on multi-selection.
Add or drag map coordinates for photos lacking/wrong locations. Values belong to Ente's separate metadata and do not strip/replace GPS inside the original or phone-library copy.
Filename edits in the info panel are stored separately and synced; original filename is preserved.
View all GPS-tagged media or one album on the map across clients; location search is local and coordinates encrypted. Desktop changelog explicitly references OpenStreetMap tile loading.
Create labels such as Home/Office by choosing a center and radius; the app groups matching photos locally, with encrypted location labels.
Search location tags and geographic areas locally; Magic Search can be narrowed to a tagged place.
Mobile editor crops and straightens arbitrary tilts; saved result is a separate copy.
JPEG-only rotation/flip edits avoid re-encoding; other edits may re-encode. Originals remain untouched.
Mobile editor offers filters, brightness/contrast/saturation/exposure/hue/temperature/tint/fade. Recent changelog explicitly removes Sharpness and Luminance.
Mobile editor draws and layers text/stickers with font/color/background/alignment controls and per-object edit/duplicate/delete; text becomes image pixels rather than searchable caption metadata.
Choose layouts, swap tiles by long-press/tap, pinch/drag framing and save to device gallery; no videos or web/desktop creation.
Mobile editor sets start/end with preview and a one-second minimum; this documents trimming only, not joining. Each export is a finalized new file, not a saved edit recipe.
Mobile crops freely or to 1:1, 9:16, 16:9, 3:4 or 4:3 and rotates in 90-degree steps, accounting for original orientation.
Native AVFoundation/Media3 export produces H.264 MP4, with FFmpeg H.264/AAC fallback; iOS simple trims can use passthrough. New copy preserves date/location/album membership where available.
Native export uses hardware acceleration where supported; software FFmpeg fallback runs when native export fails.
Photo/video edits leave original files unchanged and save new finalized copies. Edited dimensions/format or secondary metadata can change; not a reversible development-history stack.

Original downloads retain embedded metadata verbatim; Ente/Takeout corrections travel as JSON sidecars, not rewritten EXIF. Edited copies preserve selected camera/date/location fields but not necessarily all metadata.
Live Photos participate in album slideshows and photo OCR; differing video-frame thumbnail extraction does not affect exact duplicate identity.
Backup FAQ explicitly calls RAW support limited; desktop v1.7.30 improves RAF/ORF/PEF/NRW/SRW previews on Linux/Windows. Universal camera compatibility is not claimed.
Accepts image/* and video/* originals up to 10 GB, without upload compression; backup eligibility does not guarantee every client can thumbnail/play the format.
FAQ explicitly says JPEG XL may upload while lacking a thumbnail/preview; reliable viewing across clients is not established.
Desktop v1.7.30 preserves HDR gain maps in Ultra HDR JPEG thumbnails generated on Linux/Windows; this is narrower than a universal HDR rendering guarantee.
Share an album or selected items without requiring recipients' accounts. Quick links create a backing album, can become ordinary albums and can be revoked without deleting photos.
Optional link password gates server access to encrypted content but does not re-encrypt it or change the embedded link key.
Choose preset/custom expiry and later extend/change it; expired or removed links stop granting access.
Limits unique IP+User-Agent combinations, not actual physical devices; already admitted combinations retain access after the cap is reached. Free plans have a ten-device cap.
Paid plans can create public links without the free tier's ten-device limit.
Public viewers support proportional masonry, date groups or map/timeline Trip layout; Trip currently redirects custom-domain links to albums.ente.com.
Owners can hide download buttons, but recipients can still copy via browser/tools/screenshots and metadata is not stripped. This is not DRM or guaranteed original-file protection.
Public links can use an owner-controlled domain; Trip and app-reopen/join flows have documented custom-domain limitations.
Each user has their own account/storage; invited collaborators share selected albums. Multiple accounts are not counted as selectable libraries.
Email-invited participants add photos/videos. Each uploader pays their own quota, and their contributions leave the shared album if they leave while remaining in their account.

Viewer views/downloads/comments, collaborator adds/removes own uploads, admin manages members/removes membership and suggests deletion; only owner manages links/deletes album and nobody permanently deletes others' assets.
Anyone with the enabled link can view/add through a browser; collected files count to the owner's quota and guests cannot delete uploads. Current guide says contributor attribution is unavailable.

Shared albums/public links support comments, quoted replies, likes and anonymous display names. Same photo has separate threads per album; owners/admins moderate. Comments cap at 500 characters and do not apply to unshared private albums.

Mobile, web and desktop support commenting, quoted replies and likes on shared photos/videos; public-link visitors can participate anonymously when enabled. Owners/admins moderate comments, each album keeps a separate thread for the same photo, and comments are limited to 500 characters. Unshared private albums do not support these interactions; comment and like data remain end-to-end encrypted.
Mobile Feed aggregates likes/comments/replies from shared albums; it is social history, not an operation-recovery journal.
On mobile, album owners/admins remove others' selected photos from the album and send a deletion suggestion; actual photo owners accept/delete or reject/keep in their queue.
Paid subscriber plus five members share one plan while content stays private by default; admin can set individual storage limits.
Within family sharing, select owned albums in bulk and optionally share newly created albums automatically; shared capacity alone never grants content access.
Deleted Ente assets remain recoverable for 30 days and count toward quota until purged. Bulk restore targets a chosen album, not each previous membership; permanent deletion is unrecoverable.
On Android 11+, deleting local gallery items through Ente uses Android system trash and exposes a Device recovery tab even for unbacked media; system retention is distinct from Ente's 30 days.
Cloud deletion, empty Trash and device-space cleanup require confirmation; duplicate cleanup reviews results and reclaimable-space information first.

Native-device deletion does not delete backup, and cloud deletion does not silently erase the device original. Ente remembers uploaded files to avoid automatically re-uploading deliberately deleted cloud copies.
Previously accepted Ente trusted contacts can request recovery with a 7/14/30-day owner veto period, then change account password; configured from Photos mobile and applicable to photo succession.
Mobile/desktop offer PIN/password locks, configurable immediate-to-30-minute background autolock and device authentication; desktop device lock is macOS-only.
Mobile Hide content obscures app-switcher views and disables screenshots on Android; no claim of general screen-recording prevention is made.
Mobile guest view restricts browsing to one item/selection/album, hides edit/share/delete/info/navigation and requires configured device authentication to exit.

Shared account supports TOTP or WebAuthn passkeys as a second factor; adding passkeys replaces configured TOTP, rather than making Photos passwordless. This does not inventory Ente Auth's authenticator features.
A 24-word key recovers access after password loss; absent password, signed-in recovery route/key or preconfigured trusted contact, support cannot decrypt Photos data.
CLI exports selected albums or individual files and supports scheduled local/NAS backups; restarting export resumes. It is not a two-way filesystem sync tool.
Advanced FAQ explicitly says there is no public third-party API and directs automation users to CLI; open server source is not equivalent to a supported public API.
Cast sends an album slideshow to Chromecast or any Internet-connected screen using PIN pairing; multiple sessions can be managed. It does not mirror the photo currently scrolled on the phone.
iOS/Android widgets show configured albums, memories or ML-selected people, usually refresh about every 15 minutes and require account features for album/people widgets.
Mobile notifications cover shared additions, memories and tagged-person birthdays. Categories are configurable; birthday reminders occur on the day, not earlier.

Mobile rituals link an owned album to weekdays/reminders and track capture-date-based scheduled-day streaks. Ritual camera supports up to 20 photos/session, not video; ritual settings stay local although the album syncs.
Hosted specification describes two hot encrypted copies in Amsterdam/Frankfurt and one cold copy in Paris across Backblaze/Wasabi/Scaleway; self-hosters must design their own redundancy.
Hosted Wasabi replica uses compliance hold plus a 21-day release buffer; cleanup occurs later after customer permanent deletion. This does not promise user restoration after Trash expires.

Specification describes HA Postgres, six-hour snapshots, daily portable dumps, encrypted locked cross-provider copies and daily restore testing with alerts. These are service operational claims, not tested here.
Reliability document describes manually tested secondary-storage/database recovery and lists fully automatic failover as future work; primary DB active/passive failover is already distinct.
README describes Photos as a paid service with a 10 GB free allocation; additional hosted capacity requires a subscription, separate from self-hosting.

Release notes identify translated UI labels maintained through Weblate; user-selected language changes translated event titles, Things labels and localized numeric formatting. English-only Things search vocabulary is a separate limitation.
Own-server library with browser frontend and local ML; README recommends at least 4 GB RAM and preferably 8 GB+ for analysis.
Single-container install or separated backend/frontend/proxy Compose; Kubernetes and Unraid are recorded separately rather than inferred from generic Docker compatibility.
README explicitly provides Kustomize manifests in deploy/k8s; 1.6.0 release notes confirm those manifests were updated to the 1.6.0 image version.
README lists Unraid as an installation choice and links its dedicated installation guide. This records the documented deployment surface without asserting additional NAS integrations.
One folder with librephotos.exe, no Docker/Python installation required; SQLite and protected-media data are local to the Windows application.
Light/dark desktop/mobile layouts, phone bottom sheets and configurable pinned sidebar plus recent albums in 1.6.0.
Mobile guide points users needing an installable app to UhuruPhotos; 1.6.0 restores compatibility for its released builds. Official Expo client is separate and unreleased.

Implemented official Expo Android app runs through Expo Go or a development build, but has no Google Play, F-Droid or GitHub APK release. It is distinct from the released third-party UhuruPhotos integration; production distribution is not counted as present.

Official mobile guide explicitly supports running the implemented iPhone app from source through Expo Go or a development build, but says there is no App Store or TestFlight release. This is an upcoming/source-preview surface, not currently packaged native iOS availability.
Scans existing image/video/RAW/XMP files without reorganizing them by default; unrelated sidecars/non-media are skipped.
Main scan folder, additional admin-added folders and separate upload folder form one library; unreadable/unplugged roots are skipped without marking their photos missing.
Browse indexed directories/subdirectories with recursive counts and newest-photo covers; empty/unindexed/hidden directories are not listed.
Rereads new/changed files and sidecars and retries prior metadata failures; cancelled/partial/failed scans do not replace the last complete-library baseline.
Admin chooses hourly, daily or custom weekdays/time, off by default. Overlapping queued/running scans are skipped and server timezone is shown.
Official guide provides an inotifywait/curl/jq watcher feeding scan-files API, batching after 30 seconds; not an always-enabled native filesystem watcher.
API accepts up to 1000 changed paths and separately 1000 removed paths; validates library scope and detects move-out/move-in without losing personal edits.
Leave out subfolders recursively, with optional trashing of already-indexed out-of-scope photos. Exclusion alone never deletes disk files; hidden/skip-pattern folders also stay out.
Drop multiple photos/videos anywhere, append to active queue and upload directly into own unlocked albums; account scan directory and admin upload enablement are prerequisites.
Uploads one file at a time in 1 MB chunks; cancel stops after current chunk, retries failed/cancelled files while tab remains open and removes old partial uploads daily.
Checks MD5 plus user ID before upload; existing photos can still be added to the target album without retransmitting bytes.
Scans adjacent JSON for capture UTC time, GPS/altitude and description only as lower-priority fallback; handles supplemental/truncated/duplicate/edited filenames without rewriting originals.

Select remote folder, copy into nextcloud_media/user, reuse unchanged files and refresh changed media/XMP. Deleted remote files are marked missing, not silently deleted locally; no write-back to Nextcloud.

Move within library with all variants/XMP, retaining albums/faces/ratings/shares. Skip missing, shared-file and Nextcloud-copy cases; selections over 100 use a background job. Copy is not established by this workflow.
Choose year, year/month or year/month/day destinations with preview counts; undated photos remain until given dates.
Presets/custom year/month/day/hour/minute/second/original-name tokens rename photos and companions, preview changes and suffix collisions; over 100 photos runs in background.
Move chooses rename-keep-both or skip; rename adds numbered suffixes. Destination files are never silently overwritten.
If one file of a photo cannot move, previously moved companion files are put back; rename also retains old names on failure. Docs establish per-photo rollback, not a durable crash-recovery journal.
Single-photo page selects original variant; multi-photo ZIP includes all file variants and XMP sidecars with collision-safe paired names, optionally adding all stack photos.
Capture-date grouped timeline with newest/oldest account-saved order, undated bucket and simple or photo-density scrubber; events always chronological.
Views cover favourites, recent latest-import day, hidden/archive, photos/videos, screenshots/documents and missing-date/location/album cases; filter-aware select-all targets only displayed scope.
1.6.0 uses cursor pages for /api/days rather than offset/page-number queries, retaining scroll geometry while rows load. Reported speedups are not independently measured.
Black-stage lightbox, thumbnail strip, fullscreen toggle and deep-link photo address; browser Back closes viewer and restores grid position.
Signed-in authorized viewers fetch original when zooming; RAW/HEIC/TIFF/JXL/rotated images may remain preview-only with original-download link. Public visitors retain display-size previews.
Intervals 3/5/10/15/30 seconds with keyboard control; public album ?slideshow=1 starts automatically, stops at last photo and respects reduced-motion preference.
Ctrl/Cmd+K, Ctrl/Cmd+P or / opens palette for people/places/albums/search/actions; viewer keys handle rating, text selection, archive, slideshow, navigation and video seek.
1.6.0 redesign covers pages, viewer, dialogs and sidebar; map display darkening is performed in-browser without a second tile source.
WebGL drag/swipe/pinch viewer uses GPano equirectangular metadata or exact 2:1 images at least 6000 px wide; cylindrical panoramas and 360 videos are not sphere-rendered.
Checks browser codec support, plays original when possible and falls back on decode failure. Keyboard seeks 10 seconds/one minute except during live conversion.
For signed-in viewers unsupported videos convert while playing to H.264 capped at 720 lines and are cached; public unauthenticated visitors do not receive this conversion.
HDR phone video is tone-mapped during thumbnail/conversion paths; HDR badges and probe/rebuild job repair older previews.
User controls newest/oldest date order across lists; missing dates remain last. Per-album date sort refers to oldest member capture time, not album creation.
Text search includes indexed file paths alongside captions, people, location, cameras, lenses, types and ISO-format date fragments.
Maker/model/lens plus inclusive min/max ISO, aperture, focal length and 35-mm equivalent; values absent from a photo cannot match their filter.
Matches user tags and XMP/IPTC keywords, including sidecars. Display-translated AI Things remain searchable by English word in current guide.
Every word must appear somewhere in indexed text; commas split words and quotes preserve phrases. Case/diacritics are folded except OCR; semantic augmentation can return nonliteral matches.
Before/after dates plus current-year/last-year/last-12-month shortcuts combine with other filters.
Person-name search and repeat person filters require all chosen people in a photo; suggestions rank matches by face count.
Filter rating 1–5 threshold or favourites-only according to chosen rating UI.
Find by place name, custom private place or whether GPS exists; Places map limits visible place albums to current viewport.
Photos/video/screenshots/documents plus main-file extension and Has a RAW file, including RAW companions.
Active filters live in page address, appear as removable chips and preserve words/media when cleared; this is URL persistence rather than a saved-query catalogue.
Disabled by default; choose top 10/50/100 semantic matches above threshold, merged with ordinary text results. Requires completed embeddings/index, persisted under protected_media/similarity.
Lightbox shows semantically similar photos from OpenCLIP embeddings, distinct from pHash duplicate detection.
OCR text joins normal text search; PostgreSQL matches words whereas SQLite permits substring matches.

ExifTool reads dates/UTC offsets/GPS/altitude/orientation, camera/lens/serial, exposure, rights, video duration/codec and dimensions; on-demand raw-metadata dialog filters groups/tags/values and copies JSON.
Reads Keywords, Caption-Abstract, ObjectName, By-line and CopyrightNotice with documented XMP/EXIF precedence.
Reads basename.xmp and filename.ext.xmp, uppercase variants and RAW/video companion sidecars with field-specific precedence; hierarchy keywords flatten to last level.
Save to media file writes supported ratings/dates/manual captions/GPS/keywords/rights and optional face regions via ExifTool; support varies by format and image bytes are not re-encoded.
Updates highest-priority existing main-file sidecar or creates filename.ext.xmp, preserving unrelated tags. RAW companion sidecars are read but writes target the main photo's sidecar.
Bulk UI edits use background write-back when enabled; Write now exports pre-existing catalogue edits in 200-photo batches with per-file errors and cancellation.
Shift a selection by days/hours/minutes/seconds preserving intervals, or assign one timestamp. Manual dates survive rescans; Remove timestamp returns control to date rules.
Ordered rules choose XMP/EXIF/video/GPS/Takeout/name times, use recorded or GPS/default timezone and can be reapplied without rewriting originals or overriding manually set dates.
Map click/drag, address search, pasted coordinates, explicit browser location or nearby-in-time photos; bulk defaults to filling missing GPS, with replace-all choice and optional write-back.
Comma-separated autocomplete, bulk additive tagging, single-photo replacement/removal and user-private tag albums; rename/merge/delete can update keywords with write-back enabled.
Choose stars or favourite toggle; keyboard 0–5 and bulk selection ratings map to imported/exported XMP rating, with configurable favourite threshold.
Favourites derive from rating threshold; removing a favourite sets rating to zero and therefore clears any existing star rating.
User captions are editable and searchable; generated suggestions are separate and do not overwrite a manual caption during bulk generation.

Reads/displays creator/copyright and fixed Creative Commons/all-rights/public-domain licence choices, with supported write-back. Licence-bearing public photos expose relevant rights regardless of other detail switches.
Imports XMP RegionInfo faces/names and merges overlapping detections; optional face-write switch plus metadata-write mode exports normalized regions/names with rotation handling.
ZIP export includes existing and newly written XMP beside originals/RAW companions, adjusting names together for collisions; privacy-constrained shared downloads intentionally strip metadata instead.
Thumbnails omit EXIF/XMP but retain colour profiles; restricted sharing serves full-size JPEG or video stream copies without recorded metadata. Old-thumbnail cleanup is available.

Rotate stills in 90-degree steps and regenerate thumbnails; default originals unchanged. Optional sidecar orientation works across formats; original EXIF orientation writes limited to JPEG/PNG/TIFF/WebP.
Supports RAW indexing/preview, including upload formats browsers mislabel; paired RAWs can be downloaded even when browser zoom remains on preview.
Upload/index/preview HEIC and HEIF; HEIC/AVIF display orientation follows container rotation/mirroring rather than blindly trusting EXIF.
Explicit upload support and supported ExifTool metadata-write format; browser presentation uses derived previews where required.
README/upload/manual list JXL indexing and uploads; viewer may retain a derived preview and offer original download.
Viewer always uses the animated GIF original rather than enlarging a static display preview.
Same-folder/base-name files represent one photo, no toggle; main-file preference JPEG then video then RAW. Repair job merges orphan RAW photos but not already separate Live Photo videos.
Scan groups same-capture still and clip as variants of one photo, with all variants in ZIP downloads.
Extracts embedded JPEG video into protected_media/embedded_media while preserving its embedded copy in original; enabled by default through feature toggle.
Move, rename and ZIP keep RAW/Live variants and both XMP naming conventions paired; extracted motion-video derivatives remain in app storage.
Create empty or selected-photo albums, upload into them, choose covers and remove membership without deleting originals.
Private labels such as Travel/Family group an album into several collections; deleting a collection preserves albums/photos. Not a nested filesystem hierarchy.
Manual generation chains captures less than 36 hours apart with minimum two photos; people/place affect title, not grouping. Regeneration preserves chosen covers and localized web titles.
Per-person face covers, name merge/delete, private many-to-many people groups and birth date with age-at-capture display; birthdate also constrains recognition suggestions.
GPS/geocoded location generates place collections; private circular places can override local grouping while keeping provider names.
Object/scene classifications form Things albums separate from user tags; caption hashtags remain visible independent of selected tagging model.
API-enforced lock blocks adding/removing photos including uploads, but not editing/deleting underlying photos, renaming/sharing album or deleting album.

EXIF burst/sequence and explicit filename patterns group same-camera frames; default two-second temporal continuity with subsecond times and sequence restarts. Optional proximity/pHash rules are disabled by default.
Group separate captures, merge stacks, pick cover and unstack/break apart while retaining photos; timeline shows cover only and lightbox opens members.
Detailed guide explicitly says Bracket is a reserved type not currently created; no bracket detection exists and Create stack always makes Manual, despite broader README wording.
Detects exact-copy candidates by MD5 file hash, distinct from visual hashes. No separate byte-comparison verification is documented.
64-bit DCT pHash/Hamming distance from large thumbnails; strict/normal/loose sensitivity and two-pass BK-tree batches, default 10,000, including cross-batch comparisons.
Thumbnails and group type/status/savings plus per-photo resolution,size,camera,date,path in review modal.
Highest-resolution photo is preselected but user can choose another; resolution moves other photos to application trash and can be reverted/restored for resolved groups.
Not duplicates preserves all photos, unlinks them and marks group dismissed; this action cannot be reverted through UI and dismissal list currently returns no groups despite counts.

Filter pending/resolved/type, delete group records individually/in bulk or clear pending groups before detection. Looser reruns exclude photos already in visual groups, so groups must be cleared to reconsider them.
InsightFace, OpenCLIP and optional caption/OCR models execute locally; models download on demand or can be prepositioned for offline use.
README documents optional NVIDIA acceleration in separated Docker Compose deployment; no GPU benchmark or universal model acceleration is asserted.
Current model produces semantic embedding and tags in one pass; 1.6 caps five Things with class-specific thresholds. Manual retag refresh does not overwrite personal tags/captions.
Admin custom_tags.txt adds words or word=description with multiple prompt descriptions separated by |; at most two custom/five total labels, no model retraining, and old photos need retagging.

Per-photo suggestion or manually initiated whole-library background generation, preserving manual captions. Optional recognized names/place context defaults on; no automatic whole-library caption job after scan.

Admin selects PP-OCRv6 Tiny/Small/Medium and confirms plaintext privacy warning. Extract missing or all text; current versions queue after scan/upload, with three-failure suppression and retry-all override.
Own-photo viewer T action overlays recognized text for mouse selection/copy; requires OCR results.

Screenshots are detected on scan; document inference combines OCR and content labels, so OCR is needed for automatic documents. Manual/bulk category corrections persist across rescans and support undo.
SCRFD finds boxes, merges overlapping imported MWG regions and offers a minimum relative face-size setting; imported regions are retained regardless.
512-dimensional ArcFace embeddings with selectable speed/memory model packs and learned classification against manually named people; confidence shown separately from clusters.
Stable clustering has auto size thresholds, min-samples and merge epsilon; labels split outputs by known person. Upload-triggered training waits for sufficient new faces and user inactivity.
