Dashboard/lightbox naming with recent-person shortcuts; clearly matching unnamed faces in bursts/duplicate groups can be labelled together, respecting prior rejections.

Not-person decisions persist across training and person merge; false detections are soft-deleted/excluded from training and can be restored. Merge people preserves target cover but cannot itself be undone.
Draw a box to request enlarged-area detection/encoding or retain manual box if no match/service unavailable; prevents overlapping duplicate regions and requires usable thumbnail.
Up to eight frames from 5%–95%, at most one/second, consolidate matching identities using largest face. Faces retain timestamp for seek-to-person; clips under two seconds use first frame only.
MapLibre displays actual photo coordinates, viewport-filtered place tiles and click-to-open previews; online PhotoPrism/OSM basemaps or None.
Photos within about a metre combine at one point; zoomed-out clusters count photos once, not every administrative place name.
New-install ExifTool/GeoNames geocoder finds nearest town ≥2000 population within 50 km plus district/region/country; no street/POI and borders can choose a town across a country line.
Nominatim or keyed Mapbox/MapTiler/OpenCage/TomTom; Nominatim rate limit shared across workers around one request/sec. Language settings/provider switch only affect new lookups unless rerun.

Define up to 100 places of 25 m–2 km radius with live photo counts; smaller overlapping circle wins. Names dynamically group photos/search and can title events, but never leave owner via sharing/write-back.
Multiple accounts retain their own photos/faces/ratings/albums; all sharing preserves source ownership. This is not a shared co-owned editable catalogue.
Can view versus Can add photos; contributors remove only their own contributions, owner controls cover/lock/sharing. Contributions leave album when contributor exits or loses contribution rights.
Links contributors' media without copy/move; recipient details require intersection of owner and contributor switches. Contributor photos are never included on owner's album public link.
Members can post plain-text comments up to 1000 chars/like photos, with own edit/delete and owner moderation; per-user 30/minute limit and membership/removal lifecycle.
Share ongoing own photos with another account and independently opt into location/people/camera/captions/originals; recipient may mix them into timeline but cannot edit or add to own albums.

Only manually labelled person photos count; existing labels initially approve, later labels await review. Inferred/unknown faces do not auto-share; metadata switches start off and originals are withheld.
Album custom/random slugs, replace/revoke single-photo random slugs and distinct Make public raw-image exposure; revoking burns slug instead of reviving old links later.
Public album expiry supports exact date/time or 7/30/90-day presets and Never. Expiry is explicitly unavailable for single-photo links.
Guide explicitly says password protection is not available for photo shares yet; album password support is not established either.

Public date/location/camera/caption/face-name switches default off. Original public delivery requires all five; otherwise metadata-free copies are served. Whole-library originals independently override embedded privacy expectations.

Admin enables members-only/everyone and each user independently opts in. Gallery provides timeline/towns/named people/photographers, not private links or contributor photos; search engines default discouraged.
README explicitly supports OpenID Connect SSO; LDAP compatibility is not inferred as native directory integration.
Swagger/ReDoc plus documented metadata/search/targeted-scan/processing-status/upload/retention endpoints; Basic/JWT authentication described for scripts.
Scan selected/all/Nextcloud roots, rebuild index, write metadata with dry-run, rehash, strip derived metadata, back up SQLite and repair upgrade data.
Trash marks photos deleted while retaining them; restore reverses it. Permanent/empty-trash deletes originals and derivatives. Auto-delete defaults 0/off and shows per-photo countdown when enabled.
Confirm permanent deletion, retention reductions and key destructive actions; unsaved metadata prompts on viewer navigation, page leave and tab close.
Notifications undo favourites/hide/archive/public changes and face operations; timestamps can revert previous value, resolved duplicates restore trashed copies. Not a crash-recovery file journal.
Scans only read originals and write-back is Off by default; sidecar mode preserves media bytes. Read-only mounted files cannot be permanently deleted, but catalogue edits still work.
Missing-file detection checks whole result before changes, refuses apparently unmounted roots or configured excessive missing count and avoids flagging photos after unreadable-subfolder scans.

Check file contents rereads every byte to detect replacements retaining old mtime, then reimports/reindexes changes with appropriate personal-data preservation. It is not documented as bit-rot recovery or copy verification.
backup_database keeps newest three by default, configurable, and can guard pending migrations. PostgreSQL needs separate pg_dump; originals/models/secret require their own backup.

Progress card covers thumbnails/Things/search/places/faces/OCR/captions, run-missing-stage actions and per-item errors; ordinary user jobs serialize globally while upload processing can run alongside.
Jobs stop at checkpoints and clear queued steps; move/rename preserve completed changes. Model/ZIP downloads finish and clustering finishes current rebuild; upload-import jobs cannot cancel.

After restart previously taken queue work reruns around ten minutes later; failed/cancelled scans do not advance baseline and later jobs fill missing analysis. Stuck checks target lack of progress, not simply duration.
Scan prioritizes thumbnails; upload progress distinguishes sent/processing/ready and timeline fills without reload while analysis continues.
Tiny/grid/large/face derivatives, extracted motion clips and persistent similarity/model files; bulk ZIPs auto-expire around one day.

Rescan up to 1000 chosen photos, re-detect selected/folder faces, retry particular stages, rebuild embeddings/geocoding and repair RAW variants/old video previews without indiscriminately clearing manual data.
Admin health/start/stop for ML services, job details, log refresh/download and JSON CPU/RAM/GPU/storage/per-user report; job-log removal is distinct from cancellation.

1.6.0 retains at most 30 reports for 30 days locally, deduplicating repeats; admin may opt into maintainers or own Sentry/GlitchTip. Reports rebuilt from allowlisted fields remove paths/names/URLs/identifiers.
Preload model files, use offline ExifTool, hide online maps and disable release checks. OpenCLIP remains required; disabling caption/face features avoids their model downloads.
Local ML and original-folder indexing do not require third-party photo upload; optional online maps, reports and Nextcloud have separate disclosures.

Archive removes photos from the main timeline and Memories while retaining them in albums, search, people, places, folders and other filtered views; Unarchive returns them. Unlike Hide, archive does not remove photos from all ordinary views. Neither mode changes original files.

Hide removes photos from ordinary timeline, album, people, place, search and folder views; they remain available in Hidden until unhidden. Hiding takes precedence when a photo is also archived. This is visibility control, not encryption, and the guide establishes no separate authentication guarantee for the Hidden section; original files are unchanged.
Photo/day/person/face/event/place counts with inferred/labelled/unknown breakdown, plus data-volume usage bar that includes other content on that disk.
Monthly photo chart and chronological location-stay duration bar; timeline density scrubber also visualizes busy months/years.
Country/region/town tree with horizontal/vertical/radial layouts, counts, collapse, pan and zoom.
Top 100 terms sized by frequency, clickable to search their photos.
Unweighted edges connect people appearing together in at least one photo, with draggable nodes/zoom; not an inferred social relationship beyond co-occurrence.
Projected embeddings coloured by identity, hover thumbnails, click-to-photo and per-person highlights assist correction.
1.6.0 shows per-user busiest day/month and most photographed people/places from Dec 20–Jan 6, computed on own server and admin-disableable.

Unreleased app implements album-selected photo/video backup, Wi-Fi/charging conditions, content skip and processing badges. OS background limits apply; not advertised as a released official backup client.

Unreleased mobile app mirrors metadata/grid thumbnails and queues favourite/hide/trash/rating/caption/album edits; full originals still need network unless already on device, and resync rebuilds disposable mirror.
Unreleased mobile app schedules on-this-day notifications locally two weeks ahead without push service; they stop if not reopened/synced within two weeks.
Implemented Android development-build share target accepts images from other apps, not Expo Go; iOS share extension explicitly still being finalized.

General Interface preferences populate a language selector from supported locales, fall back to English for an unknown preference and require restart after changing language. French translations explicitly cover menus, duplicate-review labels and deletion dialogs; release 4.3.1 also updates Italian translations.
Release supplies installers and portable ZIPs; 4.3.1 packages require Windows 7 or later.
ZIP distribution is offered alongside the Windows installer.
4.3.1 notes Intel/M1 compatibility and signing without a paid developer subscription.
Debian/RPM binaries, Arch packaging and Ubuntu PPA are documented; binary Python compatibility is release-specific.
Add existing folders to the scan list; no managed photo import is required.
Add multiple recent/new folders or drag directories into the selection list before a single scan.
Standard Contents groups by file size, drops unique-size files and compares MD5 digests. This is hash-based equality, not documented full byte-for-byte verification.
Normalize case/punctuation and compare shared words against filter hardness; optional character-weighting and approximate-word matching increase flexibility, time and false positives.
Dash-separated fields are compared individually; an order-independent mode can match artist/title reversed between files, with each field used once.
Music mode compares chosen tags such as artist/title as separate fields and displays audio metadata columns. This is not a claim of acoustic fingerprinting.

Picture Contents averages RGB values over a 15×15 grid and compares corresponding cells against a configurable threshold; 100 applies an additional exact-picture constraint, while 99 permits small differences.
Preferences can permit differing dimensions and rotations in the same picture duplicate group and allow mixed file extensions.
A separate scan treats matching DateTimeOriginal tags as duplicate candidates; modified images retaining the timestamp can be false positives.
Folder Contents compares contained file contents recursively and returns the largest matching folders instead of redundantly listing their matching subfolders.
Time-consuming 15×15 picture-analysis results are cached in a database. The release also refers to a standard-content hashing cache bug fix.
Picture matching is documented as utilizing multiple cores, while still requiring quadratic pair comparisons; no benchmark was performed.
Reference-state folders cannot contribute deletable duplicates. States inherit to subfolders unless overridden, and protected references cannot be demoted.
Exclude roots or individual subfolders from scanning with inherited per-folder state.
Defaults to a protected reference or largest file; manually promote a duplicate or apply ordered size/folder/filename and other prioritization criteria with tie-breakers.
Group references cannot be marked, ensuring at least one group member remains; reference-folder members are additionally protected.
Add Selected to Ignore List suppresses that duplicate/reference pair in future scans, not the file globally; the same file may match a different reference. Ignore list can be cleared.
Remove selected/marked candidates from results or leave them unmarked; removing result rows does not touch their files.

Details panel compares selected file and reference metadata; numeric Delta Values show relative differences and differing text is highlighted. This evidence establishes metadata comparison, not a thumbnail comparison claim.
Hide reference rows to sort all duplicate files independently by columns, combine with relative values, and mark batches such as extension or bitrate differences.
Case-insensitive filter searches complete paths using simple text plus wildcard or regular expressions. Nonmatching members remain visible but cannot be marked through the filtered view.
Shift/Control/Command selection and Space toggle selected duplicate marks; marked and selected states remain distinct.
Exports current result columns into an XHTML report and opens it in the browser.
Send Marked to Trash uses the OS trash; a separate direct-delete option bypasses it for cases such as incompatible NAS deletion.
Scanning first produces reviewable groups; deletion presents options. Groups discard ambiguous non-transitive matches rather than overlapping candidates that might delete distinct files.
Deletion options can link removed paths to reference files; manual documents macOS/Linux support and Windows version/admin-privilege caveats.
Alternative link replacement uses symlinks, with the explicit caveat that moving/deleting their reference target breaks them.
macOS/Linux preference excludes duplicate candidates already referring to the same inode.
Destination layout can be flat or recreate relative/absolute source paths; source folders can be removed after becoming empty.
Copy/move naming conflicts prepend a number instead of silently overwriting the destination filename.
Action menu prompts for a new filename; a batch naming-template system is not established by this action.
Configure a command with duplicate and reference path placeholders; results can also open in the default application or reveal their containing directory.
README explicitly provides official executable Windows builds from GitHub Releases; these are desktop applications, not a Docker-host or browser-only compatibility claim.
README explicitly lists macOS desktop builds for both Intel and Apple Silicon, distributed through official GitHub Releases.
README explicitly lists executable Linux desktop releases; it warns that package-manager distributions are unofficial rather than claiming official support for every package source.
README explicitly offers self-contained portable Windows and Linux releases intended to be easier to move between locations; macOS portable packaging is not claimed.

Roadmap marks interface translations and application language settings implemented; v9.6.4 specifically updates Dutch, French and Hungarian translations. This does not imply the separately planned multilingual tag-name feature.
Roadmap explicitly marks filename result sorting completed in v9.5.2; file creation/modification/capture-date sorting remains unchecked and is not included in this claim.
Results can be ordered by when the file entry was added to the library, explicitly distinct from file creation, modification or photo capture time.
Random/Shuffle Sort is explicitly checked as implemented in the current search-result sorting roadmap.
Creates a layer over a chosen directory and its descendants without moving, copying or changing media files.
Open/Create selects a library root; each library has its own tags, fields, colors and database, not a global tag universe.
Relative entry paths allow moving the whole content/data folder together, including external drives or differently mounted NAS paths.

Manual Refresh Directories and configurable scan-on-open update the catalogue. README mentions a 10,000-file threshold, while newer manual describes a user toggle; exact threshold behavior is not independently resolved.
.ts_ignore supports directory-relative patterns, *, ?, **, ranges, comments and negation. Applies when adding new files, not retroactively; cannot re-include children of an excluded parent.
Tool finds missing entries, searches/relinks or removes only catalogue records after confirmation. README says matching uses filenames, ignores ambiguous matches and cannot relink renamed files.
Tags have nonunique unrestricted names, shorthand, aliases, colors and relationships rather than just flat text labels.
Tags inherit from multiple parents transitively; searching a parent finds entries assigned descendants without redundantly adding every ancestor to each file.
Aliases/shorthand are searchable; marked parent tags add their name or shorthand in display parentheses to distinguish same-named tags without changing base identity.
Category tags group inheriting tags in inspector, including multiple categories. Per-tag exclusions control category display; v9.6.4 release confirms the feature.
Built-in and user-defined namespaced palettes set primary/secondary text/border colors on tags; not an independently established media color-label rating system.
Built-in Favorite and Archived tags inherit Meta Tags; their category/parent behavior can be customized.
Is Hidden excludes tagged entries from default searches; Archived carries it by default and a checkbox includes hidden entries.

Create/edit/delete custom templates for text or datetime fields. Template information is copied into an entry; editing the entry does not mutate the template. Newer manual/roadmap supersede README's fixed-name claim.
Single-line/multiline text stores titles, notes or comments; datetime values follow application date format. Values are in the catalogue, not written to media.
Add Tags to Selected supports fast keyboard searching/creation and repeated Enter-to-add; unassigned tags are removable in inspector.
Macro previews a hierarchy for confirmation, creates a tag per folder, applies to entries and assigns parent-folder tags as parents; v9.6.4 fixes this workflow.
Default search matches tag names, shorthand and aliases including inherited parents; tag: is optional.
Implicit/explicit AND, OR, NOT and parentheses; quotes or underscore substitution escape multiword names.
path: searches whole-path substrings by default or optional glob patterns; lowercase is case-insensitive, mixed case is sensitive. No forced case-sensitive all-lowercase query is available.
filetype: and mediatype: search extensions or media classes; roadmap marks optional extension-synonym consolidation implemented.
special:untagged finds entries without tags. special:empty availability conflicts across docs and is not included in this present claim.
Grid entries show detailed preview, file statistics, tags and fields in an inspector; roadmap marks infinite scrolling and configurable page size implemented.
Shortcuts cover opening/refreshing libraries, creating/managing tags, adding to selected entries and saving backups, with macOS equivalents.
Requires FFmpeg; thumbnails use a viable middle frame. Player supports play/pause, loop, autoplay, volume/mute and timeline scrubber, not yet fullscreen per roadmap.
FFmpeg enables common audio formats. Thumbnails use cover art or waveform; waveform caching is explicitly not implemented.
Matrix lists Canon CRW/CR2/CR3, DNG, Fuji RAF, Nikon NEF/NRW, Olympus ORF, Panasonic RAW/RW2 and Sony ARW.
HEIF and HEIC are explicitly listed in image preview matrix.
AVIF appears in image support and in FFmpeg video-format listing; no universal animation support is inferred.
JXL is listed as supported image preview, but its animation column is explicitly unsupported.
SVG thumbnail/preview is supported; animation is explicitly not supported.
GIF, animated WebP and APNG play in Preview Panel; grid uses cached thumbnails.

PDF previews render the first page. Apple iWork and OpenDocument documents use embedded thumbnails; PowerPoint support depends on an embedded thumbnail being available. This is preview support, not full document editing or established multipage navigation.

Photoshop PSD previews render a flattened image; Blender, Krita, Clip Studio Paint and other listed creative-project formats use embedded thumbnails, with availability caveats for formats such as Blender and Krita. Blender thumbnails do not establish interactive 3D model rendering.
ZIP/RAR/7z/Tar variants show first archive image; EPUB shows cover and comic-book archives use cover/first page.
Font formats show Aa/alphanumeric samples; plaintext previews render only first 256 bytes. Full text/syntax highlighting remain planned.
README cites Move File(s) to Trash as the exception to otherwise non-modifying cataloguing; no general undo journal is asserted.
Library autosaves; manual Save Library Backup and automatic migration backups preserve ts_library.sqlite under backups. Original content files are excluded.
Library Information provides unlinked repair, remove ignored entries, delete old backups and remove legacy JSON without deleting source media.
Panel shows library statistics and consolidated cleanup/backup access; no exact scale benchmark is claimed.
Image thumbnails are generated first viewing or after modification and stored in .TagStudio/thumbs; full preview panel does not use them.
Installed ripgrep replaces wcmatch scanning for speed and Git-style glob parity; docs warn fallback pattern behavior can differ.
Tools manual describes a working early preview generating all-library collage output under .TagStudio/collages with no customization yet.

Tools page describes loading dupeGuru result files and mirroring entry fields before deleting elsewhere, but current roadmap marks Fix Duplicate Files a regression still to restore; not a current built-in scanner.
Roadmap and library manual explicitly plan multiple content roots and a separately stored data directory; present root must host .TagStudio.
HAS/component relationships and tag overrides are planned, distinct from implemented parent inheritance.
Field search and comparisons of date/duration/size/dimensions are unchecked roadmap tasks and explicitly unavailable in search manual.
OCR and fuzzy search appear as future low-priority roadmap items, not built-in recognition.
Entry groups with nesting, per-group ordering, numbering and custom covers are planned; tags do not establish this album feature.
UI-agnostic core and CLI with intended MIT licensing are roadmap work, not a released public API.
Versioned TOML macros with add/refresh triggers and tag/field actions are planned; implemented Folders to Tags is a narrower tool.
README explicitly rejects native cloud integration; OS-mounted virtual drives are suggested instead.
README explicitly rules out built-in ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini/cloud-LLM connections; future external API possibilities do not change present status.
README documents a standalone Windows release binary without NodeJS or Docker; this is the uploader/archive CLI, not a native desktop gallery.
Standalone macOS executable distribution is documented for the upload/archive CLI; no desktop photo-browser UI is implied.
Standalone Linux executable is documented; connects to a separate Immich server for upload/server operations rather than providing its own gallery.
README explicitly includes FreeBSD among the supported standalone executable platforms.
Uploads images/videos recursively from local directories or ZIP files with optional headless operation; no NodeJS or Docker installation is required for the CLI itself.
Matches media with Google JSON and restores albums, descriptions, dates, locations and status flags. All split archive parts should be supplied together; unmatched media is excluded unless enabled.
Archived and partner photos default to included; trashed, unmatched and untitled-album inclusion are separate switches. Can select an album and group partner photos into a named album.
Reads iCloud export CSV metadata for dates and organization; optional --memories turns memories into albums. This is export ingestion, not documented live iCloud synchronization.
from-picasa automatically reads .picasa.ini, and folder ingestion can enable the same album-name processing.
Source and destination have separate server/API credentials and timeout/TLS settings; filters include dates, archived/trash state, favorites and minimum rating.
archive supports folders/ZIPs, Google, iCloud, Picasa and Immich inputs, writing local media rather than requiring a destination server.
Writes year/year-month folders while retaining original filenames where possible; archive destination is not wiped before an update.
Adds new files, checks changed existing files and refreshes sidecars from current server state; archive operation does not propagate deletions.
FOLDER or full PATH naming with customizable path joiner; alternatively put all media into one specified album or preserve Google/Picasa/iCloud associations.
Custom repeated tags, folder-derived tags, upload-session tags, Takeout timestamp tags and people-name tags are supported; imported people names do not establish face recognition.
XMP is passed unchanged for Immich to consume hierarchical tags, descriptions, GPS, capture time/timezone and camera settings; actual interpretation is server-dependent.
Folder uploads process associated XMP unless --ignore-sidecar-files is enabled; originals are forwarded without modification.

Technical guide prioritizes embedded EXIF, XMP, JSON and filename fallback, including common phone/screenshot naming patterns; this establishes ingestion metadata, not embedded rewriting of source files.
Archive sidecars contain original filename/date, GPS, album titles/descriptions, hierarchical tags, rating and favorite/archive/trash/partner flags; original XMP companions are also retained.
Pairs same-basename assets using directory/time/size heuristics; can leave separate, keep only one type, or stack with RAW/JPEG chosen as cover. Existing-server keep-only modes delete the other type.
Offers separate, keep-HEIC, keep-JPEG and either-cover stacking modes based on matching basenames; this is not by itself proof of Live Photo video pairing.
Uses device filename patterns for Huawei/Pixel/Samsung/Sony/Nexus/Nothing and a 900 ms temporal rule; modes include stack and RAW/JPEG preference. Docs warn rapid unrelated photos may be grouped.
Groups original, _a corrected and _b reverse-side scans with corrected image as stack cover.
stack operates on existing Immich assets without uploading media, using the same burst/pair/scanner rules and an optional timezone override.
Technical guide describes SHA-1 content checksums combined with server metadata and size checks to avoid redundant uploads; no perceptual similarity matching is established.
'--dry-run simulates upload transfers or stack mutations; recommended before keep-only stack operations.
'--ban-file distinguishes directory patterns by trailing slash; defaults exclude NAS thumbnail trees, Lightroom catalogues, OS artifacts and iCloud Recently Deleted.
Include/exclude extensions and IMAGE/VIDEO/all filters constrain transfer/archive selection rather than providing a photo-browser search UI.
Accepts a year, year-month, day or explicit comma-separated date range; source-server transfer has a separate from-date-range option.
Archive output preserves names where possible, appends numbered suffixes on conflicts and sanitizes incompatible characters.
Deduplication lets a restarted command skip files already on the destination; this is restart/idempotence behavior, not a byte-level partial-transfer checkpoint claim.
Parallel tasks default from CPU count and can be set within 1–20; timeouts and stop/continue/tolerated-error policies are configurable.
'--pause-immich-jobs defaults true to reduce thumbnail/other server workload during a bulk upload, requiring appropriate server permissions.
Interactive terminal UI can be disabled; API tracing and log level/file controls support diagnosing upload and stacking operations.
v0.32.0 detects server version and adapts errors/API behavior; album assets are retrieved through paginated metadata search for large collections.
Upload manual lists --overwrite, but v0.32.0 removes ReplaceAsset and its permission; exact surviving replacement behavior is not established by these conflicting docs.
Prebuilt cross-platform command-line program exposes upload, archive and stack operations without a NodeJS runtime.

Language chooser loads the locale manifest, displays language/native names and changes the user's VueI18n locale through the language API. Listed choices include Arabic, French, German, Japanese and Chinese variants; French navigation strings are verified. Some chooser text remains English, so full translation completeness is not claimed.
Operators run their own PHP/database instance, with Docker Compose now recommended and conventional installation still supported.
README recommends maintained Docker images/Compose; stable release documents image rebuild and database migration workflow.
Help provides distinct desktop and mobile-browser post-composition entry points.

Instance-configured ActivityPub supports inbox/outbox/shared inbox and remote follows; network timeline can show other servers' content. The config flag defaults off, so federation depends on deployment.
Configured federation supports signed follower-collection synchronization for followers-only delivery and block-list synchronization with cooldown/page limits.
Home shows followed accounts, Public shows local users and Network shows remote unmoderated content; these are chronological post feeds, not capture-date photo-library timelines.
Composer accepts several media files together or individually; per-post count is instance-configured (default max_album_length is four).
Optional captions are attached during composition; maximum length is configured by the instance (500 default), rather than embedded IPTC writeback.
Help documents media descriptions for visually impaired users, federated where supported. Help labels the composing UI experimental; current config sets an alt-text length limit of 1,000.
Help describes choosing a filter in media options, labels it experimental and explicitly says filters are not federated.
Hashtags in captions/comments link to topic pages; help documents up to 30 hashtags per post/comment and public-post discoverability.
Search bar locates hashtags; public tagged posts can appear in discovery/search pages.
Following a hashtag adds its photos/videos to feed; help gives follow limits of 20/hour and 100/day.
Private Account setting limits photo/video visibility to approved followers and prompts about existing followers/new requests; not an encryption feature.
Unlisted posts do not appear in public timelines, as explicitly documented in timeline help.
Post menu can enable or disable comments/replies from desktop or mobile browser.
Help documents tagging/mentioning up to five profiles in a post or comment; no automatic face recognition is implied.
Archived posts become unavailable for viewing/interactions and can be unarchived via profile Archives; help warns remote interactions may not be received while archived.

Direct supports photos/videos, text, feed posts, profiles, hashtags and locations; unsolicited messages may enter a filtered inbox. Help says direct media does not appear on hashtag/location pages or share onward through Pixelfed to other sites.
Accounts can be muted/blocked from feeds; direct messages can be reported or deleted. Config bounds user mutes/blocks/domain blocks.
Current configuration supports custom content filters with bounded keywords, scan length, regex size and creation/update rates; default limits include 20 filters and 10 keywords per filter.
When administrators enable the feature, parents create linked child accounts and choose posting, commenting, liking/sharing and federation permissions; configured child-count limits apply.
Profile security help explicitly directs users to enable 2FA in security settings.
Security help recommends reviewing Account Log for suspicious activity. This is account history, not a durable pre-operation crash-recovery file journal.
Migration uses account aliases and compatible Pixelfed/Mastodon migration extensions. Post migration is documented for Pixelfed v0.11.9+ only when server-enabled; completion can take hours.

Imports Instagram JSON ZIP data including photos, captions and hashtags. Current dedicated config defaults to 1,000 posts, permits video/WebP, excludes archived posts and supports administrator/account-age/follower eligibility restrictions.
Current instance configuration separately enables profile and post embeds by default; exact embed UI is not established by the unfinished help page.
Image optimization/resizing defaults on with configurable quality (80 default); upload file-size/account quotas are also configurable.
Configuration documents video upload resizing/optimization enabled by default; accepted video MIME types remain instance-dependent.
Optional HLS requires FFmpeg and defaults off; configurable bitrate governs generated streams.

README links official API documentation; config enables OAuth and application registration with rate limits, while personal access tokens are separately optional.
Federation configuration independently enables Atom feeds by default.
Instance config supports the push.pixelfed.net gateway with an API key; notification garbage collection has separate configurable retention.
Config controls open registration, email verification, maximum accounts and invites; curated registration and user invitations are optional modes.
Disabling hides profile, photos, comments and likes until login reactivates the account; permanent deletion is separate and may have an admin-configured grace period.
An off-by-default STORIES_ENABLED flag exists, but built-in Stories help is unfinished; inspected evidence does not establish lifecycle/privacy semantics or current shipped UI.
v0.15.2 notes continued refactoring toward a new Nuxt interface, not a completed shipped replacement.

Official feature/configuration guides document dynamic Chinese/English UI switching, persisted language preference, configurable default language and synchronized component-library locale; this is UI translation, not AI tag-language selection.
Web upload/admin/public-gallery interfaces support desktop and mobile layouts, Chinese/English switching and stored language preference.
Deploy the serverless service to one's Cloudflare account or self-host the Docker service; external storage providers remain separately configured.
Node.js/Hono Docker deployment uses SQLite and a persistent local data directory for service data.
Cloudflare Pages and Workers run the shared engine with KV/D1 persistence; Workers deployment via GitHub Actions supports secret-typed variables.

README explicitly links MarSeventh/satellite as the project's desktop client, separately from the hosting server and web frontend. The inspected README does not establish exact supported desktop OSes or release parity, so no Windows/macOS/Linux availability is inferred.
Click, drag/drop, clipboard files or URLs and batch upload with live progress and retry.
Uploading folders preserves their relative directory structure; upload directory picker supports suggestions/completion.
Telegram/R2/S3/Discord support chunking, while Hugging Face uses LFS direct upload. Guide quotes Telegram 20 MB parts and Discord commonly 10/25 MB, subject to provider policy.
Configure R2 bindings or S3 endpoint, credentials, bucket, optional region/path-style/CDN and custom User-Agent; quota/cost varies by provider.
Store payloads through configured bots/channels, with optional proxy URLs and Discord Nitro setting; not private local disk storage.
Configured token and dataset repository support private repositories and LFS-based large-file uploads.
Configure service URL, optional credentials/custom headers/public HTTP URL and automatic parent-directory creation.
Manage multiple channel configurations, configure load balancing and automatically retry through another available channel after upload failure.
Optional upload optimization has configurable 1–20 MB trigger threshold and target size from 0.5 MB to that threshold; release excludes animated files to preserve animation.
Can convert images in-browser before uploading and displays conversion/size-reduction badges; animated GIF/WebP/APNG skip conversion.
v2.7.8 skips local compression, WebP conversion and Telegram server-side compression for animated GIF, WebP and APNG.
Visual card/list views with rubber-band selection and batch operations in user-selected order.
Create directories and navigate a visual directory tree; search can retain folders or recursively expand results, with preference saved.
File management uses paginated loading and mobile swipe pagination; this is not a claim of virtualized rows.
Theme switching, custom title/logo/icon/footer/link prefix and solid, fixed, rotating or Bing backgrounds are configurable; Bing is an external request option.
Release describes video preview loading/orientation handling in File Details; codec coverage is not exhaustively specified.
File Details provides a compact audio player and skeleton preview states; other file types fall back to an information row.
Feature guide lists name and directory search, with recursive expansion configurable in v2.7.8.
Search/filter by user or AI-applied tags; no semantic embedding search is claimed.
Filter listed files by file type, using centralized MIME inference where metadata is missing or generic.
Filter by storage channel and access state in addition to name/directory/tag/type.
Autocomplete and common tags assist editing; multiple selected files can receive tags, preserving existing ones when AI suggestions are added.
Shows upload time, size and source IP; supports editing display filename/type and renaming File ID. These are hosting fields, not EXIF/IPTC editing.
Move files among directories with a visual destination picker; batch copy actions primarily concern generated links, so payload-copy semantics are not assumed.
File Details and batch management offer downloads; untransformed Read API returns original file content.
Ordinary /file paths usually do not require authentication, subject to configured domain/file/moderation rules; links can use custom prefixes.
Format preference is independent of content-link preference; choose hosted link or channel-specific Telegram/S3/CDN/WebDAV-public link, with unavailable choices falling back.
Enable unauthenticated browsing only for configured directory roots through /browse paths.
Separate admin/user sessions, user upload controls and per-user upload statistics are documented; this does not establish isolated personal photo libraries.
API tokens independently grant upload/delete/list/manage, can expire and be auto-deleted; web/API uploads use configured authentication codes.
Allowed source domains, file/IP allow/block lists and whitelist-only access can restrict public delivery; CDN caches may delay enforcement.
PBKDF2 with legacy password migration, HttpOnly sessions, isolated admin/user login and configurable age. HTTPS-only Secure cookies are configurable and disabled by default.
Supports moderatecontent.com API or separately deployed nsfwjs service; moderatecontent free registration is noted unavailable.
Optional custom API receives upload IP and selected JSON fields populate UploadAddress. This is uploader network geolocation, not photo GPS mapping.
v2.7.8 provides manually invoked single/batch tag recognition with selectable suggestions, progress, cancellation of future work and failed-item retries, without needing stored thumbnails.
OpenAI-compatible chat endpoints, up to 8 providers/16 models, configurable prompts/language/preferred vocabulary and structured output; text connection test does not prove image capability.

Live documentation describes opt-in post-upload tagging of originals on supported channels, excluding External and images over 20 MiB. Disabled by default; upload response does not wait. Presence in frozen v2.7.8 is not established by its notes.
AI_CONFIG_SECRET encrypts saved API keys; operator must keep a separate backup because secret loss/change makes keys unreadable. This does not encrypt hosted images end-to-end.
Read API accepts dimensions 1–4096, bounded aspect-preserving resize without enlargement, exact centre crop with cover or stretching with squeeze; admin can restrict allowed sizes.
With both dimensions and fit=cover, delivery resizes and centre-crops. It is not an interactive photo editor and requires image processing enabled.
Upload/read/delete/batch-delete/list/random-image/token endpoints with CORS; reads support HEAD and channel-dependent byte ranges, but not Range combined with resizing.

Enable /dav with separate credentials and destination channel for PROPFIND/GET/PUT/DELETE/OPTIONS/MKCOL. Feature overview also lists MOVE, while dedicated method table omits it; MOVE compatibility needs verification.

README links browser, WordPress/Typecho/Obsidian/OpenList integrations; feature guide names PicGo. The separately named Satellite desktop client has its own deployment finding rather than being inferred from API availability.
Counts, storage usage, channel distribution and date/channel upload trends, with capacity thresholds for R2/S3/WebDAV.
Admin can rebuild the file index in batches to avoid runtime CPU limits.
Feature guide documents batch file-data backup/restore; whether this includes every remote original rather than hosting records is not specified and must be verified before relying on it.
Cloudflare delivery caches public responses and avoids Range fragments; configured Cloudflare API credentials can purge cached content after deletion/access changes.

Live docs describe future-upload expiry presets up to 3650 days, optional uploader choice and scheduled/manual cleanup. Application access stops on expiry, while underlying public links/caches can persist; release parity is unverified.
Admin settings can disable telemetry that may disclose access URLs/domains. v2.7.8 removes remote sampling configuration, not telemetry itself; sampling defaults to 100%.

User preferences store an interface language and changeUserPreferences accepts a language setting. The supported UI translation enum includes English, French, German, Japanese, Ukrainian, Turkish, Dutch and Simplified/Traditional Chinese variants among others; v2.4.0 explicitly adds/updates translations.
Server reads operator-managed photo/video directories; README lists Linux deployments and appliance/community wrappers.
Recommended/minimal Compose examples separate media cache, catalogue database and read-only media mounts.
Web UI offers gallery, timeline, face and map views with authentication.
Filesystem paths are scanned without mandatory managed copying, preserving the operator's original organization.
Admin API adds/removes root albums for a user; Compose documents multiple media mounts with non-overlapping container paths.
Admin can scan all users or one user for new media; periodic scan interval is configurable and zero disables scheduled scans.
Scanner compiles per-album ignore lines using gitignore semantics and skips matching file names.
Directories become albums with parent/subalbum relations and breadcrumb paths.
Albums correspond to server directories, not a separately imported virtual organization.
Browse parent/child albums, root-only lists and optionally empty albums.
API assigns a selected cover photo or resets the album cover.
Timeline orders media first by day then album and supports older-than-date pagination and favorite-only results.
Viewer first displays a thumbnail until the high-resolution preview has loaded.
v2.4.0 explicitly adds swipe gestures for media viewing.
README says photos load when visible; this is image lazy loading, not evidence that DOM rows are virtualized.
Album/media/face/timeline API lists accept pagination to bound result sets.
Mark/unmark media and filter albums/timeline to favorites or albums containing favorites.
Schema exposes description, camera/maker/lens, date shot, exposure, aperture, ISO, focal length, flash, exposure program and GPS.
Displays dimensions, duration, codec, frame rate, bitrate, color profile and audio information.
Search API returns albums and media with separate result limits; inspected contract does not establish semantic or arbitrary EXIF search semantics.
README documents RAW photography support; release v2.4.0 specifically adds CR3.
v2.4.0 fixes HEIC EXIF extraction and README lists libheif as a server dependency.
Same-stem compatible JPEG/web images can accompany a RAW/non-web image and be skipped as separate catalogue entries. Disabling RAW processing instead leaves compatible images standalone.

For non-web-compatible photos, discovers filename.ext.xmp, stores its hash and regenerates JPEG preview/thumbnail when sidecar changes or disappears. This establishes sidecar change detection, not a general XMP field reader/writer or searchable sidecar metadata.
Video media expose videoWeb resources and are optimized for browser delivery; v2.4.0 improves playback startup.
Server converts supported video into web-ready resources rather than requiring browser-native support for every original container.
Configure qsv, vaapi or nvenc and expose required devices/runtime; only QSV is explicitly maintainer-verified.
Scanner detects faces and schema records normalized bounding boxes; custom builds can omit face support.
README describes grouping photos of the same person; schema stores face groups and counts.
API can compare unlabeled faces with labeled groups and move matches into those groups.
Set or clear a person's group label.
Merge source groups into a destination, move selected faces to another group or detach them into a newly created group.
MAPBOX_TOKEN enables a globe-projection map of geotagged media with map controls and media viewing; no offline map is established.
Map's GeoJSON source clusters nearby media with a 50-pixel radius and carries thumbnail properties into marker rendering.
Create users associated with assigned root paths, separating accessible directory trees.
User administration and scans require admin role; owned-media or valid share credentials authorize catalogue access.
Generate revocable public share tokens, optionally labeled for their owner/administrator.
Shares can require a password and have password protection changed or cleared.
Share creation and update APIs accept an optional expiration time.
Media exposes a list of downloadable file versions with role/title, URL, dimensions and file size; exact variants depend on processing.
README calls the gallery read-only and Compose mounts media using :ro while cache/database remain separate writable volumes.
Generated previews are stored in configurable PHOTOVIEW_MEDIA_CACHE; media can include blurhash placeholders.
Admin API sets the maximum concurrent scanner jobs; v2.4.0 also allows scanning to continue after individual-media failure.
Typed GraphQL queries/mutations cover catalogue, accounts, scans, faces and share tokens; development mode exposes a playground.

Legacy Lychee exposes upload, photo/album management and sharing through a browser connected to its PHP/MySQL server. The FAQ lists supported browser families; its historical compatibility list is not a current-version guarantee.
README lists the separate lycheeupload extension for uploading photos to Lychee via SSH. This is an advertised companion capability, not a built-in upload transport or independently tested extension.
README lists a separate Jekyll Liquid tag for embedding Lychee albums in generated sites; no current Jekyll-version compatibility was established.
README lists lychee-redirect as a separate extension that redirects an album name to a Lychee album, rather than a core routing guarantee.
README lists lychee-FlashAir for importing photos from a Toshiba FlashAir WiFi SD card. Hardware/network setup and current extension compatibility were not separately verified.

README describes lychee-webroot as a separate extension controlling photo accessibility and keeping Lychee files hidden. Its existence must not be interpreted as default core original-file protection.
README lists lychee-create-medium for generating missing medium-size photos; this is an external maintenance extension, not built-in image editing.
Runs on the owner's PHP/MySQL server and offers browser upload, management and sharing.
README recommends kdelfour's separate lychee-docker image, not a native desktop/mobile application.
Browser upload supports JPEG, PNG and GIF photos; server uses its own folder structure and database.
Import accepts a chosen server directory, recurses into subdirectories and creates albums named from folders with an Import prefix; reserved Lychee derivative directories are excluded.
URL import accepts multiple comma-separated URLs, verifies extension and image type before download, then feeds the managed photo-add path.
Requires a Dropbox drop-ins application key, requested on first use and configurable later.
skipDuplicates setting suppresses uploads of existing photos; older changelog also documents duplicate records sharing one stored file.
Changelog records stored photo checksums, switch from MD5 to SHA-1, and detection that stores only one file; no perceptual comparison or cleanup review workflow is established.
Create albums, rename and describe them, move photos between albums and merge albums; documented hooks and changelog establish each action.
Changelog documents Recent and Unsorted smart albums and downloadable SmartAlbums; arbitrary user-defined query albums are not established.
FAQ says covers are selected automatically from starred photos and upload order; starring an image influences the album thumbnail.
Photo tagging is available through the UI and t shortcut; setTags hook exists and IPTC tags can seed imported tags.
Photos and albums expose title/description editing and information panels; these are catalogue fields, not demonstrated embedded writes.
Photo shortcut s/f and setStar hook mark favorites, also influencing album covers.
Imports/displays EXIF including capture date and handles EXIF rotate/flip orientation with GD or Imagick.
Changelog documents headline/caption, title fallback when headline is absent, and photo-tag import.
Imagick path removes metadata from medium images and thumbnails; this does not establish stripping metadata from downloadable originals.
Search is available from the album overview; changelog explicitly describes albums shown before photo results. Exact searchable field semantics were not traced.
Changelog documents takedate sorting fixes; settings permit photo ORDER BY field/direction configuration.
sortingAlbums and sortingPhotos store SQL ordering fragments; some settings require direct database editing rather than a UI option.
Shortcuts cover previous/next photo, search, metadata editing, favorites, select all, upload and delete.
Changelog documents swipe gestures and later touch/swipe fixes.
Changelog describes fullscreen entry/exit based on mouse activity and hiding the pointer in fullscreen.
Share individual photos and albums; hidden shared albums can be reachable only by direct link rather than public listing.
Album password setting/checking hooks and password-prompt/download behavior are documented; this is album-level, not a claimed per-image password capability.
Public albums can be configured downloadable or not; no claim is made that this prevents saving images already displayed.
Shared images, but explicitly not albums, support Twitter Cards and Open Graph; historical Twitter domain approval instructions are not current service guarantees.
Download individual photos and album archives, including smart albums after the v3.1.6 fix; changelog notes title-based download filenames.
Creates thumbnails; when Imagick is present it additionally provides medium-size images for small screens and documented quality/performance improvements.
Changelog documents preloading large photos then preferring medium images for prefetch, plus album caching and saved scroll positions.
FAQ instructs copying the whole installation folder and cloning albums/photos/settings tables; this is a manual procedure, not scheduled backups or a versioned action journal.
FAQ points to plugins/Diagnostics/index.php for detected errors; changelog documents configuration/system checks.
Separately registered PHP observers receive before/after album, photo, session and import hooks; docs explicitly say plugins cannot modify the frontend.
README lists lychee-watermark, a separate plugin that adds a second watermarked photo on upload; not normal built-in editing.
README lists lycheesync as a separate extension for syncing an existing photo directory; this does not remove core managed-storage limitations.
README lists lychee-rss as a separate feed-generating extension.
FAQ explicitly says the app cannot use the existing folder structure and requires upload/import into its own storage/database.
FAQ says videos cannot be uploaded and video support is not planned for this legacy application.
FAQ explicitly answers no/not yet to creating multiple users; public album viewers are not independent owner accounts.
README supplies a downloadable Windows .exe with prompted or command-line operation; it is an organization utility, not a desktop gallery viewer.
README documents a downloadable macOS terminal executable and instructs Apple Silicon users to install Rosetta for the x86 build; native ARM64 distribution is not claimed.
README documents a downloadable Linux binary and an AUR package, with interactive prompts or explicit CLI options for headless use.
Processes manually merged extracted Takeout folders and assembles photo/video output with reconstructed filesystem modification times.
'--divide-to-dates creates year/month structure, including within album outputs; unknown dates go into date-unknown even without date subdivision.
'--copy avoids altering source file placement but needs additional space; default rename/move can leave a partly processed input on failure and does not support cross-drive moves.
Groups identical exported instances across year/album folders and merges their album associations before output.
Default album strategy creates Windows .lnk shortcuts or Unix symlinks to originals using relative target paths; failed link creation falls back to materializing a file.
duplicate-copy materializes files per album, trading substantially more space for portability across systems.
json strategy puts all media including Archive/Trash in the general output and writes albums-info.json mapping output basenames to album lists; not a full metadata-preservation sidecar.
nothing mode keeps year-folder photos without albums; documentation explicitly warns this omits Archive/Trash assets outside year folders.

Priority is Google JSON, embedded EXIF, optional filename guess, then aggressive JSON matching. --fix recursively applies dates to an arbitrary photo/video folder without running Takeout organization.

Matches photoTakenTime JSON through direct names, Google truncation, moved bracket suffixes, known edited suffixes and extension removal; last-resort aggressive suffix/digit removal is explicitly described as potentially dangerous in the pipeline.
Within the size limit reads Image DateTime, then DateTimeOriginal, then DateTimeDigitized, normalizing separators; skips non-images and files above 64 MiB.

Groups candidates by size and hashes equal-size groups with SHA-256; cached in memory. Critically, files larger than 64 MiB receive the same constant digest instead of content hashing, so exactness does not hold for those assets.

Drops repeated candidates within each album/year set, then merges album representations by size/hash; selects the best date-extraction accuracy when merging. Subject to the oversized-file digest limitation.
'--skip-extras removes recognized edited/effects/smile/mix suffix variants in several languages, with Unicode normalization for macOS names.
Repeatedly appends (1) before the extension until the output path is free; same helper protects link destinations. Separate startup logic may offer cleaning a pre-existing output directory.
Interactive mode prompts for folders/date division/album strategy; explicit input/output/album switches support headless NAS use and automation, with --help argument documentation.
README TODO explicitly lists JSON-to-EXIF writing as unimplemented in Dart; suggested ExifTool command is an external follow-up, not a built-in function.
README notes GPS transfer existed in older implementation but is missing in the Dart version.
Current README and commented-out CLI blocks explicitly disable interactive unzipping; users must unzip and merge beforehand despite stale help text suggesting auto-extraction.
Documented processing takes local input/output folders and operates on those files, without an upload step; downloading the initial Takeout remains external.

README identifies Weblate-powered app translations; inspected changelog explicitly adds Thai in v1.15.0, Urdu in v1.15.6 and Kurdish/Kurmanji in v1.14.6. These are application translations, not merely translated repository documentation; exhaustive language coverage is not claimed.
Native Android application built with Flutter, including Android TV integration and media read/write permissions.
Accesses/manages existing local photos/videos; Android 11+ uses MediaStore preferentially and requires Media Management permission for edits.
v1.15.4 adds calendar layout and a collection layout bar; later versions support Persian and Hijri calendars.
Catalogues panoramas/photo spheres and 360-degree videos; released changelog also adds panorama audio playback.
Supports videos including older AVI; UI exposes autoplay, looping, resumption, background playback and picture-in-picture, plus seek/play gestures and brightness/volume swipes.
v1.14.6 adds detection/filtering of slow-motion clips and range control in the player.
UI settings include repeat, shuffle, fill-screen, animated zoom, transition, interval and video-playback behavior.
Reorder browsing/selection quick actions; long-press tag quick action supports applying multiple tags; video gestures are separately configurable.
Date sorting is exposed; changelog specifically addresses mixed files with/without metadata dates.
Sort options include name, path and album plus item title.
Sort-by-size is an explicit user-interface option.
Sort-by-duration is an explicit option, separate from video playback controls.
Random sorting is added in v1.15.9.
Search includes metadata, dates and formats; filters identify undated, untitled, untagged, unrated and unlocated media, favorites and rejected ratings.
Search facets cover countries, states, places and coordinates. Recent releases add state-level Brazil/Canada display and coordinate-center copying.
Tags are searchable/navigable; tag/group renaming is documented and album/country/tag text filters accept slash-wrapped regular expressions.
Search contains ratings including unrated/rejected states; sorting by rating is also offered.
Filters distinguish images/videos, RAW, animations, Motion Photos, panoramas, slow motion, 360 video and GeoTIFF.
v1.15.9 displays credentials, overlays validity icons and filters unknown/invalid/valid/trusted states; removal of JPEG JUMBF credential metadata is supported.
Info displays embedded metadata including distinct Exif SubIFD sections; changelog notes handling large GIF XMP and metadata capture dates.
Tag editing offers recent tags and country/state/place placeholders; tags and groups can be renamed directly.
Info offers a rating editor and collection badges; precise embedding formats are not established by the strings.
Add/remove favorites actions and favorite filtering are exposed.
Info provides Edit title & description; this establishes the edit affordance, not universal file-format write compatibility.
Set a custom date, shift timestamps, extract from filenames or copy another date field; v1.15.0 explicitly saves assigned undated-item dates to metadata.
Editor offers latitude/longitude, map selection, custom coordinates and removal of location.
Location editor includes Import GPX and time-shift controls for associating locations with timestamps.
Removal actions include all metadata or selected categories/location/JUMBF. UI warns removing Motion Photo XMP can prevent embedded video playback.
Info exposes an Export metadata action; the exact serialization and sidecar interoperability are not established here.
Export dialog offers Write metadata along with format, dimension and quality controls.
Multi-item rename offers a naming pattern, inserted counter/hash/name fields and a preview.
Changelog documents moving files from app-media directories and rename/move handling on SD cards; these are ordinary file operations, not a catalogue-only action.
README explicitly supports SVG and v1.15.9 improves malformed SVG rendering.
README specifically identifies multipage TIFF as supported media.
Detects Motion Photos and exposes still conversion, separate video opening and image-only/video-only sharing; rotation attempts to rotate the video component too.
Detects GeoTIFF and exposes Show as map overlay rather than merely treating georeferenced TIFF as an ordinary thumbnail.
Collection has configurable burst patterns; v1.15.6 adds Realme pattern recognition.
Clockwise/counterclockwise rotation and horizontal flip are explicit actions.
Convert/export exposes format, quality and width/height controls; v1.15.9 supports a single target dimension across mixed aspect ratios and removes BMP output.
Export controls width/height and supports mixed-aspect-ratio conversions by one target dimension.
Maps integrate with album/tag/location navigation. Google Maps depends on Google Mobile Services and is excluded from Libre; base-layer options include Humanitarian OSM and Stamen Watercolor.
README explicitly attributes INTERNET permission to map viewing and reverse geocoding; offline geocoding is not claimed.
v1.14.6 adds showing paths on the map; the changelog does not specify every track-import format for this overlay.
UI confirms moving items to the recycle bin and offers Restore; changelog addresses recovery when the original directory is inaccessible. It is not treated as a durable operation journal.

Vaults support pattern/PIN/password and biometric unlock, with optional lock when the screen turns off. Warning states app uninstall/data-clear loses vault items; encryption at rest is not established by these sources.
Terms describe management of local media and state the developer never accesses photos/videos; map and opt-in diagnostics traffic are separate exceptions.
Play version can send anonymous error/diagnostic data to Firebase Crashlytics with consent; Izzy and Libre omit this capability.
v1.14.6 introduces automatic settings export; subsequent releases improve export failure feedback and storage-access handling.
Stats show geolocated-item count and top countries, states, places, tags and albums.
Provides launcher shortcuts and global search handling and can act as a media viewer for other Android apps; widget, picker and screensaver capabilities are recorded separately.
README explicitly lists widgets among Aves' Android integrations. Widget layout, refresh frequency and parity across Android/Android TV are not specified by this source.
README explicitly says Aves can serve as a media picker for Android applications, independently of opening media as a viewer; no cloud-provider or document-picker scope is inferred.

README lists a screen saver among the application's Android integrations, alongside Android TV support. This establishes a screensaver function, not desktop wallpaper scheduling or a separate casting protocol.
UI actions include copy to clipboard, open-with, set-as and opening coordinates in a map app; sharing and printing are recorded separately.

Android viewer exposes Share plus image-only and video-only sharing actions for supported compound media. These are app sharing affordances, not hosted public links or automatic publication to a social network.
The Android media-action strings explicitly include Print. Printer compatibility, print-layout controls and platform-specific print-service behavior were not established by the inspected source.

Runtime registers English, Simplified/Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Turkish, Brazilian Portuguese, French, German and Spanish. Bundled message graph permits offline view-language switching; English is fallback and French/Russian have explicit plural rules.
Native Windows installer for 64-bit Windows 10+; WinGet and official download are documented.
DMG and Homebrew Cask distribution for macOS Monterey 12.5 or later.
x64/ARM64 .deb and AppImage distributions; Ubuntu 22.04+ recommended and other distro compatibility depends on libraries/desktop.
Shared cleanup engine offers scan-only default, --apply, selection policy, --dry-run, JSON output and --no-progress; non-interactive mutation additionally requires --yes.
Scans system/user temporary data, application caches/logs/update packages, browser caches, package managers, IDE/compiler/Xcode data and inactive container build caches.
Finds dependencies, caches and build directories across Node.js, Rust, Gradle, Swift, Python, .NET, Godot and CMake projects.
Surfaces large local AI models, cached downloads and temporary transfers as reclaimable-space candidates, not as photo-analysis models.
Finds large installers, video files, archives and other bulky content for review without implying video playback or perceptual-video matching.
Groups equal-size files by BLAKE3 content hash after sample filtering. Sample hashes alone do not establish equality; full hashing checks open-file identity/size/time and current path.

Builds recursive fingerprints from file sizes/content hashes and child-tree fingerprints, sorting tokens without incorporating filenames. Skips empty trees, unreadable/unknown entries and link-like objects; this is content/tree equivalence, not identical names.
Prefer shortest path by default, shortest filename, oldest modification or newest modification; deterministic tie-breaks handle equal/missing times. Protected copies become keepers automatically.
Protected locations participate in matching but cannot be deleted. Directories containing protected descendants are also rejected; protection changes deletion authority, not scan coverage.
Public product scan entry accepts exclusion options alongside typed cleanable/protected roots.
Duplicate scan APIs accept minimum_bytes to limit eligible files; no maximum-size selector is established here.
Toggling an already-selected smart-selection group clears its paths while retaining selections in other groups.
Both selection utilities and native validation require at least one remaining entry in every affected duplicate group.
Duplicate scan takes a vector of filesystem roots, including separately protected descendants; this is scan scope rather than multiple photo catalogues.
Complete bounded duplicate results remain in Rust; only an initial page enters the WebView and later pages load on demand using a scan ID.
Concurrency depends on available CPUs and volume scheduling; rotational, removable, network and unknown storage use one hashing worker to limit random-I/O costs.
Hashing checks cancellation between reads/samples and recursive directory fingerprinting checks its operation guard; disk analysis also documents cancellation.
Switch visualization and depth while browsing folder/file lists; Standard measures physical allocated bytes, while Windows Fast uses logical lengths.
Reports omissions by permissions, read errors, exclusions, link/mount boundaries and unknown causes; unreadable is distinguished from measured empty directories.

Exports current-directory analysis with depth 1–6, optional full paths, configurable entry limits and separate remainder/omission accounting; never silently rescans. Reports are evidence, not importable state or deletion authority.
Default scans do not modify files. Cleanup, uninstall and system changes require explicit review/confirmation; this is not an immutable library mode once actions are approved.
Native duplicate deletion verifies current-scan membership, expected size/modification and protected roots independently of UI selection; stale/foreign candidates are rejected.
Records completed cleanup/system changes, reclaimed space and failures. Duplicate deletion appends history after execution; this is not an undo-capable transactional operation journal.

Duplicate and disk-analysis deletion directly remove selected files, report removed/already-absent/failed outcomes and reconcile scan caches. Analysis stops a batch on possible partial mutation or lost authority.
Analysis export flushes and syncs a sibling temporary file before atomic publication; failed writes preserve the previous report destination. This is report safety, not copied-photo verification.
Clears selected browsing history, searches, cookies, recent items and clipboard traces; this is an OS/application administration tool, not photo-metadata privacy or secure disk erasure.

Deep Cleanup overview documents application optimization to reduce supported application size without affecting normal use; exact eligible apps and transformations are not specified there. This is not photo compression.
Uninstalls applications and reviews associated caches/settings/leftovers, treating potential personal files cautiously. AI manual warns vendor uninstallers control their own final scope.
Manage startup registrations to reduce login/background load, with ability to turn entries back on.
Only built-in validated settings are accepted; no arbitrary commands/scripts/registry paths. Values are reread after changes and high-impact, elevated or restart-required actions are flagged.
Documented maintenance targets missing search results, incorrect icons, sound and network issues; available operations depend on platform.
Since 1.2.3, browse by app/menu location, disable/restore/remove entries, configure file types, switch supported Windows 11/classic styles and optionally restart Explorer.
Add copy-path/name/image-dimensions, terminal-here, desktop shortcuts and system-tool shortcuts.

CPU/GPU/memory/network/disk trends; supported devices also expose temperature, power, battery and disk-health information, with menu/taskbar/tray/floating displays. These are whole-computer metrics, not photo-library analytics.
Find and quit resource-heavy applications and free memory manually or automatically; performance improvements are project claims.

Explains cleanup, privacy, startup, settings, maintenance, large/duplicate files and uninstall candidates on explicit request. Does not select items, change risk classification, execute commands or authorize cleanup.

Official builds offer a daily free quota; custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints can include local loopback services. Official initial policy is 20/day with 60-second cooldown and 30-day context/reply retention; provider settings and billing remain separate.
1.2.3 scans uninstall/startup/privacy pages on first opening and preserves results, scroll position and category choices on page switches.
Cloudflare Pages serves the upload homepage; current homepage is dependency-free, while the older Nuxt page remains separately accessible.
Deploy through Git integration or Wrangler Pages; a free pages.dev hostname and custom domains are documented. This is a Pages Functions project, not a directly deployable Worker entry point.
Upload multiple files by selection, drag-and-drop or paste, with per-file progress.
Anonymous uploads remain enabled unless both upload Basic Auth variables are configured.
UPLOAD_BASIC_USER and UPLOAD_BASIC_PASS protect both browser and multipart API uploads independently of dashboard credentials.
Upload returns a /file path; interface copies URL, Markdown, BBCode or HTML links.
KV plus ENABLE_SHORT_URLS allocates short IDs of 4–16 characters, default six. Old long URLs continue to resolve.
A bot token and channel/chat ID route uploads into a channel where the bot is an administrator; source files reside on Telegram.
An img_r2 bucket and STORAGE_PROVIDER=r2 redirect new uploads to R2. Self-describing provider IDs preserve access to old Telegram and R2 files across switches.
POST /upload accepts multipart file and returns a JSON array containing src. It works with configurable upload clients such as PicGo.
Images, video, audio and PDF are served for inline browser opening rather than forced download; browser format support still applies.
Binding img_url KV enables dashboard grid/waterfall layouts, online image preview and batch record selection.
Dashboard preview allows zooming in/out and viewer rotation; documentation does not establish rewriting the original image.
KV listing supports cursor/load-more and a limit defaulting to 100 and capped at 1000; internal short-link/cache keys are excluded from returned file keys.
README describes server-side filename-prefix search; list endpoint passes the supplied prefix to KV rather than providing full-text catalogue search.
Administration supports renaming listed files; July 2026 notes record a fix to this workflow. Physical Telegram object renaming is not established.
KV-backed administration displays total recorded images and each item's list/moderation state.
BASIC_USER and BASIC_PASS enable dashboard login. Cloudflare Access is an alternative, with both /admin and /api/manage/* requiring protection.
KV records can be blacklisted to block loading or whitelisted to bypass moderation; whitelist-only mode requires approval before serving.
ALLOWED_REFERERS accepts exact and wildcard-subdomain hosts. Other referring sites receive 403, but absent referers and the host's own domain remain allowed; this is not private-link authentication.
AI binding plus KV enables remote vision moderation; verdicts are cached per file. Adult-content classifications redirect to a block page. Review failures are explicitly fail-open.
Override the vision model or use a built-in fallback chain. Optional Cloudflare account credentials discover active vision models, exclude retired ones and cache the catalogue for six hours.
Existing ModerateContent keys remain usable only for old Telegraph-hosted files; new registrations are closed and Telegram Bot API files cannot be reviewed by this provider.
Homepage identifies missing environment variables or bindings and tells operators where to configure them before the first upload.
Delete removes the dashboard record, not the Telegram/Telegraph original; later access can recreate a record. Blocking access uses the blacklist instead.
disable_telemetry disables documented remote telemetry; file-serving middleware and upload handler otherwise call telemetry functions.
Configure site/header name, title, background and hiding the dashboard entry via GET /api/config; hiding the entry does not make /admin inaccessible.
An enabled GitHub Actions upstream-sync workflow updates the fork hourly, after which connected Pages deployment can rebuild.

The self-hosted PHP application exposes browser image upload, waterfall management and administrative role/storage settings; this is the discontinued open-source web interface, not a native desktop client or the separate paid Pro+ edition.
Browser upload/management application deployed on a PHP/Imagick server, not a local photo catalogue.
README lists MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite and SQL Server with explicit minimum versions.
Strategies support AWS S3, Alibaba OSS, Tencent COS, Qiniu, Upyun and Minio in addition to local files.
WebDAV is explicitly a storage strategy, alongside FTP and SFTP; no automatic desktop-library sync is implied.
README explicitly lists FTP as a configurable remote storage backend; this is storage integration, not source-folder library synchronization.
README explicitly lists SFTP as a configurable remote storage backend; release 2.1 updates its driver extension.
Drag-and-drop and pasted images enter managed storage, with dynamic selection of a storage strategy allowed for the uploader's group.
README explicitly lists multi-image upload; role-group configuration additionally exposes a concurrent-upload limit.
Ingestion checks a global allow-guest setting, assigns the guest role group and applies guest upload limits by IP.
Upload checks user status, optional verified email, per-user capacity and default album/visibility settings.
Each role group can access multiple strategies, and each strategy can serve multiple groups; per-group policies control upload behavior.

Role group sets permitted extensions, maximum individual file size in KB and concurrent upload count; ingestion rejects unsupported extensions or oversized files. Total account capacity is a separate control.

Before accepting an authenticated user's upload, ImageService adds its size in KB to the sum of that user's existing image-record sizes and rejects the upload if the result exceeds the user's capacity. This establishes account-level recorded-storage accounting, not a physical-backend free-space measurement.
Configurable minute/hour/day/week/month counts apply to a logged-in user or anonymous uploader IP, based on recent image records.
Naming rules combine year/month/day, timestamp, unique/random tokens, original filename and user ID (zero for guests). These are upload-path rules, not capture-date organization.
README describes waterfall display, context menu, single/multiple selection and rename operations.
API lists/deletes albums and ingestion can assign a valid user-configured default album; no nested/smart album semantics are established.
README lists a public image square; ingestion defaults to private and honors a registered user's default image permission.
Upload UI offers copying and one-click link copying; API returns computed links and storage paths.
Group can enable original protection, withholding direct links and serving processed/cached responses through PHP with configurable image cache lifetime; not encryption.
Supports text or image, tiled positioning, offsets and rotation; text has font/color/size and image has dimensions/opacity. Modes either overwrite stored image or generate dynamically.
Role group selects saved format and quality; store applies processing before hashing, excluding ICO/GIF/SVG from this conversion path.

Within a storage strategy, ingestion matches both MD5 and SHA-1 of post-processed upload bytes; matching content reuses path/name and creates only a new database record. No byte verification or visual similarity is claimed.
Group selects Tencent, Alibaba or configured NSFW.js service; can flag unhealthy or delete/reject. NSFW.js threshold is configurable; PSD/ICO/TIF/SVG skip the examined scan path.
Ingestion creates thumbnails; original protection/dynamic watermarking uses cached processed images with configurable TTL and explicit cache clearing.
README lists file cache by default plus configurable Memcached, Redis, DynamoDB and relational database alternatives.
