API v1 exposes upload, storage strategies and token issuance; authenticated routes list/delete images and albums, revoke tokens and fetch profile. Feature can be globally enabled/disabled.
Authenticated image listing uses pages of 40 and returns dimensions, MIME, extensions, sizes, hashes, timestamps and link fields.
2.1 adds per-strategy image URL parameters; docs recommend provider-side transformation rules for third-party storage to avoid heavy PHP processing.
README lists both upgrade modes as implemented; this is historical functionality and does not imply continued upstream updates.

Current paid-edition documentation advertises plans, orders, tickets, feedback, announcements, coupons and Alipay/WeChat payments. These belong to separate Pro+, not demonstrated open-source repository functionality.
Lychee runs on a server/web space and lets users upload, manage, view and share photos from a browser; no native desktop gallery is implied.

README recommends published Docker images and Compose, including persistent uploads/settings-related storage and an optional separate background worker. This packages the web server, not a native desktop client.

Official edition comparison explicitly includes multiple supported UI languages in both Free and SE. Its footnote warns that some languages remain untranslated, so complete translation coverage is not assumed.
Runs on the user's PHP server or supplied Docker images; current README requires PHP 8.4+ for source deployment and distinguishes latest stable from edge.
Upload from a local computer or import server files through web UI/CLI; chunked upload and full directory-tree import are listed in the free edition.
Official overview lists URL and Dropbox sources; provider-specific current authentication restrictions were not established.

Free comparison lists directory-tree import and optional removal of catalogue photos/albums no longer present in source directories; these are potentially destructive sync choices, not a read-only guarantee.
Free edition lists fast filename/title duplicate checks and separate content-hash duplicate detection. These are distinct matching modes; visual similarity is not established.

Edition table includes hash deduplication and administration duplicate finding. Current/original checksum tracking is documented; contradictory algorithm descriptions are not resolved into a specific algorithm claim.
A photo can belong to multiple regular albums without duplicating files; album title, description, cover, header, sorting and layout can be customized.
Regular albums contain photos and child albums with subtree operations; tag and system smart albums are flat.

User-defined tag albums dynamically match tag combinations and are shareable; system albums include Recent, Highlighted, Public, Unsorted and On This Day. Arbitrary custom system-smart queries are not supported by this model.
Built-in smart collection selects capture dates matching today's month/day in earlier years, subject to permissions.
Justified, masonry and square layouts, album cover/header controls and customizable album thumbnail aspect ratio are free.
Free standalone and album timeline views respect access control and offer date navigation; custom granularity/format are SE-only.
SE comparison separately gates custom timeline granularity, formatting and per-album timeline customization.
Flow page presents albums as a feed with access control and configurable base album; separate frame-display module is included free. Compact/extensively customized flow cards are SE.
Official overview documents full-screen images and forward/backward keyboard navigation.
Free edition includes photo slideshow and album previous/next slideshow.
Both themes and multilingual UI are free edition features.
Configurable 1–1000 item pages, defaults 30 albums/100 photos; choose infinite scroll, load-more or page navigation independently. Infinite scroll retains loaded pages and grows memory usage.
Free feature table and overview establish basic photo searching; arbitrary technical-field query syntax is not established.
Tag listings and autocomplete accompany global tag rename/merge/delete management and dynamic tag albums.
Extracts camera/lens/exposure, GPS/orientation and capture timestamps; display can hide sensitive metadata and manual catalogue values can override extracted values.
Official overview explicitly supports/display IPTC; processing guide states default metadata access is read-only rather than writing user changes into files.
Processing reference identifies EXIF/IPTC/XMP as read metadata sources; external sidecar matching is not established here.
Desktop-like multi-selection and editing tags/metadata for selected photos are documented; baseline edits change catalogue data.
Edition comparison marks numeric photo ratings as a free v7 capability; optional embedded writing exports the owner's rating only.
Assign tags singly/in bulk and globally rename, merge or delete tags; highlighted photos feed a built-in smart album.
Personal favourites are specifically SE in the edition table and are separate from free photo highlighting/smart albums.

Current reference documents disabled-by-default ExifTool queue jobs writing title/description/tags across EXIF/IPTC/XMP and owner's rating into original and preserved RAW files. Local disks only; S3 is skipped. Separate checksum-refresh option defaults on.
Photo records associate still and video using content ID/checksum/path for motion viewing. v8 hover playback is version-specific rather than baseline UI.

Current photo reference supports legacy MicroVideoOffset and Motion Photo 1.0/Ultra HDR embedded clips, plus artisan extraction for prior still-only imports; v8 grid badges/hover behavior is separately identified.

Imagick pipeline converts supported camera RAW/PSD sources to a JPEG display original and retains untouched RAW; conversion failure keeps source as-is with limited preview. RAW downloads have a separate default-off setting.
Current dual-variant pipeline lists HEIC/HEIF among Imagick-convertible source formats and retains native originals where conversion succeeds.
Requires Imagick/ImageMagick built with libjxl; accepts signatures and can write JXL variants. GD cannot handle it and unsupported browsers have no image fallback.
Generates medium/small/thumb and high-DPI variants plus low-quality placeholders; dimensions/quality are configurable and original access is separately permissioned.

Current processing settings offer original/JPEG/WebP/JXL variants, with codec dependencies for optional formats. Quality 0 requests lossless WebP/JXL; changing settings only affects new variants until old ones are regenerated.
Free import auto-rotation is listed and edit grant includes photo rotation; no claim of a general nondestructive editor.
Free GPS localization and map module plot media; no offline basemap or offline geocoder was established.
Regular albums can attach multiple GPS/GPX tracks displayed on the map; this does not establish automatic GPX-based geotag writing.
Albums/photos can be public; link-required albums are not listed and require knowledge of the URL. Owners/admins alone control visibility/sharing.
Album passwords are checked even for explicitly permitted users and unlocking persists for the session.

View, full-original, download, upload, edit, move and delete rights are separate. Destination albums require edit; ownership-changing actions are constrained. Detailed grant section says permissions must be explicitly propagated to children, although a later legacy paragraph contradicts it.
Unlimited users, registration, invite links, cross-user sharing, per-user trust level and WebAuthn/OAuth login are listed free.
Upload and edit grants let selected authenticated users contribute or edit without permission to change sharing; upload moderation is available in v7.
Public-link upload grants require SE; public shares never grant edit, move or delete.

SE's per-user upload quota is explicitly defined by the user manual as quota_kb, a storage limit in kilobytes tracking total photo storage for each user; further uploads are blocked when that quota is exceeded. This is account-capacity enforcement, not a per-upload file-size or file-count limit.
SE includes named user groups for team/client/family access management; a user can belong to multiple groups and membership records carry a group role.
Edition comparison explicitly lists group administrators for delegated group management as an SE capability, distinct from granting full-system administrator status.
SE supports group sharing and per-album group access rights. AccessPermission can target a user group so album grants apply to its members; this is separate from free individual cross-user sharing.
Edition matrix separately lists per-user space usage for SE; reporting consumed storage is distinct from enforcing the account-capacity quota.
SE provides an admin note for each user; the user manual distinguishes this internal note from the user's public/profile description.
Edition matrix lists multi-admin support as SE; the user model's may_administrate permission grants full system administration, unlike a delegated group role.
Edition table marks album embedding and RSS feeds as free modules.
SE offers secured image URLs; this is link protection, not evidence of encrypted-at-rest media or end-to-end encryption.
SE supports watermark images with adjustable scaling, placement and opacity.
SE gates dominant color-palette extraction; photo model describes five stored colors. Search/theming use cases in architecture prose do not independently prove a complete color-search UI.
SE adds installation/library/photo/album statistics including downloads and shares; API v3 Insights also has an SE gate.
Edition comparison specifically gates renaming rules on import/upload to SE; free UI retitling is a different operation.

Pro addon above SE supplies pricing, size/license choices, basket/order administration, managed download links and Mollie/PayPal/offline payments. Print support does not integrate with printing services.
S3 disk supports bucket, endpoint, region, root and path-style configuration; default image disk is local. Metadata write-back currently skips non-local variants.
Free worker mode uses a separately running queue worker/container for processing; face scans and metadata-embedding jobs rely on queues.
Photo/album ZIP downloads are free but subject to download/full-photo grants; preserved RAW export additionally needs raw_download_enabled.
Free logs, diagnostic checks, maintenance settings and CLI derivative regeneration are documented; optional JXL and face services expose health/configuration diagnostics.
API documentation and CLI import are free; current repository has v2 and newer v3 routes, with v8-specific gates on some endpoints.

Concrete setup guide describes Python sidecar, queue worker, detection/size/blur thresholds and bounding-box overlays, but live table marks Soon v8 and edition claims conflict. Not counted as generally released.
How-to describes DBSCAN cosine-distance grouping of stored embeddings, noise labels and reviewable clusters; shares unresolved v8/edition availability.
How-to describes person profiles, similarity thresholds and selfie-based profile claims. Requires configured sidecar/model; exact current released entitlement remains contradictory.
Documented workflows assign/merge people, destroy dismissed faces/embeddings, reset failed/stuck scans and synchronize embedding stores. Four permission modes range from public to restricted.

Configured face service reads a shared read-only photo volume, stores SQLite/pgvector embeddings and downloads a model initially; publication/edition ambiguity remains, and this is not fully air-gapped setup.
Comparison table explicitly labels sensitive-content detection Soon v8 and SE-only; existing manual sensitive-album flagging is separate.
Free sensitive-album module and is_nsfw album field allow manual content marking; no automatic classifier is implied.
Edition table explicitly labels custom Flow inclusion strategy Soon and SE rather than an already available core feature.
SE separately provides compact Flow cards and extensive card customization; the basic access-controlled feed is free.
Edition comparison gates displaying tags directly on the album view to SE, despite free tag assignment, listing and tag-album creation.
SE v7 can remove Lychee branding; free users can separately hide SE promotional calls to action without obtaining white-label entitlement.
Official edition matrix lists contact form as an SE-only v7 module.

v0.3.3 adds Hungarian, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Ukrainian and Traditional Chinese, bringing documented UI languages to fifteen; v0.3.2 adds a welcome-screen language selector. Date/time formatting follows the system region independently of UI language. This is separate from optional multilingual semantic search.
Indexes existing ordinary files without mandatory managed re-import copies; uninstalling the app/catalogue does not delete original media.
Supports multiple libraries with management controls and per-library cache sizes/cleanup.
Folder-based albums and cached subfolder trees reflect existing directories; subfolder refresh can update hierarchy without full media rescanning.
Rescans detect many external changes, and Live Photo associations update incrementally; external renames/moves can disrupt database-only organization.
Album import, drag/drop and clipboard workflows copy media into chosen folders, respect exclusions and update the library without a separate full scan.
Choose YYYY/YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY/YYYY-MM, YYYY or one folder; uses capture date with modification-time fallback and preserves filenames.
Import skips duplicate content and reports imported/skipped/failed counts; identical or nested source/destination paths are guarded.
In-app rename/move/copy/delete updates catalogue records and carries supported grouped components together.
Drag photos/videos into the OS file manager or other apps as actual files, up to 1,000 per operation; catalogue-only annotations do not travel with them.
Keeps removable/network albums visible with cached metadata/thumbnails and an availability warning; operations needing originals are gated until reconnection.
Per-album file-type, small-image and folder exclusions have a scan preview; v0.3.3 replaces the previous global small-image filter.
Toolbar switches mutually exclusive grid, filmstrip and map modes; configurable thumbnail badges expose format and exposure settings.
Hierarchical Years/Months/Days navigation supplies localized month names and counts; grouping adapts to dates, folders, cameras, lenses or locations.
v0.3.0 explicitly improves virtualized viewport loading and grouped/search result loading to reduce browsing work.
Compare up to four images side-by-side; optional navigator sharpness grid assists focus comparison, without documenting an automatic quality score.
File Info preview has scroll zoom, double-click fit and a draggable full-image viewport navigator; video zoom pans around the cursor.
Page Up/Down navigation, viewer shortcuts and keyboard stepping for straighten are documented.
Release notes explicitly describe stopping slideshows when leaving filmstrip or entering map mode.

Viewer and hover playback support videos and paired motion content. H.264 has compatibility processing when native playback is unavailable; HEVC/VP9 are natively supported on macOS and Linux depends on GStreamer plugins.
Regular filename, text and metadata result caps were removed in v0.3.2; in-view/sidebar search added in v0.3.3.
Browse/filter by date, camera, lens, location, tags, ratings and faces; camera/lens sidebar tabs include counts.
AI Search and Smart Albums accept file-type constraints, including a combined Live & Motion Photos condition.
CLIP-based image/text similarity supports natural-language prompts and similarity cutoffs; the earlier 1,000-result cap was removed.
Optional downloaded model extends search to over 50 languages; download failures on slow connections are explicitly discussed in release notes.
Local image similarity finds visually related media; it is separate from documented duplicate cleanup, whose exact detection algorithm is not established by these docs.
Semantic search, smart tags, face detection/clustering and video indexing execute locally along with thumbnail/RAW preview generation.
Local smart tags and subject-based browsing/search are documented; user-managed tags are stored in the catalogue.
Privacy policy explicitly lists local face detection and storage of derived face data.
Locally groups faces and exposes a People list with incremental loading and person avatars; manual correction/naming specifics are not established here.
Collections accept drag/drop across the library, reordering and duplicate-aware additions; removing membership does not move originals to Trash.
Saved rules include file types with configurable grouping/sorting/order; built-ins include Recently Added and On This Day.
Reads capture time, camera, lens, orientation and GPS; video metadata includes Apple QuickTime tags and GPS where available.
Bulk tag management supports collapsible/reorderable groups and moving tags between groups, with a protected Default group. Groups are not documented arbitrary-depth tag hierarchies.
Ratings support organization and filtering but remain in Lap's database, not embedded files or XMP sidecars.
Favorite state is exposed in library navigation and stored locally.
Comments are library-only metadata and do not automatically appear in other photo applications or exported copies.
Local catalogue preserves culling states including Picks and Rejects, separate from file-embedded metadata.
Scans PNG prompts from Automatic1111, InvokeAI, ComfyUI and NovelAI into empty comments without overwriting existing notes.
Refresh file info rereads selected files together; unchanged cloud-only OneDrive/macOS dataless entries are detected without forcing downloads.
Duplicate scans can target a collection or selection; library-wide cleanup reports reclaimable space and bulk removes chosen copies. Sources do not specify hash versus perceptual equality.
Bulk removal across duplicate sets explicitly preserves each set's keep choice.
Supports many camera RAW families; choose rendered or embedded previews, adjust render brightness and request full rendering when zooming. Preview fallback works both directions.
Listed image formats include HEIC/HEIF/HIF with FFmpeg/ImageIO fallback decoding discussed per platform.
AVIF is explicitly included in supported image formats.
JXL is explicitly included alongside HDR/EXR/PSD and JPEG 2000 image formats.
Recognizes HEIC/MOV pairs, displays a LIVE badge and plays motion; companion MOV files are suppressed from ordinary lists.
Plays embedded video in supported Android/Google Motion Photo JPEGs and can recognize them in existing libraries.
Enabled pairs appear as one item with viewer switching between RAW modes and paired JPEG/HEIC.
Live Photo MOV, Apple AAE adjustment sidecars and enabled RAW companions stay together during rename/move/copy/delete.
Crop includes arbitrary-angle horizon straightening with a zero-snapping ruler, keyboard stepping and live result preview.
Built-in image editing supports rotation and flipping; saved edits write a resulting image to the selected destination.
Resize is explicitly included in built-in editing.
README documents basic image adjustments, without asserting a full RAW-development workflow.

Grid, justified mosaic and picture-pile layouts support layering/moving/rotating/scaling, randomization, backgrounds, spacing, borders and shadows; export from originals at full resolution or print at 300 dpi to configurable/A4/photo pages.
Map follows current filters and can retain position/zoom across cluster exploration; map styles, density heatmap and nearby-photo panel are documented.
Clusters geotagged media and provides configurable photo-marker size.
Tianditu is available for China with the user's own API token; normal maps fetch online tiles, including OpenStreetMap.
Core browsing and provisioned local AI are designed for offline use, but map tiles explicitly need Internet and update/telemetry/model requests are separate exceptions.
No forced cloud account or photo upload; policy says library paths, queries, annotations, embeddings and media are not sent in analytics.
Thumbnail quality/resolution is adjustable up to documented 1024 px, with grid sizes up to 720 px and reduced-resolution RAW previews.
Date-based import exposes progress, cancellation and continuation controls.
Documented import continuation works with duplicate skipping and imported/skipped/failed feedback; not claimed as a universal durable task journal.
Manage Libraries shows cache sizes and removes thumbnails per library without implying removal of personal organization data.
Settings > Storage controls database location and creates a backup; README recommends backing up database/configuration alongside originals.
Detects per-library corruption and prompts a library switch while preserving the original database instead of silently rebuilding it.
Configure multiple external apps and a default; opening more than 100 files requires confirmation.
Wallpaper action supports macOS, Windows and GNOME Linux, including suitable paired RAW companion images.

Changelog repeatedly documents translation updates and explicitly adds an Android 13+ app-language picker in 6.25.0, with in-app language change in 6.26.9. This establishes localized UI without inferring an exact completeness/language count.
Native Android application; version 6.26.0 raised minimum Android to 6 and README links the F-Droid package.
Folder and All Files views operate on device media; no managed re-import is required. Android 11+ storage permissions affect visibility.
Manage Included Folders adds missed locations; exclusions are recursive and affect only this app. An included folder wins when also excluded, allowing a root exclusion plus selected inclusions.
Switch folders/all-files, group direct subfolders, pin multiple folders, select a default folder and reorder folders by dragging.
Square cropping, rounded or square corners, spacing, horizontal scrolling, file-type labels, duration labels and folder media counts are configurable.
Group by capture date or last modification, daily or monthly, with optional per-section counts; grouping and sorting are independent.
FAQ documents date-taken sorting and its associated date-fix action for copied files.
Main screen can search files rather than folders and switch to searching across all visible folders; destination picker also supports search.
Filters distinguish images, videos, GIFs, RAW, SVG and portrait categories; thumbnails can also be grouped by type or extension.
Hide system UI, choose black background or maximum brightness, select orientation policy and configure visible bottom actions and extended details.
Options include one-finger zoom, deeper zoom, 1:1 zoom with two double taps and highest-quality image rendering to reduce banding.
Vertical swipes adjust photo brightness or video volume/brightness; rotation gestures, edge taps and downward dismissal are configurable.
Supports autoplay, looping, remembered playback position, double-tap seeking, separate-screen horizontal gestures and double-tap video zoom.
Choose photo/video/GIF inclusion, interval, random or reverse ordering, looping and fade/slide/no transition.
README explicitly lists panoramic photos among supported media; spherical metadata requirements are not specified.
README allows appearance customization; release history adds automatic and Material You themes, with Material You default on Android 12+.
README lists RAW and media filters provide a separate RAW category; individual camera decoder coverage is not specified.
README and file-type filters explicitly support SVG images.
Version 6.21.0 includes HEIC zoom fixes, establishing the supported viewing path without a conversion claim.
Version 6.23.2 adds .avif support specifically on Android 12.
Supports GIF, WebP thumbnail animation including folder thumbnails in 6.28.0, and APNG from 6.21.0.
Copy/move destination picker remembers the last folder, can show excluded folders and supports SD-card paths subject to Android permissions.
Release history documents file renaming and resizing-with-renaming; FAQ describes renaming dot-prefixed hidden folders. Batch-rename templates are not established.
Settings can delete empty folders after deleting their contents; this is not a whole-disk empty-folder scanner.
Mark favourites on thumbnails, toggle in the viewer and export/import favourite file paths; this export is not a full media backup.
Select thumbnails and use Fix Date Taken when copied files sort incorrectly; exact embedded-versus-MediaStore write semantics are not documented by the FAQ.
Editor offers draggable corners and free, fixed and custom aspect ratios.
Rotate left/right/180 degrees and flip horizontally or vertically in the editing workflow.
Set width/height with aspect preservation or batch-resize selected images by a factor between 10% and 90%; batch resizing appears in 6.26.9.

Proprietary build conditionally includes IMG.LY advanced editor. UI defines exposure, highlights, shadows, clarity, gamma, colour, blur-focus, overlays, text and sticker controls; these must not be attributed to every FOSS build.
Video Trim UI and 6.26.4 merging belong to the Advanced Editor; its SDK is conditional on the proprietary flavour.
Viewer includes a dedicated Share a resized version action rather than requiring full-size transmission.
Set home, lock or both wallpapers with portrait/landscape and adjustable aspect ratios.
Widget settings select the displayed folder and whether to show its name.
UI exposes Show on map and an unknown-location state. An integrated offline basemap or geocoder is not established.
README documents app-level, selected-media and function locks; excluded-folder visibility can also be password protected. Locked folder copies require unlocking in 6.27.1.
Hide creates a removable .nomedia marker recursively; Exclude hides only within Simple Gallery. Hidden access requires All Files permission on affected Android versions.
Deleted items can be restored for 30 days, after which automatic deletion occurs. Restoration falls back to Pictures when the original folder is inaccessible; recent versions allow bypassing the bin.
Version 6.23.8 adds the size of items to be deleted to the confirmation dialog.
FAQ describes up to 250 MB of cache for faster image loading; recycle-bin media adds further application storage.
Settings expose file-loading priority choices including speed, compromise and avoiding invalid files, plus high-quality deep-zoom rendering.
Commands cover query/export/import, batch edits, timewarp, sync/compare, metadata inspection, orphan discovery, library inventories and interactive help/template tools.
PhotosDB, PhotoInfo, QueryOptions, PhotoExporter and comparison objects expose structured metadata and programmable export rather than requiring GUI automation for reads.
macOS supports Photos-app interactions and Python/tool-manager or standalone Intel/Apple Silicon distributions.
Prebuilt macOS binaries do not require a separate Python install, but README warns they are not notarized.
Query, export and Python API can operate on copied Photos libraries on Linux; macOS-specific CLI commands are omitted.
'--library selects among distinct Photos libraries; absent that, uses last-opened or System Photo Library. Compare/sync accepts separate source catalogues.
Limited iPhoto 9.6.1 support includes export/query metadata; v0.78.1 adds iPhoto support to sync --export.
Copies original media out of Photos using original import names by default, with selectable inclusion of related versions/companions.
Defaults to original and edited versions with a configurable edited suffix; can skip edits or export only edited when one exists.
API exposes ordered preview paths and optional preview export/suffix, including derivative stills/video previews when available.
'--export-by-date organizes by capture year/month/day; template directories can choose arbitrary date formats.
folder_album templates reproduce Photos nested albums; multi-album/multi-keyword templates can export multiple copies and filters can restrict chosen hierarchy branches.
Directory/filename templates support defaults, nested conditionals, multi-valued fields and filters; use title, date, place, album, keyword or original name without renaming Photos originals.

SQLite export state enables --update to export only new/changed files. --only-new ignores removed prior exports; --ignore-signature avoids replacing externally edited output merely because file size/mtime differs.

'--download-missing asks Photos via AppleScript or optional PhotoKit to obtain originals before export; requires network and iCloud sync, may restart Photos after crashes, and does not retrieve all burst companions.
Exporter supports creating hardlinks instead of copies. These share the underlying file and are not an independent backup.
Exports associated RAW and JPEG components with skip controls; import groups paired assets on macOS 11+ and API distinguishes RAW-as-original from standalone RAW.
Exports still plus live video and imports recognized pairs together on macOS 11+; optional auto-live creates pairing metadata for same-basename non-Apple pairs, modifying inputs.
Default export includes burst photos unless skipped; macOS 11+ import groups burst members, unlike older versions. Missing iCloud bursts remain a documented limitation.
Export AAE adjustment files and re-import with original/edited companions to preserve non-destructive edits when Photos naming conventions match; unmatched edits become separate assets.
Convert non-JPEG images such as RAW/HEIC to JPEG with quality 0–1 and extension normalization; README says conversion requires a Mac GPU and may fail in VMs.

With separately installed ExifTool, writes Photos keywords, persons, GPS and other metadata into exported files, optionally merging existing keywords/persons and deriving hierarchical tags from albums.
Export XMP or ExifTool-compatible JSON without installing ExifTool; configure extension-dropping and keyword/description templates.
Exporter options control inclusion of location/persons, replacement/merging of keywords and generated metadata; this does not automatically remove every pre-existing embedded field.
Write keywords to Finder tags and template-driven author/comment/copyright/description/headline attributes without altering image bytes.
'--touch-file sets exported file modification time to photo date; separate from changing embedded EXIF or Photos capture time.
Photos 5+ API exposes the EXIF subset cached by Photos; a separately installed ExifTool reader provides complete file metadata when the original is locally available.
Expose names, face/person objects and region metadata from Apple's catalogue. This is not an independent face-recognition engine.
Read normalized labels produced by Photos image categorization and use them in queries or export keyword templates; labels originate from Photos, not a new OSXPhotos classifier.

Photos 5+ ScoreInfo exposes overall, composition, blur/focus, noise and other existing scores; the author explicitly has not fully decoded their semantics. Not claimed as newly computed culling or best-shot inference.
PhotoInfo exposes mediaanalysisd metadata and an AI caption when one exists; OSXPhotos is reading existing analysis, not generating captions itself.
On macOS 10.15+, detected_text runs Vision on edited/original/preview fallback with confidence thresholds and cached results; explicitly distinct from Monterey Live Text.
Query original/media names and match regular expressions against template values such as full folder/album hierarchy.
Search title, description, album/folder, EXIF values, UUID and Photos labels; support query expressions/functions for custom predicates.
Filter capture start/end/year and added-before/after/recent intervals; tutorial also documents time-of-day selection.
Filter photos/movies, UTI, RAW companions, live/burst/HDR/portrait/panorama/screenshot/selfie/slow-motion/time-lapse states.
Query minimum/maximum original size, e.g. select large videos and add them to an album.
Search people identified by Photos and combine them with export/query constraints.
Query repeated keywords and absent-keyword state; export only matching media.
Query Photos reverse-geocoded place names and presence/absence of location/place data; no offline-map UI implied.
Different query options combine as AND; repeated keyword values combine as OR. Regex/template and custom function/expression hooks support more specific selection.
Query missing originals, referenced versus managed, iCloud-managed/synced, hidden, favorite, edited/external-edit, in/no album, deleted and missing descriptive metadata states.
Save and reload export options, including filters/templates, as TOML configuration files for repeatable workflows.

PhotoInfo.duplicates matches original byte size, creation time, height and width—not hashes or byte comparison—and works even with iCloud originals missing. Results are expressly only possible duplicates.
Expose Photos' stored hash of original file for cross-library matching, distinct from the metadata-based duplicates property.
Import files/directories into the most recently opened Photos library, optionally recursively and with glob filtering. Ordinary assets import individually, affecting Photos Imports grouping.

Choose Photos' dialog-based duplicate checks or OSXPhotos --skip-dups. Default matching uses photo fingerprint, but video fallback uses lowercase filename+size; custom signatures compare with library state at import start.
'--dup-albums adds an existing matched asset to the albums skipped import would have created, preserving folder-to-album organization without extra copies.
Import sidecar support recognizes standard and supplemental-metadata.json Takeout names; UTC-only sidecar dates can be ignored to preserve more accurate embedded timezone information.
Read JSON/XMP sidecars or OSXPhotos export database for title, description, keywords, GPS, albums and date/time. XMP parsing needs ExifTool; JSON wins if both sidecar types are found.
Parse strptime-like filename or folder patterns and supply timezone overrides; missing components fall back to Photos' date behavior. Direct named-timezone writes carry an undocumented-database risk.
Album templates and split-folder delimiter create nested Photos folders/albums; multiple target albums and relative-to path templates are supported.
Selected/query-matched assets can receive template titles/captions/keywords, GPS and favorite flags; an open album with no selected photos targets all its photos unless queries are provided.
Batch-edit adds keywords by default with an explicit replacement switch; import can merge rather than overwrite existing keywords.
Batch set/clear favorite; import optionally maps an XMP star-rating threshold to favorite. Native numeric ratings are iPhoto-specific, not Apple Photos ratings.
Batch/import set explicit latitude/longitude; add-locations fills missing GPS using nearby geotagged captures rather than a GPX track.
Find the nearest geotagged photo within a configurable ±time window (default one hour) and copy its location; assumes correct capture times and offers dry run.
Set or offset date/time, parse filenames, assign named IANA/UTC-offset zones and optionally preserve wall-clock time with --match-time; named zones account for DST.
Set date-added independently or copy capture date to added date, useful for removing old scans from Recents without changing their capture timestamp.
With ExifTool compare Photos versus embedded timestamps, collect mismatches in an album, pull metadata into Photos or push it into originals; missing EXIF can fall back to file time.

push-exif uses separately installed ExifTool to write keywords, GPS, face regions/persons, timestamps, titles/descriptions into originals and optionally edits. Compare/dry-run and change tracking reduce repeated writes; this is intentionally destructive to original bytes.

Sync matched assets using original filename/fingerprint from another library/database or exported SQLite metadata. Set overwrites chosen fields; merge preserves/combines them, and album sync only adds memberships.
Compare identifies assets unique to each catalogue and same/different pairs, accepts custom signature functions/templates, outputs CSV/TSV/JSON and offers nonzero-difference exit status.

Compare UUID-named files in originals/renders/derivatives/shared scopes against catalogue IDs including trash and burst members. List candidates or copy them to a destination with collision-safe names; not automatic deletion.
'--cleanup deletes files not in the current export set, including unrelated user files unless protected by .osxphotos_keep/keep rules; dotfiles are excluded. Explicit dry run is recommended.
Batch-edit keeps prior values in a local store and --undo restores last metadata changes, but cannot undo album additions; this is not a general crash-safe file-operation journal.
Timewarp --reset restores original recorded date/time/timezone only on macOS 13+ and only where Photos stored those original values.
Export/import/batch/sync/geotag/push-exif support dry-run paths; import also validates/render-checks templates and checks already-imported versus not-imported files without importing.
API exporter defaults overwrite=false and increment=true; it can instead fail on collision when increment is disabled. Orphan recovery increments names as well.
Import --resume skips files recorded in an import database; export database permits restarting/updating prior exports. Reports are not equivalent to transactional rollback.
'--retry sets export retry attempts for failures such as intermittent NAS connections.
Place export state on a faster local disk or use RAM then flush on completion; RAM mode can improve NAS workloads but loses progress if interrupted.
API documents concurrent export using threads on Python 3.11+; PhotosDB cannot be pickled for multiprocessing. This is an API/example capability, not a claimed default CLI speedup.
Export/import/sync/push-exif reports support CSV/JSON/SQLite outcomes including new/updated/skipped/missing/errors; import/sync can append reports. These logs are not crash-recovery journals.

Export executes template-based commands by output category; import can call configured Python post-functions, and timewarp accepts a custom timestamp function. External scripts are user-controlled executable integrations.
CLI provides inspect, UUID, show, REPL and interactive template commands for exploring selected Photos items and developing repeatable workflows.

Release 1.14.2 explicitly updates translations, and the Android app manifest enables right-to-left layout support. The inspected sources establish localized UI but do not provide a verified complete language/completeness matrix.
Distributed through Android stores/repos and GitHub; registers as image/video viewer, picker and editor.
Reads device folders/MediaStore with manual inclusion for missing folders; permissions and Android version restrict hidden/path access.
Folder or all-content views, grouped direct subfolders, pinned/default folders and custom drag order are documented.
Grid/list layout with configurable column count, horizontal/vertical scrolling, square/rounded thumbnails, spacing, filenames and folder counts.
Group by capture date or last modification daily/monthly; also by folder, media type or extension. Grouping and sorting are independent.
Options include hidden system UI, black background, brightness, keep-screen-on, extended details and configurable bottom actions.
Settings offer deep zoom/highest quality, one-finger zoom, two-double-tap 1:1 zoom and video double-tap zoom.
Side taps change media, down gesture closes viewer, vertical gestures adjust photo brightness or video volume/brightness, and video supports horizontal seeking.
Choose interval, photos/videos/GIF inclusion, random or reverse order, loop and none/fade/slide animation.
Select in-app/default player; autoplay, looping, remembered position, playback speed, seek gestures and durations are exposed.
README lists RAW and UI has a RAW filter; camera-specific decoding coverage is not enumerated.
README explicitly supports JPEG XL and manifest registers .jxl content handling.
AVIF is explicitly listed among supported formats.
SVG is listed in README and filter UI.
GIF filter, animated thumbnails and GIF inclusion in slideshows are user options.
In-app setting explicitly enables showing Ultra HDR photos in HDR; device/version support is not fully specified by this source.
SearchActivity performs case-insensitive name containment across fetched visible media and prioritizes names starting with the query; not semantic or metadata search.
Filters include images, videos, GIFs, RAW, SVG and portraits.
Sort by name or full path, optionally numeric/natural value, ascending/descending; preferences can be global or per-folder.
Size ordering appears alongside filename, dates, random, folder count and custom folder order.
Sort by Date Taken or last modified independently of grouping, with ascending/descending and folder-specific settings.
One selected item uses RenameItemDialog; multiple items use RenameDialog. Android 11 SD/OTG root rename needs all-files access.
Invokes file destination workflow, rescans source/destination, fixes date values and updates favorite paths on moves; moving directly from recycle-bin paths is blocked.
Batch add/remove favorites, display favorite marks and maintain favorite paths after moving files.
Settings expose favorite path import/export; export selects a .txt destination and confirms overwriting an existing file. This is not a full database/photo backup.
Selected-media action repairs Date Taken used for ordering, especially after copying; source calls fixDateTaken rather than establishing arbitrary EXIF timestamp editing.
README explicitly offers stripping sensitive EXIF including GPS and camera details; exact field-by-field scope is not documented.
Basic editor crops by dragging corners and supports fixed/free/custom aspect ratios.
Editor offers horizontal/vertical flips; media selection routes support 90/180/270-degree rotations.
Resize dimensions with aspect-ratio lock or batch scale factor between 10% and 90%; settings also advertise sharing a resized version.
README explicitly includes drawing and image filters in the basic editor; no professional RAW processing is implied.

Save-as dialog chooses directory, basename and extension, optionally adds _1, validates names and asks before overwrite. Also exposes overwrite-original option, so edits are not universally nondestructive.
SaveAsDialog calls ensureWritablePath with confirmOverwrite=true; favorite-text export also explicitly prompts on collision.
Deleted photos/videos can be restored. FAQ says bin contents count toward app storage and automatically expire after 30 days; deletion can explicitly bypass bin.
Delete dialog shows item count/size and bin-versus-permanent action; user can remember skip-confirmation or bypass bin. Password-protected deletion is a separate path.
README advertises locking media or app; FAQ permits reset via reinstall/clear data without media removal, so not an encrypted vault guarantee.
Hide recursively creates .nomedia affecting other galleries; Exclude hides only within Fossify. Included folders override recursive exclusions; Android permissions can restrict both.
FAQ documents up to 250 MB app cache for quicker image loading, separately from recycle-bin storage.
Search loads cached media into its adapter before starting asynchronous media fetch and stops the current fetch when destroyed/replaced.
Dynamic Material themes and custom themes, launcher colors, bottom action visibility and thumbnail styling are documented.
Single and multiple selections route through Android media-sharing helpers; not a hosted public-link service.
Manifest registers PICK/GET_CONTENT for image/video, VIEW, photo EDIT/CROP and camera review intents.
Set a photo as home-screen, lock-screen or both wallpapers, with aspect-ratio controls; manifest registers wallpaper activities and SET_WALLPAPER permission.
Widget settings select the displayed folder and whether to show its name; manifest registers the widget configuration activity and app-widget provider.
README defines Piwigo as a photo gallery for the web; official manuals document its browser gallery and online administration panel.
README explicitly offers a Docker installation guide for the self-hosted web server; Docker availability does not establish a native Windows/macOS gallery application.
Official feature overview links a separate Piwigo Android mobile app for uploading phone photos to the server; it is a companion, not part of the PHP browser UI.
Official sources document the separate iOS upload app, including converting MOV videos to MP4 during transfer; mobile companion availability is distinct from the server's web deployment.

Official manual documents over 70 interface languages. Administrators enable/disable languages and select the default; users choose a saved personal language that immediately translates menus/buttons. Database titles/descriptions are not automatically translated.
Language Switch adds a flag selector for one-click switching among enabled gallery languages; base per-user language preference works without this convenience plugin.

Extended Descriptions provides manually authored photo/album title and description variants selected by visitor language, with default/all-language fallbacks. This is separate from translating UI and is not automatic machine translation.
Exif View translates displayed EXIF values into the gallery language; it does not rewrite the photo's underlying metadata into a different language.
PHP web application with MySQL/MariaDB and GD or recommended ImageMagick; README links manual and Docker installation.
Separate hosted offering supplies operated infrastructure, backups and standby replication; advanced features differ by Team/Enterprise/VIP plan.
Web administration uploads media; official overview also lists external clients such as digiKam, Lightroom and Shotwell, which are companion integrations rather than built-in editors.
Separate mobile apps send photos to the server; cited overview establishes upload, not unrestricted automatic background camera-roll backup.
Self-hosted galleries scan the galleries directory to create albums at arbitrary nesting depth; database sync is required after filesystem changes. Cloud does not offer this method.
Synchronize directories only or directories+files, optionally restrict to an album/subtree, include previously synced metadata or overwrite with empty values.
Simulation-only mode reports prospective filesystem/database synchronization without applying changes; distinct from a general undo journal.
Place one file in several albums without duplicated storage, select representative images and customize ordering.
Albums/sub-albums can be nested and independently public/private; folder-backed albums have more restrictive physical rename/move workflows.

SmartAlbums combines all/any criteria including tags, dates, source album, name, dimensions, author and view counts. Defaults to three-day refresh, with manual or after-upload regeneration; not real-time by default. Cloud requires Enterprise+.
User Collections lets logged-in users maintain unlimited selections separate from albums; admins search/edit/export collections as CSV. Cloud Enterprise+.
Assign existing/new tags singly or in batch, combine tags for navigation and optionally map incoming metadata into keywords.
Editable title/author/description properties accompany optional photo-page comments; visual rich-text editing and multilingual descriptions use FCKEditor/Extended Description plugins.
Official overview includes file rating as a collaboration mechanism; numeric scale details were not established here.
Photo-page heart saves favorites, browsable from Explore/Discover and available as a batch-manager prefilter.
Imports technical metadata; default display includes camera make/model, capture time and aperture, with configurable additional fields and ability to hide EXIF.
Supports IPTC field mapping into author/title/description/keywords; IPTC display is not enabled by default and requires configuration.
Write Metadata writes title, description, authors and tags back into file IPTC; normal property changes are catalogue edits. Cloud Team+.

Batch manager filters then offers whole-page/set/invert/none selection and bulk delete, album association/move/dissociation, tags, author/title/date/privacy and metadata/derivative regeneration; single mode edits per-item values.
Administrators add individual photos or whole albums to a persistent caddie while browsing, then manage that set through batch manager.
Creation date can be edited/unset individually or set in batches; changing upload/post date instead requires Posted Date Changer.
Manage Properties Photos adds text/select/radio/date/EXIF/IPTC-derived properties, ordering/visibility and batch edits; Properties Mass Update adds CSV changes. Cloud Enterprise+.
Copyrights defines selectable rights; Expiry Date can leave, archive or delete expiring files and notify downloaders/admins before/on expiry. Expiry Date is Cloud Enterprise+.
Quick search covers title, filename, description, tags and photo ID; matching albums/tags appear as navigation results. Users can choose searched fields and all/any words.
Filter on all or any selected tags, combine with albums/authors, and search inside an existing album or tag selection.
Preset and custom year/month/day ranges have result counts; capture and post dates are independent filters.
Multi-criteria bar includes file type, uploader and author alongside album/tag criteria.
Width/height bounds and portrait/square/landscape/panorama ratios are available in gallery and batch filtering.
Size sliders restrict selection and combine with other criteria; gallery remembers visible filter controls per user, not a documented saved query library.
Raw displayed EXIF/IPTC is not searchable by default; configuration can map metadata such as camera model to tags/properties for filtering.
Color Palette extracts a configurable number of colors and finds images sharing selected colors. Palettes are lazily generated when photos are viewed, so initial coverage is incomplete.
Pinned batch-manager source supports md5sum matching alongside filename/date/dimension options and excludes null checksums; this goes beyond the manual's older name-only description.
Duplicate prefilter can group matching filenames, capture dates and dimensions, independently or together with checksums; these are not perceptual or necessarily exact duplicates.
Batch results default to 20 files with 50/100/all options and page controls.
Photo toolbar starts fullscreen slideshow over current album/tag/search selection, rather than always using the entire library.
Loupe adds hover magnification with mouse-wheel zoom; availability is explicitly an installed plugin.
Stores originals and generates configured square/thumbnail/medium and optional sizes on request, with editable dimensions/quality; batch manager can delete/regenerate derivatives.
Center-of-interest tool marks the important region to retain in square/other cropped derivatives; this is not a full destructive original-image editor.
Configuration selects a custom watermark image and position, commonly transparent PNG, for gallery presentation.
Rotate Image adds a Rotate tab to the photo editor.
Photo Update replaces an original or a non-image representative thumbnail while retaining catalogue properties.
Since v14 supports HEIC with generated browser-compatible preview; self-hosting must enable all-type upload/extensions and have supporting server codecs.
GIF originals animate while thumbnails can use the first frame; WebP support dates to v14 and may require config/server updates, especially animation.

VideoJS required on self-hosted servers, preactivated in Cloud; listed formats include MP4/M4V/WebM/OGG and configurable player preload/autoplay/loop/style. Uploaded MOV is not generally browser-playable.
VideoJS also exposes audio playback (including MP3) represented by an icon rather than a video frame.
enable_formats plus format_ext associates files such as CR2, CMYK JPEG or ZIP in pwg_format with one image. Cloud offers this from Enterprise; storing RAW companions does not prove RAW decoding.

Configured PDF/SVG/EPS/TIFF/PSD/AI types can have generated previews; v15 adds an inline PDF reader. Other office formats may be downloadable only with generic icons. Cloud premium formats require Team+.
Panoramas selects special viewing using configurable filename markers, default _180 or _360.
Back2Front links a reverse-side photo to a front ID, can hide the back from album listings and exposes See back in the viewer.
Official feature overview documents unlimited user accounts and permission assignment per user or group. Accounts are not separate user-selectable catalogues.
Public/private albums, user/group access and independent Everybody/Contacts/Friends/Family/Admin image privacy levels combine; original download rights are separately controllable.

Community grants selected users/groups upload destinations/subtree access, album creation and photo/storage quotas. Low-trust uploads require approval; contributors manage their own pending photos/tags. Cloud Team+.
Community can permit any visitor, including anonymous users, with low/high trust, per-user limits and administrator approval notifications.
Private Share generates scoped photo URLs and emails them without granting general gallery access; User Collections separately shares personal selections. Ordinary public galleries remain core.
User Collections permits a password on generated public collection links; Cloud Enterprise+.
User Collections has expiry dates; Private Share offers 1/2 weeks or 1/3 months and admin history/revocation controls.
Photo download returns original by default if user has Download permission; toolbar can be hidden and viewer sizes restricted.
Download by Size adds size selection to the download action using configured derivatives.
Embedded Videos imports URLs or embed code from YouTube/Vimeo/Dailymotion and others, with optional title/tag extraction and player settings; playback depends on those external services.
Social Buttons (or Bootstrap Darkroom theme) offers platform sharing; docs warn disabling light mode introduces platform tracking cookies.
Repository advertises extension ecosystem; manuals name function-specific plugins, and release upgrade tool warns about version incompatibilities.
Official overview exposes API/script integrations; v16.4 fixes API-key token handling and original-protected URL responses. Lightroom/WordPress/auth providers require companion connectors.
Official overview describes day/month/year visit graphs, activity search and upload/edit/delete logs. These are audit analytics, not rollback-capable file journals.
Official feature page advertises map display and manual coordinates but inspected implementation-specific manuals do not settle plugin/edition/provider requirements.
Official page advertises tagging through Piwigo-operated AI and separately mentions Imagga/Azure integrations; repository-core availability and entitlement are not established.
Official feature page advertises editable AI descriptions but does not clarify whether this is a Cloud entitlement or self-hostable module.
OCR is advertised alongside AI indexing with insufficient deployment/edition detail to count as core.
Official feature page explicitly says face recognition is coming soon.

GUI dynamically discovers bundled locale JSON files and reloads strings when CurrentLanguage changes; French menus, dialogs and result columns are explicitly translated. Default/load-failure fallback is English, while missing individual keys display the key. Localization parity for CLI/web is not inferred.
Finds related video content despite different resolution/frame rate and watermarks using sampled visual similarity rather than byte equality.
Image scanning is supported alongside videos; CLI --include-images is off by default, while the core settings default includes images.

Choose grayscale percentage-difference or pHash, or combine both so either match qualifies. Controls include hash-difference threshold, minimum similarity and required fraction of matching sampled pHash frames.
Core settings expose horizontal-flip comparison and ignoring black/white pixels, distinct from optional neural transformed-copy detection.

A second phase uses chroma fingerprints and sliding-window Hamming similarity to find shorter clips within longer sources, reports a Clip Offset and defaults to visual confirmation at the offset. Both files need audio.
Audio clip mode defaults to minimum 10% clip/source duration, 80% audio similarity and 85% frame confirmation; the confirmation requirement is independently configurable.

DINOv2 embeddings via ONNX add matches for cropped, mirrored, zoomed, letterboxed or heavily edited copies; classic results remain authoritative and are never hidden by enabling AI. Default threshold is 94%.

Independent AI partial-detection switch compares dense keyframes by a consistent time offset; at least four hits must agree, default frame threshold 89%. Works without audio, including muted/re-dubbed clips.
ONNX runtime/model download is about 100 MB once; model is checked against pinned SHA256. GUI asks before download; enabled CLI/web/Docker auto-download. No content is sent to a cloud AI account.
Stores fingerprints for fast rescanning; optional embeddings are cached at roughly 2 KB/file, with dense keyframes in a separately cleaned sidecar at a claimed 25 KB/video.

Optional RememberDeletedContent retains fingerprints when the last copy is deleted, so re-downloaded content can be recognized; database cleanup becomes tombstone-aware. This is not a general reviewed-pair ignore list.
Settings can scan against the entire database and include non-existing files; tombstone mode also enables missing-file comparison.
CLI accepts repeatable include directories and core settings control recursive scanning.
Exclude directories, apply contains/not-contains path filters and optionally ignore read-only folders, reparse points or existing hard links.
Core scan settings expose enabled minimum/maximum file-size filtering.
FolderMatchMode permits unrestricted, same-folder-only or different-folder-only matching with configurable same-folder depth.
Configure percentage duration tolerance with minimum/maximum seconds bounds; with percentage disabled, seconds-only tolerance is supported. Maximum sampled duration is also configurable.

CLI can retain highest bitrate/resolution, largest file, longest duration or highest resolution per group. A 100-percent-only strategy acts only on fully matching reported groups; that label is not independently proven byte equality.
CLI action workflow defaults to dry-run and explicitly recommends reviewing before automatic deletion.
CLI --delete moves selected duplicates to trash; permanent deletion requires the distinct --delete-permanent option. Platform/container trash availability is not fully detailed.
CLI writes selected text, JSON or CSV output to stdout or a named file and can load comprehensive JSON settings.
GUI path search is case-insensitive substring matching or unanchored * and ? wildcards; matching a member preserves the surrounding duplicate group.
GUI filters results to all, videos or images.
Result filters support minimum/maximum similarity and groups with checked items.
An AI filter retains groups containing an AI-only accepted member along with its comparison context; it is not an AI-only rescan.
Can hide groups with at most one remaining existing member; files on disconnected drives still count as offline rather than deleted.
Core settings expose generation of preview thumbnails with count and maximum width, supporting visual inspection of similarity results.
Separate read/hashing and CPU matching limits; slow/network drives default to a low per-drive cap while SSDs share the global budget. Automatic drive classification can be overridden.
Automatic checkpoint interval defaults to five minutes; zero disables interval saves but retains phase-boundary saves. This is not a file-operation undo journal.
Can call FFmpeg functions natively for claimed speed improvement; requires compatible FFmpeg 8.x shared libraries rather than master builds.
Separate scan/compare and combined CLI workflows are suitable for scripts and scheduled jobs without a display.
Self-contained web server supports headless/NAS access, configurable listening port, generated or configured password and optional 30-day remember-me cookie.
Web image bundles FFmpeg, supports amd64/arm64 and separates persistent settings/database from mounted media; numbered tags avoid rolling latest.
Documented Docker examples and guidance recommend :ro media mounts for scan-only safety; deletion needs a writable configuration.
All documented comparison occurs on the scanning machine, with optional model/runtime downloads but no cloud content-analysis service.

Release history explicitly adds localization with many languages from v2.0 and later localized metadata dates; README links the application's Transifex translation workflow. Separate from optional multilingual Lens queries.
Install through Nextcloud's app store, configure the admin panel and index existing files; not a standalone service independent of Nextcloud.
Browser UI works on desktop and Android/iOS with touch layouts; a native iOS Memories binary is not claimed.
Available through Google Play, F-Droid and separate GitHub Android releases; latest notes add mTLS client certificates and optional HDR disable.

Hardware-transcoding guide provides a separate radialapps/go-vod Docker service alongside Nextcloud; current-source Lens setup provides Docker Compose for its daemon and Qdrant. These are optional companions, not evidence that Memories is a standalone photo-server image independent of Nextcloud.
Uses existing files and their metadata without requiring a second proprietary original store; folder hierarchy remains intact.
Configure multiple timeline paths and recursively include mounted volumes/shares within them; this is one user's scope, not separate catalogues.
Flat date display is layered on the unchanged directory hierarchy, with optional folder browsing.
Background jobs and immediate upload hooks index new/changed files. External modifications may need Nextcloud files:scan first; rerunning memories:index is incremental unless forced.
Direct web upload, Android destination-folder upload and selected local photo uploads are documented in release history.
README directs automatic camera/photo/video upload to official Nextcloud Android/iOS apps rather than attributing background backup to Memories itself.
OCC command copies Takeout JSON into EXIF, optionally overriding existing fields and scoped by user/folder; it modifies source files and documentation requires backups.
Move from timeline to folders and, since 7.5.1, copy rather than move; copying triggers immediate indexing in later releases.
Move-to-folder workflow can organize selected files by year and month.
Archive moves photos to .archive at timeline/storage root, which may be mounted to cold storage; this is a filesystem move, not just hiding.
Supports .nomedia, app-specific .nomemories, hidden folders/files, regex filename/folder patterns and MIME blocklist; v11.1.1 fixes name-blocklist application to files.
Individual and whole album/public album/folder downloads are documented; v10 adds resumable file downloads.
Sort photos/videos by capture date with a scrubber and #day/yyyy-mm-dd links; memories can jump to the corresponding day.
Uses EXIF date rather than filesystem modification time; GPS can supply timezone information when camera EXIF lacks it.
Official feature explanation explicitly identifies infinite virtual scrolling plus random-access date scrubber; no benchmark is inferred.
Choose folder-view root, use breadcrumbs, optionally show a recursive timeline, and browse folders within shares.
Past photos appear in an On this day view and optionally at the top of the timeline, with age and direct-day navigation.
Select entire days, shift-click or touch-drag, pinch/scroll zoom and swipe-to-refresh; later releases preserve navigation scroll position.
Fullscreen viewing includes Shift+F keyboard shortcut and photo deep links.
Full image can load upon zoom with configurable administrator defaults; desktop mouse wheel and newer video zoom are supported.
Slideshow supports photos and videos with optional metadata display.
v10 introduces interactive PhotoSphere panorama viewing; not a generic inference from a 2:1 image.
Browser-supported codecs play directly; optional HLS transcoding handles other formats, with quality selection/fallback and user/admin autoplay controls.
go-vod generates thumbnail sprites/VTT storyboards for video hover previews, cached persistently with keyframes.
Current VIPS provider supports RAW out of the box and can be disabled. Older camera-raw-preview app is a fallback, not a current mandatory dependency.
Bundled VIPS handles HEIC/HEIF with no extra image dependency when enabled; older provider fallback requires ImageMagick support.
VIPS decodes AVIF; old files may require MIME repair and reindexing after upgrade. Editor also offers AVIF output.
v11 VIPS decoder supports Ultra-HDR/Samsung HDR and ICC profiles; Android offers HDR-display disable.
Paired live-photo viewing, autoplay/loop settings and editing via a separate copy; earlier JPEG-only limitations are superseded by later HEVC/HEIC handling.
Release history documents Google MVIMG, Samsung HEIC Motion Photos and Huawei Moving Picture.
Can hide/stack RAWs beside another same-basename file; current releases support metadata edits of stacked JPEG+RAW pairs.
Bundled ExifTool extracts photo/video capture and technical metadata, displayed in sidebar and used for timeline/maps.
Supports changing EXIF dates, title/description and GPS; RAW metadata editing is added in v11. These are source-file edits, not a default read-only catalogue.
Bulk date/other EXIF edits and collaborative tags; lossless bulk rotation writes orientation metadata rather than re-encoding pixels.
Edit EXIF date individually/in bulk, with a warning when a metadata edit would lose the date.
GPS editing supports precise coordinates and a configurable location-search provider.
Edit/create collaborative tags individually or in bulk and show tags in sidebar; existing Nextcloud tags carry over.
Select and favourite/unfavourite files, with a dedicated Favorites view.
Create albums of photos/videos, add to multiple albums, choose covers and sort lists; configuration explicitly requires the Nextcloud Photos app for album support.
People grouping comes from Recognize or alternative Face Recognition app, with face thumbnails in sidebar and selectable person covers.
Uses separately installed Nextcloud Recognize or Face Recognition; alternative Face Recognition integration is described as alpha with extra fine-tuning.
Release history documents naming/renaming Recognize face groups rather than merely face detection.
Merge face clusters, move photos between people, move unclustered faces and create a new cluster while moving; version requirements belong to Recognize.
Object/tag grouping is provided by Recognize rather than a built-in mandatory AI engine.
v7.1 introduces basic search and album-picker/face-merge dialogs have search. Exact full-library query grammar is not established by these docs.

Current-source Lens guide describes multilingual image description search after indexing, requiring a dedicated non-admin service account, separate daemon and Qdrant. Packaged release parity remains unverified.

Lens caches a pinned model snapshot and runs normalized image/text embeddings locally in its daemon, on CPU or CUDA. Initial model provisioning accesses Hugging Face unless complete offline cache exists.
Lens embedding backend selects CUDA when configured/available, with Float16 there and Float32 CPU fallback.

De-duplicate identical files setting collapses matching AUID entries and retains hidden copies for bulk actions. Missing AUID is derived from MD5(timestamp plus file size), not file bytes; this is presentation deduplication, not verified exact-content cleanup.
GPS-tagged photo map, configurable tile server, high-precision marker setting and Android local-photo geolocation; no bundled offline basemap established.
Download/import planet database into MySQL/MariaDB/PostgreSQL for server-side place lookup; can supply a custom planet ZIP. Map tiles remain an independent feature.
Places hierarchy and a filter for files without location, with configurable place covers; named places depend on geocoder setup.
Uses Nextcloud user/auth ecosystem rather than reimplementing accounts; README and FAQ explicitly support multiple users.
Share individual or selected media and folders externally; album shares use Photos dependency and can be shared with Nextcloud users/groups or public links.
Password-protected folder shares and fixes for password link shares are explicitly documented.
v7.8 adds upload to public shares; v9 fixes video uploads there. Availability still follows the underlying share permissions.
Share at high/low resolution, use native share interface, and transcode shared videos to smaller outputs.
Current VIPS editor offers free/original/fixed aspect ratios and straightening from −45° to +45° in half-degree steps.
Editor state supports rotation and horizontal/vertical flips; separate bulk rotation updates EXIF losslessly.
Brightness, exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, saturation, vibrance, hue, temperature, blur, sharpen and vignette, plus warm/cool/monochrome/negative presets.
Save dialog offers JPEG/PNG/AVIF, with 90/85/75 quality presets for lossy output and lossless PNG.
Choose copy versus explicit overwrite; Live Photos always create copies and format changes force copy mode. This is save-as safety, not a full reversible edit recipe.
go-vod adapts resolution to connection speed, supports quality selection and direct HLS-fMP4 streaming of HEVC/AV1/VP9. Disabled by default; CPU fallback without hardware.
Intel QuickSync/compatible VA-API and NVIDIA NVENC require device/drivers/FFmpeg; newer NVENC uses Jellyfin GPU HDR tone mapping.
Deploy separate go-vod containers/hosts and list several addresses for load distribution with per-client sticky routing; supports external/object storage with documented setup.
Preview derivatives and optimized loading reduce repeated work; optional Preview Generator app pre-generates previews. Sizes/quality are configurable and may otherwise exceed compact originals.
Run multiple memories:index processes concurrently; can scope to user/group/path to avoid full-library work.
CLI supports retry failed entries, forced refresh or clear/reindex; UI supports Refresh Metadata on selected photos and lists failures in admin settings.
v10.2 adds a Trash view for restoring or permanently deleting photos within the Nextcloud-backed application; retention is not specified here.
Viewer deletion confirmation exists; v11 allows opting out. Metadata editor warns when a date would be lost.
Release history documents support for server-side encrypted storage. Encryption is supplied/configured by Nextcloud, and server-side readable originals are not E2EE.
Release history documents basic offline support through cache, not a complete offline original-library replica.
Index, reverse-geocoder setup and Takeout migration are documented command-line actions; deprecated OCCWeb is explicitly incompatible.

Setting language=1 loads the bundled jquery.s2t script and converts page elements to Traditional Chinese. This is a built-in Chinese-script conversion option; English or a broader translated UI catalogue is not established by this evidence.
PHP application does not require a database; README recommends Linux with Nginx and lists required PHP extensions.
HTML5 desktop/mobile upload UI returns reusable links; README retains legacy-browser fallback language.
Project documentation links DDS-Derek/EasyImage-Docker rather than establishing an official core image.
Upload queue supports multiple files and HTML5 drag-and-drop; defaults configure 30 files per upload and 10 MiB per file, adjustable subject to PHP limits.
chunks configuration enables split uploads; release 2.8.7 fixes large-file chunk merging into the wrong directory.
Default storage root is /i/ with year/month/day folders; configuration warns changing that structure can impair operations.
Separate upload-user, administrator and token-ID directories; the public square excludes those separated uploads and lists guest uploads only.
Guest hosting is a primary scenario; mustLogin switches to authenticated-only uploads, with optional daily counts and IP restrictions.
Create accounts restricted to uploading while administrative file/configuration operations require admin identity; this is not a full collaborative account system.
Configure daily uploads, per-upload count/size, allowed extensions and minimum/maximum pixel dimensions.
Upload IP blacklists/whitelists are supported; trusted_proxy configuration added with fixes to prevent spoofed forwarding headers bypassing limits.
Return direct URL, Markdown, BBCode and HTML links with copying; API also supplies thumbnail and deletion links.
Enable API uploads and POST multipart image plus token. Response includes original filename, URL, thumbnail, deletion link and token ID; optional token-ID filename suffix is documented in 2.8.7.
Separate PicGo web-uploader plugin maps image/token fields and the response URL after enabling API upload.

Configuration includes remote FTP host, port, passive/SSL mode, local-after-transfer deletion and synchronized remote deletion; deletion controller invokes the FTP delete hook. End-to-end transfer behavior was not runtime-tested.
Add extensions such as MP4, PDF or MP3 and disable image-only mode to upload other types. This does not establish a video/audio playback library.
Set image quality/compression and image-size reduction; configuration also offers a separate TinyPNG service key.
Configure target width/height, ratio, crop and quality settings for uploaded image transformations.
Convert uploaded images to a specified format, subject to server image-library support.
Configure text/image watermark, position, font, size and color.
Thumbnail generation has configurable dimensions and is exposed by the upload API; 2.8.7 fixes thumbnail/backend compression behavior.
Online gallery/administration and per-image information are documented; optional user/token/admin directory separation changes what appears publicly.
Default site configuration exposes dark-mode and theme settings.
show_exif_info configuration controls image information display; no embedded-metadata editing workflow is established.
Enable configured ModerateContent key and moderation mode to classify uploads. The manual's registration instructions were not validated against current provider availability.
Can deploy an nsfwjs REST container or compatible endpoint returning Drawing/Hentai/Neutral/Porn/Sexy probabilities; this is a separate service, not in-process local inference.
With image_recycl enabled, capability-link deletes move files to recycle storage. Admin supports recycle, restore and permanent deletion, including bulk actions.
Administrative suspic_reimg action restores files from the suspect-image area independently of the ordinary recycle area.

API returns an authorized deletion link usable without admin login. Version 2.8.7 redesigns capability tokens with authenticated encryption and separate delete/hide purposes; this encrypts tokens, not stored pictures.
Bulk deletion reports complete success, partial failure or total failure and returns failed paths instead of always claiming success.
Configurable source protection uses keyed links; 2.8.7 changes token/key handling and invalidates old links. FAQ warns web-server image caching can cause 404 behavior.
Bind an image domain directly to the image root to hide /i/ in returned paths; it must differ from the site domain for this mode.
Website charts/statistics are documented; optional public API can expose selected daily/monthly file counts, folders and used/free/total storage data.
Upload logs support uploader IP geolocation; release updates ip2region data and removes password/hash material from login logs.
2.8.7 caches/iterates square file counts, general file counting and version checks to avoid recursive full-directory scans on every request; not a measured benchmark.
Admin controller supports resetting PHP OPcache when available and deleting cached version information.
Site title/description, notices, custom code, header/footer advertisements and footer content are configurable.

README identifies PicHoro as the separate Android mobile client, and the sync guide documents transferring configuration to it by QR code. This is a companion project, not an Android build of the PicList Electron desktop application.

PicList-Core supplies the separately usable CLI, including an interactive terminal interface, setup wizard and named upload/configuration choices described in the release notes. The Electron desktop repository is not itself a standalone CLI distribution; Core requires its documented Node.js runtime.

Official configuration guide lets users choose language in System settings; v3.6.1 fixes stale interface text after switching languages. Complete language coverage is not enumerated in these inspected sources.
Release offers x64/ARM64 installers and ZIP/7z portable builds; README also lists winget/Scoop.
Intel and Apple Silicon DMG/ZIP releases; menu-bar/main-window behavior documented.
AppImage, deb, rpm and snap release artifacts; clipboard behavior varies under Linux/WSL/headless sessions.
PORTABLE marker beside executable selects adjacent data directory instead of Electron user-data location.
Drag/drop, multi-file selection, clipboard images, absolute paths and file URLs upload to chosen named configuration; arbitrary files depend on provider size/type restrictions.
Downloads one direct HTTP(S) image URL per line and uploads to destination; explicitly not webpage screenshot capture.
Optional monitoring uploads newly copied images automatically, including temporary screenshots; docs warn about online destination exposure.
Can reuse primary processed bytes or independently process original input using secondary settings. Errors are separate and identical configuration can be skipped; not a backfill of earlier uploads.
Maintain multiple accounts/configurations per provider; setting default is separate from saving, and up to six favorites enable quick switching.
Upload/deletion/management support includes S3/R2/MinIO, OSS, COS, Qiniu and Upyun; Doge Cloud management uses the S3 client. Requires service credentials.
WebDAV supports upload, remote gallery deletion and cloud management; credentials and serving URLs remain separate from loopback previews.
