Built-in local destination supports upload, destination-file deletion and file management. Core release notes describe writing to a temporary file before replacing the local destination to reduce incomplete output after interruption.

Configured SFTP destination supports upload, remote gallery deletion and cloud file management. Core release notes describe temporary-file writes before replacement and recursive folder downloads; network credentials and remote-file metadata are required for relevant operations.

GitHub, S.EE and Imgur have management/deletion clients; Lsky, Alist and other PicList servers have upload/deletion but no dedicated management client. Huawei OBS deletion depends on corresponding uploader records.
Cloud manager selects account/bucket/repository/root and lists objects uploaded from any device, unlike machine-local gallery history.
Thumbnail or row views, adjustable grid size, range selection, selected counts and per-file info.

First/previous/next/last/jump navigation loads missing pages; + means unknown total. Newest scans all folder pages with cancellation; normal search/sort are page-scoped, and search stays page-scoped after newest scan.
Gallery searches partial names or URL domain/path; cloud search scope is current page, not necessarily every remote file.
Gallery filter controls narrow records by provider/date and sort order; history defaults newest first.
Copy Markdown/HTML/URL/UBB/custom links individually or in batches; gallery supports url/name/extension placeholders, cloud per-bucket templates also object path/directory.
Long/short URL output is available but shortening requires a configured service; generated names or shortened URLs do not add privacy.
Cloud workflows support private temporary signed addresses and batch copying; expiration and accessibility depend on provider, not a PicList hosted share database.
Select/filter records, inspect pattern-based before/after matches and final plan before applying. This edits history only, not remote filenames or published Markdown documents.
Cloud batch renaming/moving provides preview, conflict policies and failed-item retry; provider may implement rename via copy-then-delete and require both permissions.
Downloads selected remote files/folders to chosen local path; transfer list supports pause/resume/cancel and per-item outcomes, with provider-specific paging constraints.
Delete from Cloud toggle decides whether gallery removal also deletes destination files. Adapters need stored uploader IDs, credentials and remote metadata; failed remote operations are reported.
Named configuration overrides provider overrides global defaults, including explicit disabled switches. Effective settings show value sources and can revert to inherited values.
Quality presets/slider apply during upload; docs explicitly warn quality percentages are not guaranteed size savings and PNG may not shrink much.
Zero dimension preserves proportional sizing; percentage mode takes precedence over fixed dimensions, and small-image enlargement can be disabled.
Processing supports rotation and flips; these and later plugins may change final dimensions.
Preserve source format or choose output with per-input-extension rules. Bypass extensions upload without processing; preview support does not establish encoder availability.
Text uses local/custom font, size/color/margins/position; image watermark supports scale/opacity/placement and full-image repeated coverage. Missing default-font download can skip watermark.
Release specifically documents EXIF removal compatibility fixes for HEIF; complete preserved/removed field matrix is not established.
Patterns support original basename, date/time/milliseconds, UUID/ULID, random fragments, MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256 and trailing local directories; extension is appended and nested paths depend on provider.
Queue has pending/completed/failed states, reorder/priority, filename filtering, interval 0.1–99999 seconds, up to 10 auto retries, optional auto-start and pause-on-error.
taskQueue.json persists state and identifies interrupted work; resume uses current default destination at execution time and requires original source paths.
Pause lets active file finish; cancel stops relevant pending work but does not remove delivered files. Cloud requests are cancelled when switching folders/accounts to avoid stale results.
Records remote completion separately from gallery/success-script finalization. Retrying original task uses persisted finalization data and API finalizationId rather than uploading again.
Documented backup closes app then copies configs, gallery DB, queue/recovery data and scripts; actual destination objects and outside fonts/dependencies need separate backup.
Upload/download common settings, management settings or all configs using selected private Git/WebDAV target; direction can overwrite current defaults and contains credentials.
Plans additions/updates/deletions/conflicts and supports local, remote or both conflict choices with exported summary; transfers records, never all cloud objects.
Sync snapshots allow local rollback on failure with retention, size display, export/deletion and active-use protection. Cannot restore deleted remote objects; not general file-operation undo.
Scroll/+/− zoom, drag pan, reset, arrow navigation and Esc/close are documented.
v3.6 adds SVG image previews; non-image gallery entries use extension icons.
JXL can use generated PNG previews without changing stored original; JXL encoding support is not promised.
Management media preview/playback depends on platform codecs, server response/range support; uploading arbitrary video files alone does not ensure playback.
Management preview supports text/code and audio/media where runtime codecs and remote responses allow; unsupported content can be downloaded externally.
Default endpoint is loopback port 36677/upload, with later port fallback; nonloopback callers need configured key query value, recognized loopback requests receive it automatically.
Typora >=1.6 selects PicList directly; older Typora uses PicGo(app). Obsidian requires Image Auto Upload plugin and VS Code uses VS-PicList extension.
Many PicGo plugins work, not all. System npm is default; experimental bundled npm avoids separate installation but native plugins can still require build tools.

Scripts run at startup/shutdown, preprocess/transform/upload/success/gallery removal or manually; advanced uploader stage can set result URLs. Access includes filesystem/network and local .env values; no separate Node runtime required for scripting.
PicHoro imports uploader configuration by QR code; codes can expose destination credentials and should be transferred privately.
Built-in/custom themes/backgrounds, ThemeHub, mini drag/drop window and tray upload entry points, including Windows tray window in 3.6.
v3.6.1 removes old built-in webpage/web server; HTTP upload API and loopback preview cache are distinct and remain documented.
Docker runs separately maintained PicList-Core upload server; desktop repo has no Dockerfile/Compose and must not be presented as containerized gallery server.
Pinry's tiled pin/board interface is reached through the running instance's web address; browser extensions are separate capture companions.
Official Docker guide runs a user-controlled server with a persistent data volume, database and local settings; alternate database backends can be configured.
README explicitly lists implemented i18n support for English, Simplified Chinese and French in its application feature checklist.
Browser interface presents saved image pins in a skim-friendly tiled board with online preview.
Creates pins from image URLs, optionally preserving referrer; server downloads content, verifies it is an image and creates local image/thumbnail records.
Image creation endpoint accepts uploaded content; pin creation can reference image_by_id instead of fetching a URL.
Pins retain description, source URL and referrer in addition to publication time and submitting user.
Pins have multiple tags; serializer can create missing tags when assigned. Design distinguishes global tag classification from single-owner boards.
Boards have per-owner unique names and many-to-many pin membership, with pin counts and a cover derived from the first pin.
README and API expose tag-name pin filtering plus tag autocomplete; no semantic or image similarity search is established.
Board search uses name; autocomplete and owner-name filters help select boards.
API supports submitter username and board ID filters and lists pins/boards newest-first by ID.
Multiuser application with configurable self-registration; Docker guide describes enabling new registrations in persisted local settings.
Object permission classes allow owner mutations and owner-only access to private pins/boards; list queries filter private records for nonowners and anonymous requests.
Public/private booleans exist independently on pins and boards; public boards support sharing by board. This does not establish password/expiry-link support.
Example configuration has PUBLIC controlling whether pins are viewable without login, separate from per-object private flags.
Image ingestion generates standard, thumbnail and square derivatives; example sizes are 600-wide, 240-wide and cropped 125-square, configurable by IMAGE_SIZES.
User profile supplies a token; DRF exposes interactive API plus pin/board creation/editing and image upload. Board add/remove ID lists are capped at ten per update.
Official docs link a separately maintained browser-pinry extension and browser stores for adding web content.
README links pinry-cli-py companion for adding an image or URL; not a built-in executable in this repository.
Configure Python plugin objects in ENABLED_PLUGINS; hooks run before image/thumbnail creation and can modify objects. Documentation offers watermarking as an example, not a ready-made watermark UI.
Docker guide instructs copying the mounted data directory containing database, settings and pins; no automatic scheduled backup/restore UI is claimed.
Deleting a pin triggers deletion of its image record; example settings enable image-file auto-deletion. This is cleanup, not recoverable trash.
Published images cover ARMv7/ARMv8/AMD64 and persist all data via a mounted directory or named volume.
Docker defaults to SQLite for small personal deployments; guide documents switching local settings to PostgreSQL or MySQL.
README description includes videos but detailed feature list emphasizes images and URL ingestion explicitly validates image content; playback semantics/formats are not established.
README mentions webpages but model/API evidence establishes image URL, referrer and description rather than a full HTML capture/archive pipeline.
Prompts for input/output paths and content, date or type organization; can retry a different mode or process another directory within the same session.
Accepts a directory or single file, recursively collects paths and excludes dot-prefixed filenames; hidden directory traversal is not explicitly excluded by os.walk.
Content mode initializes quantized Llama3.2-3B-Instruct q3_K_M and llava-v1.6-vicuna-7b q4_0 through Nexa; these models run on the user's machine.
Text summaries and image descriptions drive suggested category folder names and filenames; not a persistent searchable caption catalogue.
Content analysis produces foldername and filename values used to construct the proposed output hierarchy.
Generates descriptive names while preserving extensions; sanitizer removes unsuitable words/punctuation, lowercases, separates words with underscores and limits length to 50 characters/five words.
Date mode creates year/month-name directories using filesystem modification time, not EXIF capture dates, and retains existing filenames.
Type mode separates image_files, text_files with plain-text/document/PDF/spreadsheet/ebook subcategories, and others; this does not imply semantic ebook understanding.
All three planning modes currently assign hardlink, and execution calls os.link. Original filenames remain; output is not an independent backup and cross-filesystem creation can fail.
Shows the proposed hierarchy before executing operations and offers another organization mode when the proposal is rejected; execute_operations also has an explicit non-mutating dry_run path.
Output creation and execute_operations occur only after a yes/no confirmation in the main workflow.

Content mode adds numeric suffixes for repeated proposed destinations in the current batch. Existing destinations cause os.link errors logged per operation rather than overwrite; date/type modes do not disambiguate duplicate basenames.
Silent mode appends messages and operation successes/failures to operation_log.txt; it is not a transactional journal or undo mechanism.
CLI reports path-load time and execution uses a progress bar with elapsed time and per-operation advancement.

Readers handle UTF-8 text/Markdown, DOCX-style documents, PDF, Excel/CSV and PowerPoint text. Plain text is capped at 3,000 characters and PDF at its first three pages; legacy .doc/.ppt are routed through libraries primarily intended for modern formats, so successful legacy parsing is not guaranteed.
README lists PNG/JPEG/GIF/BMP; source additionally classifies TIFF as an image. This is analysis eligibility, not documented animated playback or RAW decoding.
The documented content-analysis workflow uses local models and requires no hosted AI API.
README documents processing without Internet once models are set up; startup calls NLTK download and missing Nexa models are downloaded, so completely disconnected first-run setup is not established.
Installation documents a Metal build for macOS and links to Nexa CUDA/AMD support; CPU installation is also provided.
Roadmap proposes telling AI how to organize and rename files through conversation.
Changing models through the CLI is an unchecked roadmap item; current model identifiers are fixed in initialization source.
Checking file duplication remains on the roadmap. Current processed-path and destination-name sets are not duplicate-content detection.
Semantic support for ebooks, audio and video is listed as future work; extension-only ebook placement is already present in type mode.
Dockerfile is explicitly unchecked in the roadmap.
macOS/Linux/Windows executables are planned; currently documented installation requires Python, Conda and SDK dependencies.
Implementing established organization schemes such as Johnny Decimal is an unchecked roadmap item.
Installer and portable ZIP are documented; current guide warns built releases may no longer run on Windows 10.
Ubuntu-built archive and source execution; other distributions may need dependencies or source installation.
Current guide says source installation is the only macOS option; discontinued Intel .app is not claimed as a current native binary distribution.

The inspected Client API guide explicitly names Hydrus Web (floogulinc/hydrus-web), Hydrui and hyAway as actual web interfaces. These separately installed clients require an enabled API and running hydrus desktop client; the API welcome page and repository server are not counted as a built-in gallery UI.

Official integration guide explicitly lists hydit and aether as Android clients connecting to hydrus through Client API. These are separate user-created projects, not an official bundled hydrus Android application; current release compatibility was not tested.

Client API guide names Hydra Vista (konkrotte/hydravista) as a separate macOS client. This does not revive the discontinued official Intel app or change the official source-only macOS installation guidance; companion availability/compatibility was not live-tested.

Bundled hydrus_server executable can be hosted on the user's own machine to provide file/tag repository services with accounts. It is not required for local use and does not provide the separately documented third-party browser gallery UI.
Default settings, databases, media and subscriptions remain under the install directory; portable archive can move across paths/machines with path adjustments.

Drag files/folders or use import dialog; originals stay untouched by default while copied files receive content-addressed managed names. Optional delete-source-after-import must be explicitly enabled.
FAQ explicitly declines tracking source files in place; after import the original path is never used again.
Exact byte-identical repeat files are not stored again; visually similar but byte-different files remain separate for duplicate review.
SHA-256 identifies managed files and exact repeats regardless of original filename; no pairwise byte-comparison verification is claimed.
Import options include min/max size, resolution and whether to reimport previously deleted files; optional pre-import tagging parses filenames/folders.
Configured folders run on schedules, importing tags/URLs/notes via sidecars and exporting selected files with naming patterns/metadata.
Drag/drop, clipboard-copy or explicit export returns managed files; filename patterns can use tags/hash and create subfolders.
Create separate searchable file-domain lists, add/move membership and intersect with tag domains without duplicating payloads. These are not independent databases or user accounts.
Create shortcuts using different --db_dir values to run separate catalogues from one install, even concurrently. This is distinct from overlapping file domains within one database.
Distribute managed media over weighted locations with approximate maximum sizes and separate thumbnail placement; not indexing arbitrary originals in those locations.
Migration guide says all managed file subfolders must be located before the client can boot; it is not an offline-volume catalogue workflow.
New imports enter inbox; archive marks keepers without moving folders. Fast archive/delete filter supports skip/back and commits decisions at completion.
Imported thumbnails stream into pages; selections show counts/total size and preview pane, with multi-select context actions.
Create search/special/downloader pages from keyboard chooser, close via middle click and organize subscription landing pages into pages-of-pages.
Double/middle click opens media viewer; F toggles frame/fullscreen and hover panels expose tags, navigation and ratings.
Ctrl-wheel zooms normal viewing; duplicate review locks relative zoom and position while switching the compared files.
Page navigation, F3 tags, F4 ratings, F7 archive, Shift+Delete undelete and configurable duplicate-filter shortcuts.
mpv embed on compatible Windows/Linux or Qt player; supported containers include MP4/WebM/MKV/AVI/MOV/WMV and others. Wayland/mpv and macOS limitations are explicit.
MP3/OGG/FLAC/M4A/WAV and others play through available media backend; guide says it is not a typical playlist music manager.
Any managed file can be launched with the OS default application; import support alone does not imply internal rendering.
Collect-by combines results into groups according to selected tag namespaces or rating services, independent of file folders.
Tag prefix autocomplete displays counts, resolves aliases and supports wildcard * patterns and namespace-oriented retrieval.
All ordinary predicates must match; leading hyphen excludes tags, Shift builds OR chains and advanced OR accepts system predicates.
Combine technical metadata, inbox/archive, local/deleted domains and file relationships with tag predicates.
Editable filesize predicates can be combined with system:limit to retrieve a bounded largest-file work queue.
Duplicate-rule examples use width and height predicates to exclude tiny images; ordinary predicate searches are reused there.
Filter JPEG/PNG/image/PDF and other types, including separate predicates for each side of a duplicate pair.
system:rating filters like/dislike and configured numeric rating services.
Save common predicate searches with the star control instead of keeping large pages open.
Choose local/trash/known-file domain and specific tag service, including union of several file domains; current/pending tags can be searched separately.
Simple sort such as size/import time is applied before system:limit; complicated tag sorts may instead sort a random limited sample.
Configure namespace-based sorting and collection rules; limit semantics differ from simple metadata sorts.
Default my tags/downloader tags remain local; create namespaces such as creator/series/person and customize namespace colours.
Siblings provide reversible tag aliases; parents imply additional tags. Each tag service has its own rules, with configurable cross-service precedence.
Like/dislike/unrated, customizable integer-star scales including optional zero, and increment/decrement counters; several services can coexist with configurable shapes/colours.
New clients include a favourites like/dislike service, functioning as an editable lightweight curation label.
Apply tag edits to selected files and F4 ratings to many thumbnails; viewer tag editor can remain open while navigating and applies immediately.
Downloaders can capture creator comments/text as notes, visible in the viewer; named notes also import/export through sidecars.
Known URLs stay attached to content hashes, support downloader skip/refetch decisions and can be exported or used for recovery.
Routers export filtered/converted tags, URLs and named notes to TXT or nested JSON; repeated JSON exports update keys rather than replacing unrelated content.
Import multiple sources into tag/URL/note destinations with filename rules, delimiters, string processing, JSON formulas and live preview; sidecars are not the internal store.
Tag migration can export a Hydrus Tag Archive of queried hash-to-tag mappings independently of media bytes.
Maintenance descriptions establish EXIF detection, media-viewer display and system:has exif search. This is not a camera-centric EXIF editing suite.
XMP presence is detected, viewable and searchable with system:has xmp; arbitrary XMP sidecar import is not established by TXT/JSON routing.
Maintenance task and label expose IPTC metadata detection and system:has iptc; detailed field indexing is not claimed.
Human-readable embedded metadata can include AI prompts and is shown in viewer; search is documented for presence, not natural-language full-prompt search.
64-bit pHash with VP-tree Hamming-distance search finds shape-similar still images in the background; adjustable distance trades recall for false positives.
Distinguishes same-resolution/pixel-content matches even when metadata or file encoding differs; pixel hashes can be regenerated independently.
Toggle A/B with locked zoom/position; show filesize/resolution/age/tags, estimated JPEG quality and more expensive visual-comparison statements.
Choose better/same-quality relations and whether to delete the worse file; configurable comparison scores suggest order, while each duplicate group maintains a best-file king.
Relationships need not delete either file; same-quality/alternate classifications can retain both when desired.
Confirmed relationships stop ordinary re-presentation and imply transitive relations; false positives are remembered across runs, without a complete per-decision audit log.
Configure transfer/merge of tags, ratings, archive status, URLs and notes, with defaults or per-action customization; content merges are not fully undoable.
Require one side, both sides or different searches per side, plus maximum Hamming distance and require/exclude pixel matches; mixed-pair or full-group review modes.
Rules combine pair searches, ordered comparisons and actions. Semi-automatic queues require approve/deny; fully automatic rules can delete and merge without per-pair approval.
Preview matched/failed pairs and resulting content updates before saving rules; ambiguous A/B ordering is flagged for better-than rules.
Rule comparators can protect EXIF/XMP/IPTC/human-readable/software metadata and ICC presence; they check presence flags, not equality or richness of contents.
Official docs point to Hydrus Video Deduplicator, which discovers video pairs and queues them through Client API; native still-image pHash is not video matching.
Basic alternate relationships exist, but ordered WIP/recolour labels and richer presentation are explicitly future work; large alternate sets currently scale poorly.
Format matrix marks HEIC and HEIF as importable, thumbnail-capable and viewable.
AVIF stills and AVIF sequences have thumbnails and internal viewing in format matrix.
JXL is explicitly importable, thumbnail-capable and internally viewable.
GIF/APNG/WebP and HEIC/HEIF/AVIF sequences; Ugoira ZIP can use embedded animation.json or note-provided frame delays, otherwise defaults to 125 ms.
Krita/OpenRaster/PSD display embedded previews; Clip Studio and Procreate have thumbnails but no direct viewing, and XCF/SAI2 are import-only.
SVG import and thumbnails are supported; format matrix explicitly says SVG is not directly viewable inside hydrus.
Can import PDF/Office/ebook/archive formats with differing previews; PDF thumbnails except encrypted PDFs and CBZ identification do not imply internal document reading.
Detects type by inspecting content rather than trusting extension/MIME; users can force a type from context menu.
User-installed downloader definitions parse gallery searches, file/post URLs or simple page links; fresh installs contain no downloaders. Tags/notes can accompany files.
Subscriptions detect new URLs, adapt interval to source velocity, stop dead queries and publish to grouped landing pages; they do not reliably backfill old gaps.
Installed watcher definitions repeatedly check a thread, adapt to incoming frequency and stop at inactivity/404; not filesystem watching.
Global, domain/subdomain and downloader/subscription/watcher contexts all must permit each request; review usage and customize limits, with conservative defaults.
Subscriptions resume where they stopped after cancellation/global pause; normal downloading/import queues can also be paused.
Slow tag/system searches display a stop button; subscriptions expose cancellation and global pause controls.
Sync all repository hash/tag metadata into a local cache; uploads are explicitly queued/pended and removals may require janitor petitions. Supports multiple repos.
Bundled separate server can host multiple services with registration tokens, accounts, uploader/downloader/admin permissions and server backups; designed for delayed sync, not live LAN browsing.
Enable a port and per-program access keys; active only while desktop client runs. Default HTTP/local policy can be changed to remote/HTTPS, with operator security responsibilities.

Official API guide lists Hydrus Companion browser upload/cookie helpers, Hyshare small-gallery sharing, kaimen virtual FUSE search folders and other workflow tools. Separate browser/Android/macOS client deployment is recorded in its own platform findings; these extensions are not bundled core features.
API guide links DeepDanbooru and model-based taggers, separate projects not authored/guaranteed by hydrus. No built-in face recognition or semantic photo search is inferred.

Deleted media enters a trash domain, can be searched and undeleted, and is automatically permanently removed after configurable time. Files leave local storage only after no local domain retains them.
Documentation says final physical deletion tries the OS recycle bin by default, providing another possible recovery stage, not a universal guarantee.
Inbox/archive and trash can be reversed; duplicate filters allow going back before commit. Auto-resolution undo explicitly cannot reverse metadata merges.
Stored originals are expected not to change; editing requires export, external edit and reimport. Metadata remains in catalogue/exports rather than in-place media edits.
Set backup location then lock and mirror database/media, copying changes thereafter. Distributed storage disables simple backup and needs a coordinated external backup with client shut down.

Maintenance tasks check expected presence/content to discover corruption or external changes, optionally move bad bytes aside, remove records or enqueue URL redownload; heavier than presence-only checking.
Queue missing-file checks/redownload from known URLs, export hashes/tags/URLs for recovery, and move orphaned payloads to a review location for deletion/reimport.
Regenerate metadata, thumbnails, supplementary MD5/SHA1/SHA512, pHash, pixel hash, blurhash and embedded-metadata presence flags independently.
Default client connects to no repository and searches local databases; network downloading/sharing is optional.
Every upload requires a conscious action according to introduction; the project states it never phones home.
Repository content attribution is reassigned to a null account after default 90 days, configurable by operator; does not eliminate IP/content inference or malicious-server risks.

Crowdin-maintained Android resource translations localize gallery controls and dialogs, not just README text. Inspected French resources cover filtering/sorting, copy/move/delete, sharing, confirmation and password/fingerprint controls; bundled release notes explicitly mention translation updates. No claim is made that every locale is complete.
Native Android gallery with F-Droid/Play distribution links; current store availability was not tested.
Queries Android media albums and operates on their existing paths; local originals are not obligatorily re-imported.
Album settings and exclusions are keyed by folder path and album contents come from the Android content-provider helper.
Album grid has separate portrait/landscape column settings, optional animations, pull-to-refresh and multi-selection.
Pinned development source defines day/week/month/year grouping and chronological group comparison; not asserted as present in 2016 release.
Tap toggles toolbar/system bars, with an immersive full-screen mode and swipeable media pager.
Slideshow schedules automatic advancement modulo album size and hides system UI; stopping removes callbacks.
Bundled release notes explicitly discuss a zoom-out fix with SubScaling ImageView enabled; exact current gesture behavior was not runtime-tested.
Video fragment renders a thumbnail and launches ACTION_VIEW with media MIME and URI permission when played; do not assume all codecs are internally decoded.
A dedicated GifImageView loads the GIF URI, separate from ordinary image and video previews.
Choose light, dark or AMOLED base theme and customize colors from a palette.
Sort by full path or numeric-aware file-version comparison, ascending or descending.
Date comparator uses getDateModified, even though a menu identifier contains date_taken; not claimed as EXIF capture-date sorting.
Compare media byte sizes and reverse order as selected.
Type sorting compares media MIME strings.
Grid exposes all-media, video-only, image-only and GIF-only modes.
Pin/unpin updates local album settings and re-sorts the grid.
Exclude selected album paths, or select a parent to remove all displayed descendants without deleting media.
Album action calls hide/unhide helpers, remembers hidden paths and exposes a separate hidden display mode; it is not evidence of encryption.
Configure password checks for hidden content/deletion and fingerprint unlock when Android M+ and hardware support it; password checks compare a stored SHA-256 hash.
Choose destination folders; helpers move/copy underlying files and rescan new paths in MediaStore.
Single-media action prompts for a new name, moves the file and updates MediaStore/path state.
Single-media and album deletion require a confirmation dialog and optionally password/fingerprint authentication before invoking deletion.
v0.7 changelog documents progress dialogs and cancellation for delete/move/copy/rename; album code shows progress callbacks as items complete.
Shows path, MIME, size, orientation, dimensions, modification date, original capture date, camera/EXIF summary and GPS DMS; all-details enumerates extracted tags.
Static-map URLs embed image coordinates for Google, Mapbox streets/dark/light or Tyler/Stamen; this is not an offline basemap or full-library map.
UCrop is launched with a PNG cache destination and free-style cropping enabled.
Successful crop output is copied from cache into the album and the UI reports a new file, rather than overwriting the source through this handler.
Single-media menu sends ±90 or 180-degree rotations to the image fragment; persistent original-file rotation is not established by this inspected handler.
Android choosers receive file URIs with read permission for sharing, external editing/viewing and attach/use-as actions.
PrintHelper renders the selected bitmap with fit-to-page scaling and reports failures.
Selected album paths can be sent to a shortcut-creation helper from the album menu.
v0.7 lists Color Palette and single-media handler opens PaletteActivity for the current file; color search/editing is not implied.
Changelog lists Affix and source can concatenate two decoded pictures horizontally into a new JPEG, but grid menu starts hidden and available entry path/release completeness is not established.
Album search menu explicitly displays a coming-soon hint; inspected album handlers do not establish an implemented search workflow.
Details dialog includes Fix Date but its callback contains a TODO/commented implementation and only reports unable-to-fix-date.
Accepts multiple directory arguments and reports duplicate groups; deletion is a separately requested mode.
Searches supplied filesystem paths directly, with no managed import or image-format requirement in the matching pipeline.
Candidate files are compared by size and MD5 signatures before normal final byte comparison; this is byte-content matching, not perceptual similarity.
Ordinary duplicate detection confirms hashes using a byte-by-byte comparison. Quick summary explicitly bypasses this stage.
'--recurse traverses all supplied roots; --recurse: traverses only roots positioned after that option, permitting mixed shallow/deep scans.
'--symlinks follows symlinked directories; manual warns that keeping a link while deleting its target can lose the usable file.
Multiple names pointing to the same disk area normally do not count as duplicates; --hardlinks includes them. This option does not create hard links.
'--minsize and --maxsize restrict candidates inclusively using byte counts.
'--nohidden excludes hidden files and --noempty excludes zero-length files; arbitrary scan-time path glob exclusions are not established by this manual.
'--permissions prevents files with different owner, group or permission bits from being considered duplicates.
'--cache reuses signatures between comparisons; manual explicitly says availability depends on the system/build.
Cache supports readonly, orphan pruning, clearing and vacuuming. Maintenance can run without directory arguments and still takes effect with readonly; operation order is clear, prune, update, vacuum.
Default output separates groups by blank lines; --sameline places a group on one line and escapes spaces/backslashes. Options omit the first member and include size or modification time.
'--summarize reports duplicate information; --quicksummary skips the slower byte-verification phase and must not be treated as fully verified equality.
Keep/delete tags can be set for individual files, lists of indices, or selected subsets; prune can process reviewed subsets incrementally.
The interactive all command tags every member of the current group for keeping.
Interactive prune refuses groups with every file tagged for deletion; at least one member must be tagged for keeping.
Select/deselect by substring, prefix, suffix, exact path or PCRE2 expression; clear or invert selections within affected sets before tagging them.
'--delete --noprompt retains the first ordered member and removes others. --immediate deletes as matches arrive without collecting groups and implies no prompt.
Order by modification time (default), status-change time or filename, with reversal; changelog documents ctime tie-breaking for mtime.
'--deferconfirmation postpones byte-level equality checks in interactive mode until immediately before deletion.
Interactive mode separates tagging from deletion via DELETE/prune, while plain line prompts remain available; --noprompt and --immediate deliberately bypass review.
Version 2.2.0 documents checking whether files marked duplicate changed during execution before deleting them; this is not a permanent integrity journal.
'--log writes file-deletion choices to a chosen logfile; documentation does not describe rollback or saved file contents.
Screen mode supports paging, file/group navigation, selected-group jumps, direct goto, keep/delete hotkeys and command help; --plain or unsupported screen builds use line prompts.

Pinned Compose resources contain French and German translations for Timeline/Albums, Settings, share/select/restore actions, metadata labels and editing dialogs. Some inspected French entries remain English, so full translation completeness is not claimed; this is independent of multilingual AI models.

General Settings Secure Mode blocks screenshots, screen recordings and the recent-apps preview. It protects display/capture surfaces rather than encrypting ordinary files; vault encryption remains a separate feature.
APK/F-Droid/Obtainium distributions; 5.2.2 release lists Android 10/API29+, while README still states 11. Features such as Trash retain higher version requirements.
README says Play price supports the project and automatic Play updates; no separate paid functional tier is documented.
Offline flavor removes network permissions, maps and cloud access; WithML bundles models for offline AI, whereas Offline NoML cannot download missing models afterward.
Device media is browsed in its existing albums/folders; app virtual organization does not require copying originals into a managed library.
Mounted Android-indexed volumes share one library while retaining volume identity; same-name merges are optional display grouping, not separate catalogues or physical moves.
Local and connected-cloud media share date sections, fast month navigation, story cards and selectable day/month/year headers; capture or modified time can order ascending/descending.
Current grid supports one to nine columns and mosaic three to six, with separate timeline/album sizing and long-press drag selection or full date-group selection.
Wide windows open viewer beside timeline with current grid item outlined; smaller windows use fullscreen paging.
Pinch/pan viewing supports heavy formats; released HDR HEIC path uses native tiles/gain maps, while current format guide offers smoothing control for pixel art.

Media3 player supports frame seeking; 5.2.2 adds Dolby Vision/HDR10/HLG playback with a setting and compatible display requirement, reporting unsupported DV profiles. Actual codec support remains device-dependent.
Uses appropriate spherical/cylindrical projections, drag/pinch controls, and for full spheres gyroscope steering with compass indicator. No projection picker or VR mode is offered.
5.1 changelog explicitly adds configurable album slideshows; timing/effect specifics were not established in inspected sources.
Wallpaper-derived or preset palettes have live Material 3 previews; release notes describe customizable Library sections and shortcut visibility.
Collections reference chosen media/whole albums without extra copies; same item can belong to several collections, and deleting/removing membership does not delete media.
Pin albums, choose covers, create collapsible named groups and override automatic Common/Apps/Other sections; deleting a group does not remove folders.
Merge same-name albums across volumes or fold subfolders/parent subfolders into one view, with unmerge; no file movement or renaming occurs.
Virtual Photos/Videos/GIF/RAW albums cover all folders and can be shown/hidden as a Library section.
Timeline groups related RAW/JPEG members into a stack cell with access to members; not duplicate deletion.
Optional smart grouping collapses burst shots and edited copies into timeline stacks without implying an automatic best-shot/culling score.
Without AI, queries match stored filename/description; matching category/place/album shortcuts and removable search history appear during typing, excluding locked albums.

Installed CLIP indexes images; current EmbeddingGemma 2 engine also indexes sampled video content and is documented as multilingual. Results sort by accuracy/date and show indexing progress; engine changes rebuild index.
Choose an example from timeline/albums for similarity-ranked results; current video-aware engine can sample several frames from a video query. Distinct from sending data to Google Lens.
Discovery exposes locations, media types, camera models, special modes and groupings; release notes add synced server tags into metadata search.
Timeline controls filter type, favorite state, year or album, independently of descriptive AI search.

Intelligence Hub manages separate search (~150–320 MB), face (~131 MB) and cutout (~44 MB) packs. Bundled builds can restore without downloads; scan-only-while-charging and skip-hidden settings are available, while locked albums are never scanned.
Face model pack enables detected-face strips, face scanning and editor blur/mosaic actions; current Standard tier uses UltraFace plus ArcFace.
Local scan groups faces into New/Named people; regroup can rebuild after new media or mistaken merges. 5.2 release identifies deterministic batch clustering.
Recognition models match recurring faces into person groups; 5.2.2 rescans preserve names using face matching rather than recreating unnamed groups.
Name people, store birthdays and choose face covers; local/cloud person sources can be selected independently.

Confirm/reject possible duplicates, merge groups, remove individual faces/photos from a person, hide/unhide and delete a person while suppressing those faces from future grouping; photos themselves remain.
Blur everywhere creates new copies of photos containing the selected person; face models also enable local blur/mosaic editor tools.

Define categories with text description, optional example photos and Broad/Balanced/Strict/Exact preference; preview matches, pin/set cover and optionally exclude videos. Categories classify locally but do not imply embedded tag writing.
Model-backed long-press or editor Cutout/Remove background uses include/exclude points with undo/redo/refinement; copy/share/save transparent PNG while keeping original.

Companion server receives resized JPEGs/video sample frames, not originals, and returns embeddings; choose device/server/both index placement and remote ranking. Bearer/HMAC authentication, per-user indexes, chunked background jobs and retries are documented; HTTP warns of unencrypted traffic.

Cloud smart-search setting lets capable servers, currently Immich, answer queries; separate provider-type switches download thumbnails for local indexing, including NAS providers without their own AI.
Separate Visual search shares current image/video frame with chosen installed app, can convert unsupported formats and needs explicit vault-item allowance because temporary decrypted data is exposed.
Fast and Accurate face-grouping tiers are explicitly Coming soon; Standard is the available tier.
Incremental refresh preserves valid results, skips failures, supports paused/resumable states and retries failed items; cancelling keeps completed work.

Independently refresh metadata, embeddings, categories or people, or run all in sequence; full refresh deliberately reprocesses complete items. Category reset deletes custom categories but not photos.
Displays label/path, capture time, dimensions/size, video duration/fps/format, print density when present and complete metadata list, with cloud/encryption state badges.
Media Info edits labels/descriptions; video descriptions remain only in the app database rather than embedded file metadata. Direct filename rename is a separate action.
Date/time edits drive capture-sorted timeline. Unsupported formats offer a dated PNG copy instead, warning that PNG flattens animation/HDR/layers/RAW; original can be kept or explicitly trashed.

Remove all or selected found categories: location, dates, device/owner, captions/authorship, camera, people, edit history, credentials, thumbnail. Supports JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF/JP2/JXL/HEIF/AVIF/MP4/MOV/3GP; preserves media data, orientation, profiles, HDR gain maps and motion clip.

Sanitization re-reads output to check removed/retained metadata and exact media payload before saving; restricted Android-folder moves copy/verify before requesting deletion permission. This is operation-specific, not perpetual integrity checking.
Favorite badges/filtering span local/cloud library; release routes supported local favorites through Android request APIs and backup can restore matched favorites.
MapLibre-based map reads existing media GPS after permission, not live tracking; display follows app/light/dark styles and can need a CARTO key. Offline build substitutes place list without tiles.
Nearby markers form numbered clusters, tapping zooms or opens a colocated-photo sheet; marker selection and grid scrolling stay linked.
Places list groups by cities/countries with photo/place/country counts, per-location timelines and recent trips when available, including builds without interactive map.
Map manual explicitly says no in-app coordinate editing; removing existing location metadata is supported separately.
Viewer previews camera RAW; current editor develops DNG/CR2/CR3/NEF/NRW/ARW/RAF/ORF/RW2/PEF/SRW. Viewer format support alone does not mean every editor accepts the file.

White-balance presets/custom temp/tint; exposure/tone; sharpening; Linear/VNG/PPG/AHD/DCB demosaic; denoise and half resolution; sRGB/AdobeRGB/Wide/ProPhoto output; clip/blend/rebuild highlights. TIFF 8/16 export only holds development, not additional crop/markup/look edits.
HEIC/HEIF viewing includes supported HDR/gain-map paths; 5.2.2 adds bundled deep-12-bit decoding fixes. Display HDR remains device-dependent and editing may flatten it.
AVIF is a supported viewer format, including 12-bit decoding fixes in 5.2.2.
JXL viewer support and persistent heavy-format thumbnails are documented; exporting JXL from current editor additionally depends on encoder availability.
GIF/animated WebP/APNG full-resolution rendering is in 5.1 release; moving GIF thumbnails can be disabled. Editing/export does not guarantee preserving animation.
Viewer opens SVG, flattened PSD and JP2/J2K; SVG is rendered as pixels and PSD layers are not editable merely because the file previews.
Detects embedded clips, exposes Motion toggle and frame strip; listed families include Google Motion Photos/Samsung Live Photos/Micro Videos. This is not a claim of Apple image+MOV pairing.
Save embedded motion as a separate video or use frame picker for stills without changing source. Editing its still creates a separate image copy.
Current tool catalogue includes light/color/curves/white balance, looks/detail/vignette/lens blur/grain/tone/posterize/edges/borders, with histogram channels and clipping display.
Current editor includes crop/straighten/perspective tools, with on-canvas grid and explicit Apply/Reset recipe steps.

Up to sixteen JPEG/PNG image layers, locked base, reorder/duplicate/hide/lock, transforms, five blend modes, opacity, clipping and erase/paint masks; output flattens visible layers and missing source media can be relinked on recovery.
Current catalogue includes Markup; with face models, blur/mosaic face operations are available. Detailed brush shapes are not inferred.
Hold canvas to view original or drag split-view divider; geometry changes switch to whole-original comparison because alignment no longer matches.
Current photo/video editor never alters opened originals; outputs go to Pictures/ReFra or Movies/ReFra with randomized edited suffix. Unsaved changes/export cancellation require confirmation.

Current recipes/layer actions have undo/redo and recover committed edits if Android stops app. Legacy editor can revert overwrite only while its separate original edit backup remains; not a general file-operation undo.

Current editor exports JPEG/PNG/WebP and encoder-dependent HEIF/JXL; Original copy preference retains JPEG quality or PNG losslessness. Removed-background copies become PNG. Legacy editor has different format/overwrite behavior.
Current MP4/QuickTime editor supports frame-precise in/out trims, split/delete/duplicate/reorder, ripple insertion, linked audio, snapping, multiple tracks and overlays.
Transform/crop Fit/Fill/Crop, scale/rotation/position/horizontal flip/background plus per-clip light/color/curves and opacity.
Current export summary specifies size, constant fps, H.264/automatic bitrate and stereo 48 kHz AAC when audio reaches mix, with progress/retry and untouched source.
Import audio, record local voice-over or extract clip sound; mix gain/pan/fades/mute/solo/master limiter, channel routing/mono downmix, sidechain ducking and three-band EQ/high-pass.

Create multiple encrypted vaults with device security or custom PIN/pattern/password and timed lockout; optional list gate/one-lock mode. Encrypt & Keep retains plaintext originals; Encrypt & Delete removes them explicitly.

Choose internal/SD/USB directory and optional device/custom gate; .nomedia removes files from normal scans. Files remain readable by direct-storage tools; removal of configuration can keep or remove hiding marker.

On Android 11+ supported device media normally has roughly 30-day provider-controlled retention, individual/all restore or permanent empty. Disabling trash, unsupported sources and private-folder deletes are permanent.

5.2.2 lets backed-up selections target device/cloud/both with remembered preference and warns when sources lack trash. Trash confirmations can be enabled; remote-backup-row deletion has an explicit no-extra-confirmation exception.
Copy/move picker supports new folders, device/removable/cloud destinations and authentication for locked albums. Read-only targets are disabled; partial transfers report retained sources.
Viewer Rename changes actual filename with Android write permission as needed; distinct from description/label editing. Inspected docs establish individual rename, not batch templates.
Folder-based WebDAV/SMB/NFS transfer collisions create numbered filenames rather than overwriting; current editor outputs also use random suffixes.
Connect Immich, Nextcloud, ownCloud, WebDAV, SMB or NFS depending on build; local/cloud listings merge but capabilities vary. Google Photos is explicitly not supported.
WebDAV/Nextcloud/ownCloud accounts browse/upload alongside SMB/NFS; server-side people/search/archive/memories cannot be assumed on simple shares.

Background upload selects local albums and destination accounts, separate cellular rules for photos/videos, charging requirement, album synchronization and account/video/per-album folder overrides; Immich manages its own physical layout.

15-minute to daily approximate Android schedules, Wi-Fi-only auto sync, unrestricted manual sync and cold-start sync; opt-in remote deletions remove only app-downloaded copies, not arbitrary local originals.
5.2.2 populates shared/v3 albums and allows owned-album rename/share/delete/member removal. Same-account Copy adds membership; Move is explicitly unsupported because albums are not folders.
5.2.2 links identical existing local files instead of re-downloading Immich assets and places downloads in account/album folders, not the server's internal storage tree.

Scan verified backed-up originals, retain favorites and choose age threshold (default Never); daily/three-day/weekly auto cleanup can run, but without All Files Access requests review instead of silent deletion.
256/512 MB or 1/2/5 GB global cache limits evict oldest cached items; pin whole accounts for previews, cache while browsing and optionally Wi-Fi only. Preview cache is not downloaded originals.
Force offline uses only cache; account pinning downloads thumbnails/previews with partial-progress/retry status, and per-account/auto-only cache clears retain accounts/listings.
5.2.2 persists JXL/PSD/JP2/TIFF/RAW/deep-bit-depth HEIF thumbnails to disk rather than regenerating each launch.
Shared Links lists existing provider links, copies URLs, edits description/download/upload/metadata permissions and revokes links without deleting media. Current app has no create-link screen.
Where Immich share-management exposes it, edit a pre-existing link's password; creation remains in server UI.
Existing link expiry choices range from one day to one year or never; app can revoke with confirmation, contingent on provider support.

FCast-compatible receiver required, discovered by mDNS or entered manually at default port 46899; remote pause/seek/speed controls depend on receiver codec support. No Chromecast protocol is involved.
Single photo or size-dependent 2x2/4x4/6x6 grids with original, black-white or icon/emoji presentation; tap opens exact photo, styles do not edit files. Widget image has no separate unlock gate.
Current editor accepts JPEG/PNG/video edit intents and returns the saved copy to caller while also retaining it in ReFra output folders.

Archive settings, favorites, cloud configs, groups/collections/categories, metadata/locations, people corrections and optional edit originals/vaults; merge restore keeps existing data and resumes after restart. Ordinary photos outside vaults and biometric/semantic embeddings are excluded.

Optional archive password protects exported vault media, which is decrypted inside archive; vault custom credentials are included only with protected archives. Without archive password restored vault uses device lock.
Daily/on-library-change or manual cleanup removes orphaned extracted data/memberships/edit backups, preserving cloud cache rows and user definitions such as people/collections/vaults.

Hidden Developer menu exposes grouped/recent logs, severity/date search, breadcrumbs, crash reports, ZIP/copy export and clear/disable controls. Docs warn filenames, paths and server URLs may remain; not an operation-recovery journal.
group emits reports; remove, move, link and dedupe consume previous discovery results. Input paths can come from arguments or stdin for composition with tools such as find.
Groups by length, file identity, prefix hash, suffix hash and finally whole-content hash. Default MetroHash128 can be replaced by xxhash3, BLAKE3, SHA-256/512 or SHA3-256/512.
Algorithm documentation explicitly says no byte-by-byte file comparison is performed; identity relies on size and hashes.
Can report unique files or groups below/above a chosen replication factor, rather than only pairs of duplicates.
One invocation accepts multiple files/directories and recursively scans directories with a configurable depth limit.
'--isolate counts matching content within one root as one replica, distinguishing cross-tree backups from repeated paths inside a tree; removal can retain/drop a root's matching files together.
Filename/path patterns, excluded paths, case-insensitive mode and Perl-compatible regex alternatives constrain scans. Hidden files and .gitignore/.fdignore matches are skipped unless overridden.
Inclusive byte-size bounds accept decimal/binary units; minimum defaults to one byte.
'--one-fs skips nested mount points and cross-filesystem symlinks and avoids matching across devices/filesystems.
Normally counts multiple links to the same underlying file only once. Flags independently control following/reporting symbolic links, matching links and isolated-root replica semantics.

Default report order preserves earlier entries; priorities can instead select removal by creation/modification/access time, Unix status-change time or nesting depth. At least one retained replica is required by the action CLI.
'--keep-name and --keep-path prevent matching entries being removed; action --name/--path restrict the eligible deletion set.
Exports default text with hashes/sizes, fdupes-compatible text, CSV or JSON. Removal tools accept default and JSON reports, allowing manual editing before action.
'--dry-run emits planned filesystem operations instead of executing them; output can be redirected with the CLI output option.
link defaults to replacing redundant copies with hard links to retained content.
link --soft replaces redundant files with symbolic links; link-following/matching combinations require care to avoid leaving dangling references.
dedupe shares underlying file data without removing filenames on supported filesystems. This feature is explicitly unavailable on Windows.
move sends selected redundant files to a target directory instead of deleting or linking them; this is not described as an OS trash integration.
remove permanently removes selected redundant entries using the separately reviewed report and keeper policies.
'--transform invokes an external program per file, with pipe or $IN/$OUT support. Documentation demonstrates stripping EXIF with exiv2 before matching, not perceptual image matching.
$IN transformations use a temporary copy by default; --no-copy deliberately permits the external command to modify the original and is warned as data-loss-prone.

Actions check sizes against the report unless disabled, lock files unless --no-lock is selected and can skip whole groups if any file changed after --modified-before. Transformed reports automatically disable size checks.
'--cache stores hashes with identity, size and timestamps; unchanged files reuse hashes even after typical renames/moves. Metadata-stable modifications can make the cache stale.
README recommends persistent caching to resume large jobs quickly after interruption; it is hash reuse rather than a transactional deletion journal.
Parallel directory traversal and staged hashing use separate per-device random/sequential pools, automatically tuned for HDD/SSD/removable/unknown devices and overridable with --threads.
README attributes low memory use on millions of paths to prefix-compressed representations; this is a project claim, not a measured result here.
Orders accesses by physical placement and uses page-cache drop-behind on Linux; documentation says these optimizations are unavailable on other platforms.
'--skip-content-hash bypasses whole-file hashing, with explicit false-positive warnings and advice to enlarge prefix/suffix samples. This mode is not safe exact-content verification.
Reports scan/grouping progress; v0.35.0 limits default progress output to terminal stderr for cleaner redirected workflows.
complete prints setup scripts for Bash, Zsh, Fish, Elvish and PowerShell; installation into the shell is manual.
Documented core workflow reads local/mounted paths and writes local reports/actions; no hosted service is required.

Application target includes English, German, French, Italian and Spanish resources. Inspected German/French strings translate search/index progress, gestures, settings and privacy help, not only example search queries. Some retain older help wording, so complete current-UI translation parity is not guaranteed.
Current README specifies iPhone/iPad on iOS 18 or later; source builds require separate MobileCLIP S2 model bundles.
In-app privacy guide describes paying for the application instead of a free app with network-dependent in-app purchases; this does not change the MIT source licence.
Search controller opens the system user-library smart album and references PHAsset identifiers without importing originals into a second managed store.
Encodes a text description and ranks saved image vectors by similarity; default top result count is 120 rather than an exact-keyword matching guarantee.
Swipe upward in a photo viewer to compare its stored embedding against the library and display similar photos; this is semantic similarity, not exact duplicate identification.
Settings exposes a persisted 10–1000 result slider in increments of ten; actual results are bounded by indexed library size.
In-app guide lists English, French, German, Spanish and Italian input and explicitly says English works best; comparative accuracy is not independently verified.
MobileCLIP S2 encoders run through Core ML locally; model files are bundled in the installed app rather than retrieved for each search.
Indexing forcibly disables network photo requests and the guide describes airplane-mode use. iCloud-only originals may remain low-resolution until a user permits download.
README says photos are not uploaded for search; inference and persisted vectors remain on-device. User-invoked sharing is separate.
A cloud-download button for a lower-quality asset enables network access and requests its maximum-size image. Offline operation remains available if declined.
Compares current asset IDs with saved embeddings and offers an Update index action for new photos. Collection observation does not itself imply automatic embedding generation.
Saves embeddings every 5,000 accumulated results, at completion and on caught indexing errors; later indexing skips already persisted IDs. Unsaved work may need repetition.
Fetches images concurrently in batches of 32, performs batch Core ML prediction and falls back to single-image encoding if a batch fails.
Metal/MPSGraph multiplies normalized Float16 embeddings using persistent buffers and a cached graph; the controller provides CPU cosine-similarity fallback when GPU search is unavailable.
Appends new embeddings and records deleted IDs, migrates the older archive format and compacts after a journal exceeds five million bytes or tombstones exist.
Displays a prominent best match followed by the remaining photo collection and opens individual results in the photo viewer.
Viewer wraps the image in a scroll view with 1×–20× zoom and displays the asset creation timestamp.

Photo has a favorite field and API registers favorite-list and bulk favorite-edit routes.

face_recognition detects locations/encodings on thumbnails and persists face coordinates, encodings and JPEG crops.

Owner-checked handlers relabel selected faces or delete their face records without deleting the parent photograph.

Active Places365 path stores attributes, scene categories and environment words in search_captions and creates thing albums. Densecap is named in README but disabled in the default caption-generation method.
Photo methods call local face_recognition, Places365 inference and Im2Vec(cuda=False); this establishes local processing paths, not all-service offline operation.

README supports custom albums; AlbumUser stores owner, photos, cover photos and title independently of the source folders.

Mapbox location features create owner-scoped place albums at different geographic levels with up to four selected cover photos.
Places365 attributes and categories each generate owner-scoped AlbumThing collections with representative cover photos.
Map viewing is listed as implemented; stored GPS coordinates and location-cluster endpoint support geographic browsing.
Requires a Mapbox API key; returned location feature text is persisted for search and album generation. Historical free-tier numbers in README are not a current pricing guarantee.
README lists location search; geocoding appends returned search_text to the photo's searchable location field.
Despite stale README roadmap, pinned backend has share/unshare handlers for photos and user albums plus shared-to/from-me routes; original access checks recognize these memberships.
Owner-checked makepublic operation and media handler permit unauthenticated access to photos explicitly marked public; password/expiry semantics are not documented.
Produces tiny, small, medium and big proportional and square JPEG thumbnails, correcting EXIF orientation, plus face crops in protected media storage.
Scanning, event generation, title regeneration and face training enqueue asynchronous jobs; LongRunningJob tracks status, times and target/current progress.
Registered handlers expose library counts, monthly/country counts, location timeline/sunburst and search-word-cloud helpers; UI completeness and helper accuracy were not independently verified.
Backend routes socialgraph and egograph to graph-building helpers, with person_id for ego view; these code paths are more specific than the old README's generic planned graphs.
Django routes expose library, face, album, job and user operations with JWT obtain/refresh endpoints; this is an application API, not a stable-version guarantee.
README lists basic editing such as rotation as longer-term work. Automatic EXIF orientation of thumbnails is implemented but is not a user editing feature.
Tagging an undetected face is explicitly listed as upcoming, distinct from naming an already detected face.

Web upload/admin application with Go backend, Vue frontend and MySQL; README offers VPS/manual deployment and cross-platform server builds.
Browser upload sends supported images to chosen enabled provider; upload size is configurable and source checks PNG/JPG/JPEG/GIF/BMP suffix/MIME combinations.
V1 multipart API accepts image, optional/configured token and apiSelect; returns image name/URL and provider deletion data, with explicit disabled/auth/empty/size errors documented.
Registered adapters include Sogou, Sina, SMMS, Upload.cc, Flickr, Imgur, Alibaba/JD/Juejin and others; these are legacy external integrations, not verified currently functioning services.
Both adapters are registered and eligible as dispatch root stores, alongside local/Flickr/Imgur; service setup/credentials remain external.
Enabled Local adapter writes image bytes to configured server filesystem and returns a server URL; use of remote dispatch/providers is a separate choice.
Local adapter uses current upload year/month/day directories and a random 16-character basename with retained extension; not EXIF capture-date organization.
V2 uploads to selected root, creates a dispatch/hash URL, starts secondary upload asynchronously and serves cached/provider redirects. Stable URL can outlive a provider target change.

Dispatch checks target availability and attempts another ranked host, falling back to root when destinations are exhausted. Source contains TODO failure handling, so this is designed behavior rather than proven reliable failover.
Admin menu drag-order controls enabled providers; provider records separately hold homepage rank and dispatch weight plus configuration updates.

Provider Auth setting distinguishes guest, any signed-in user and administrator-only use; this is upload-provider access, not password-protected photo albums.
Server enforces configured maximum size and allowed filename/MIME suffix combinations; this is not evidence of full decoding, malware scan or content-safety recognition.
Configurable enabled middleware tracks attempts/time, temporary block period and threshold for persistent blocks; release 2.3.9 includes IP-block fixes.
Admin lists image/dispatch/backup records with page/limit, provider filtering and ascending/descending ID order.
Admin-selected remote URLs are concurrently downloaded to server files and linked backup records; source uses a task lock and reports progress/completion or a 60-second inactivity timeout.
Goroutines perform secondary host upload and multi-image local synchronization; no durable queue/checkpoint recovery is established.
Dispatch stores URL targets with a 3600 cache duration and redirects directly on cache hits; release notes identify Redis cache fixes.
Admin action calls ClearAll; group-selective cache clearing remains a TODO.
Reports include images by provider, last-seven-day all/local image counts, recent registrations and API information, rendered as dashboard charts.
Paged logs and synchronization progress/completion messages expose operational status. These logs are not rollback/crash-recovery file journals.
Admin accepts ID lists; model deletes associated local paths and database rows. Inspected delete path does not establish revocation of every third-party hosted copy.

Pinch and double-tap controls accompany a responsive gallery, with native iOS browsing also available.

Detects JPEG gain maps including Apple HDR photos and composites HDR on compatible high-dynamic-range displays.

Lists storage objects before image filtering to identify paired videos and enables playback; detection is configurable.

Displays extracted Fujifilm film-simulation settings.
Auto-generates tags from directory structure; Eagle integration can also map folders to tags.

Pipeline computes tone information and stores it in manifest records; this is not documented object tagging or semantic search.

Per-photo errors mark an item failed and continue, while fatal errors terminate nonzero; logs/TUI report counts.

CLI supports configuration display, plain logs versus TUI, incremental/rebuild modes and nonzero error exits.
Supports image sharing with dynamic OpenGraph images/SEO metadata and embedding through a public SDK.

Gallery offers GIF filtering and the release lists an Android GIF drawable dependency; exact animation performance is not measured.
Choose white, dark or dark AMOLED themes, primary/accent colours, navigation styling and a separate media-viewer theme.

Move to TrashBin, restore individually/all, or permanently delete; help says only images deleted inside Phimpme appear here.

UI defines per-provider upload progress/success/retry notifications and ZIP operation progress/completion.

Local gallery and editing precede optional connected-service sharing; official store text claims the project does not store users' data.

Gettext catalogues translate runtime/CLI messages and LANG selects the locale when compiled translation support is installed. v2.11.0 adds Japanese; inspected Japanese messages include help/errors and command-option diagnostics. This evidence establishes terminal-interface localization, not completeness of every Shredder GUI translation.
Scan file/directory arguments or stdin; normal execution produces reports/scripts rather than interactively deleting files.
Linux is the primary target and README points to distribution packages; other Unices compile with some optimizations unavailable.
rmlint --gui launches separately installed GUI dependencies; 2.11.0 requires Python 3.12/GTK 3.22 for the GUI.
No media import/catalogue copying is required; scans supplied filesystem paths.
Scan several file/directory roots in a run and rank their relative importance.
Default BLAKE2b content matching with alternative BLAKE3, SHA, MD5, Highway, Metro, Murmur and xxHash variants. 64-bit hashes are explicitly discouraged for duplicate safety.
'--paranoid or --algorithm=paranoid compares file bytes rather than relying on digest equality.

'--merge-directories aggregates matching file content into duplicate trees. Default equality disregards names/layout and empty-file contents; --honour-dir-layout requires matching relative layout. Marked experimental in tutorial.
Rank by root order, mtime, basename/path alphabetic order, depth, basename length, path/name regex and inner/outer hardlink counts. Criteria chain provides deterministic tie-breaks; default is pOma.
Paths after // are preferred, but preference alone does not protect every tagged copy. --keep-all-tagged protects all, and --must-match-tagged limits candidates to groups represented in those roots.
Configure inclusive min/max sizes with decimal/binary units; empty files are separate lint by default. 2.11 adds a directory st_size lower-bound flag useful for Ceph rbytes.

Require same/different basename, extension, extensionless name, parent directory or relative path in addition to content matching; optional case-insensitivity is ASCII-only, not fuzzy-image/name matching.

Scan files newer than a timestamp or updated stamp file, retaining size siblings as comparison candidates. Separate mtime-window requires content-equal files to lie within a time window, which can transitively chain groups.
Clamp start/end by byte offset, percentage or factor to compare part of each file, e.g. excluding a fixed header. Results are partial-content matches, not exact whole-file duplicates.
Limit depth, mount crossing, hidden files and permission eligibility; follow symlinks, ignore them or compare their target strings. Loop detection is documented when following links.
Use find or another selector to pipe paths, including NUL-separated paths, rather than a built-in arbitrary include/exclude regex engine.
Default considers hardlinks; --keep-hardlinked preserves aliases of the original, while --no-hardlinked considers only the highest-ranked member and ignores other aliases.

Separate read/write/clear xattr controls cache checksum and timestamp; requires filesystem support and write access for writes, and relies on mtime to invalidate stale values. Cross-endian portability depends on algorithm.

Replay saved JSON to change ranking/filter/output or merge previous runs without rehashing. It does not discover new paths and ignores entries whose mtime changed; hashing/traversal options no longer apply.
Emit JSON including optional linewise records, CSV, shell/Python scripts, fdupes-compatible blocks, unique paths, timestamps and summaries; multiple outputs can coexist.
Unique-path formatter emits nonduplicate paths; --hash-unmatched completes hashes for same-size nonduplicates, while --hash-uniques hashes every traversed file, including unique sizes.
Generated scripts can replace duplicates with hardlinks; they require same filesystem and can fall back to symlinks when configured.
Script handlers can replace duplicates with links to the selected original.

Supports reflink copy or kernel-verified FIDEDUPERANGE clone on capable filesystems. Standalone --dedupe checks equality, shares extents and preserves destination metadata; optional readonly mode targets Btrfs snapshots with root.
Configure comma-separated handlers; smart link tries clone, reflink, hardlink then symlink. Default script handler is permanent remove, not trash.
Normal scan does not delete files; scripts can be inspected/edited first, Python output provides dry run, and GUI explicitly distinguishes dry versus destructive execution.
Generated shell script prompts before proceeding unless bypassed; GUI guide says files are rechecked before deletion and presents editable keep/delete marks.
Tutorial shows a custom handler invoking separately installed trash-cli; OS trash is not the normal built-in remove handler.
Shell handlers receive duplicate and original paths; generated Python scripts can be customized for specialized actions.
Dedicated selectable empty-file lint type, independently configurable from duplicate content matching.
Finds empty directories including nested empty trees.
badlinks identifies symbolic links without valid targets.
badids identifies files with unresolved UID/GID ownership.
Optional lint type identifies binaries retaining debug symbols; it is not enabled by default.
'--equal returns status indicating whether multiple files or directory contents match and accepts paranoid mode; directory layout is not automatically part of equality.
'--hash operates like a multithreaded checksum tool over paths or stdin using supported hash algorithms.
'--is-reflink distinguishes reflinks, hardlinks, identical paths, different devices, symlinks, unavailable extent information and inline extents through exit statuses.
Configurable worker count defaults to 16; setting it to one does not make the entire program single-threaded.
'--limit-mem caps memory for hashing/paranoid comparison, not total process RSS; path/index and other overhead remain.
Optional FIEMAP reads physical file extents to optimize disk access; disabled automatically where unavailable.
Shredder streams CLI JSON into a tree while scanning and allows editing keep/delete decisions after scan.
Filter path text plus size ranges, mtime and twin count; generate scripts for all results or only visible results.
GUI charts duplicate distribution across scanned directories and shows a running affected-byte count during script execution.

PiGallery2 is explicitly a photo-gallery website with a responsive interface for phone, tablet and desktop browsers; Docker is the recommended server deployment rather than a native client-app distribution.
Detailed feature manual explicitly lists internationalization with full translation support; it does not enumerate every available language or establish complete translation of every current string.
Feature manual describes a local filter panel that further narrows the current directory or search results, distinct from submitting the full structured query language.
Browser interface points at an existing photo tree and is intended for low-resource hardware; speed is a project claim, not a measured benchmark.
Docker is official/recommended; native Node.js installation is possible but unsupported.
Shows the original folder hierarchy recursively without mandatory reimport; database is a cache, not the authority for source organization.
Original media folder needs read permission; derived assets go to separate writable temp folder. Explicit upload mode is an exception that adds files.
Cached-folder timeout and reindex sensitivity control scans; never mode indexes only unseen folders or explicit jobs, and scheduled default indexing processes changes only.
Skip folder names/paths/globs, folders containing marker files, or photo/video filename globs; matching is case-sensitive and default excludes common trash directories.
Directory navigation includes recursive subfolders; optional flatten button lists all descendants, with documented same-path limitation.
Phone/tablet/desktop grid renders on demand while scrolling and prioritizes visible thumbnails; no stronger virtualized-row guarantee is inferred.
Fullscreen viewer includes EXIF panel, captions/face overlays, low-resolution placeholder before full image and keyboard/swipe navigation.
Lightbox can load original resolution when zoomed or cached previews are too small.
Configurable interval (default five seconds), loop slideshow and separate video loop controls.
Generates a looping display link for a directory or search, suitable for kiosk apps; recurring-date queries can produce anniversary frames.
Configurable automatic theme mode, selected theme and custom CSS theme definitions.
Direct formats MP4/WebM/OGV/OGG; other listed formats such as MKV/MOV/AVI require conversion.
Produces MP4 or WebM, with configurable bitrate, height, FPS, codecs, CRF, preset and custom input/output flags; thumbnails use ffmpeg/ffprobe.
Current config enables pairing still image and companion video by Content Identifier metadata; pinned-branch feature may postdate manifest release.
Feature list marks DNG/ARW support dependent on container libvips build; not a universal camera RAW decoder guarantee.
HEIC is listed with container/libvips compatibility caveat and browser/Sharp conversion requirements.
Current supported-photo list includes AVIF with browser/Sharp capability caveat.
