animateGif converts GIF to animated WebP and defaults on.
Viewer displays EXIF, tags/keywords, locations and GPS read from files.
captionFirstNaming optionally displays IPTC 120 caption instead of filenames; not metadata-writing support.
Reads Adobe XMP face regions, draws bounding boxes and exposes people browsing/search. Does not perform automatic face detection/recognition according to inspected evidence.
Exact/wildcard and negated filters, AND/OR, comparator ranges and n-of expressions; autocomplete suggests files/directories/captions/places/people/keywords.
file_name, directory, caption and any_text queries support exact or wildcard forms; directory glob /* includes the directory and all descendants.
Date ranges and relative recurring windows such as last four days every week/month/year or a shifted past period are documented.
Supports equality, ranges, comparisons and negation on ratings read from media; does not establish rating editing.
Resolution query uses megapixels with ranges/comparators; portrait/landscape orientation queries also supported.
person name queries and person-count numeric ranges search imported face metadata; faces tab access and starring require configurable roles.
keyword searches can drive logical albums; FAQ suggests assigning unique keywords in external Lightroom/digiKam rather than editing them here.
Position searches city/state/country; distance forms such as 5-km-from:(New York) query nearby photos.
Any search query can be saved as a logical album; .pg2conf is used for saved search/config behavior, distinct from conventional database-only manual albums.
Empty .order_[ORDER].pg2conf overrides only that folder, choosing ascending/descending name/date or random; not recursive.
Photo/search default grouping is date; configurable timestamp-offset handling uses local wall-clock time or global time, assuming UTC where offset missing.
Uses OpenStreetMap or configured Mapbox/custom tile URLs, with photo markers and clickable full-view photos; Mapbox requires token.
Displays GPX paths and differentiates activities such as running/flying with colors/icons; configurable path bending handles long flight segments.
On-demand/scheduled compression removes too-close or near-collinear points using distance, temporal spacing and deviation thresholds.
Displays .md files near gallery/map; pg-date comments attach sections to dates, enabling narrative photo presentation.
Share a folder with optional descendants or search results; effective access intersects share query with creator media/directory permissions, not merely opening-page scope.
Links optionally require passwords, and instance policy can require passwords for all shares.
Authentication/user management configurable; roles include Limited Guest, Guest, User, Admin and Developer, with sharing users constrained separately.
Admins manage settings/duplicate view; Users can share/list faces/random links. Per-user/global media and directory allow/block queries are independent; block wins and unavailable paths return 404.
Issuer/client/scopes/claims, allowed email domains, optional account creation and default role are configurable; strict linking can bind identity and cap eligible roles.
Disabled by default, minimum role Admin by default; optional .uploader.pg2conf requirement whitelists target directories, with blocked extensions and per-file errors.
Upload validates plain filename/root containment and rejects existing path with FileAlreadyExists before writing; no claim of race-proof transactional writes.
Config enables zipped download of listed directory or search results.

Admin-only duplicate view groups equal name+size or creation-date+size and merges overlapping groups; default listing limit 1000. No hashes, byte comparison or perceptual similarity are used in examined method.
On-demand thumbnail/preview sizes default 320/540/1080/2160, persisted outside originals with visible-photo priority; more sizes trade CPU/storage for quality.
Thumbnail workers default to CPU count minus one with configurable concurrency cap; this is derivative processing, not a claim of parallel scanning or perceptual matching.
Schedules indexing, cover filling, photo/video conversion, GPX compression and temp cleanup with after-job dependencies, bounded database batches and retained progress history.
AutoUpdate polls for new photos/videos at configurable interval, default 60 seconds when enabled; not a filesystem event watcher.
Creates a URL serving a random photo, useful for external wallpaper/photo-frame applications and subject to user rights.

Separate server.js extensions receive lifecycle/config/REST hooks and limited photo UI buttons; configured dependency installation may run at initialization and repository discovery reads an online list.
Visitors browse the web gallery and administrators sign in to /dashboard for uploads, albums and configuration; setup is also browser-based.
README recommends published Docker/Compose images with the data directory mounted for database, settings, session secret and local photos; this is a web-server deployment.

README explicitly lists dashboard language switching as an application feature. Exact supported interface-language list is not specified in the inspected source; separate place-name language settings and translated README files are not treated as UI-localization evidence.
Admin/browser UI and public gallery run on an operator-controlled server; Docker image with persistent data mount is recommended.
README links a separate sign-up hosted service for creating galleries without maintaining a server; inspected material does not establish pricing or entitlement limits.
Wizard creates an administrator and chooses site/storage; everyday settings persist in database and can be changed without rebuilding containers or editing .env.
Dashboard photo page accepts selected/dropped batches, optionally targeted to an album; successfully processed photos join the selected album.
When duplicate handling is Skip, an already existing photo is added to the chosen album without uploading another file. Documentation does not specify the identity algorithm.
Storage guide explicitly says directly copied/uploaded backend files do not appear automatically and scanning/importing existing storage is planned.
Photo wall uses masonry presentation with filters/sorting; header can be embedded in the wall or fixed during scrolling.
README explicitly supports browsing by time; v1.2 release preserves mobile date-range controls while redesigning the header.
Viewer provides pan/zoom and tiled rendering for large images, not merely a precomputed thumbnail grid.
README photo-browsing feature list explicitly includes histograms.
Live/Motion assets play on hover or long press; v1.2 updates mobile gallery controls and accessible header behavior.
Admin table supports sorting/filtering, persistent visible-column choice, upload-date sorting and Shift-click range selection.
Organize albums and order photos inside them; batch Add to album skips items already in the target album.

Self-hosted titles generate slugs; numeric links redirect to current slug and historical slugs temporarily redirect. Renaming title alone keeps URL; editing/clearing frees the old slug for reassignment.
Upload queue extracts EXIF and shooting coordinates, generates previews and resolves locations.
Dashboard edits descriptive metadata; inspected guides do not establish embedded-file write-back.
Rating is explicitly editable alongside title and description in dashboard.

Privacy setting automatically strips location from future uploads; existing photos require individual/batch removal jobs and queue-completion confirmation. This is not a claim to remove every identifying field.
Documented image inputs include HEIC/HEIF alongside JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP and TIFF.
Matches image and MOV sharing basename; either upload order works and pairing can be retried in dashboard.
Supports embedded-video Motion Photos with hover/long-press playback; separate from image/MOV pair matching.
Choose MapLibre with built-in MapTiler data or Mapbox, requiring appropriate tokens unless a custom MapLibre style is supplied. Photos need existing GPS; enabling maps cannot invent coordinates.
Mapbox or Nominatim performs reverse geocoding separately from browser tile rendering; configurable language affects future lookups, and existing names require reindexing.
Custom MapLibre Style JSON can reference self-hosted tiles/fonts/sprites with browser CORS; Nominatim URL can target a self-hosted service/proxy. This is not a bundled offline basemap or geocoder.
README includes share previews; photo shares retain album access scope. Hidden-album membership restricts anonymous photo access even when the same photo also belongs to a public album.
Minimum six-character album password; visitors must unlock application access. External public image URLs remain outside this protection.
v1.2 release adds controls to disable gallery reactions; precise reaction types are not stated in inspected note.
Email/password is established at setup; GitHub OAuth requires configured client credentials and returned email matching an existing administrator, not arbitrary GitHub-user admin access.
Public viewer offers original downloads and dashboard selection supports batch download; exact archive format is not established by inspected guide.
Supports endpoint/bucket/region/prefix/credentials/path-style/CDN URL configuration with examples for AWS S3, R2, OSS, COS and MinIO; browser direct uploads need CORS and multipart ETag exposure.
Uses OpenList API token/root and configurable upload/delete/metadata endpoints; remote permissions and expiring download URLs affect accessibility.
Dashboard adds/edits/selects local, S3 and OpenList schemes. Changing active scheme affects new uploads only; this is not multiple independent user-selectable catalogues.
Remote storage can provide a separate CDN read base URL; R2 S3 upload endpoint must not be confused with its public image domain.
EXIF, thumbnails, locations and Live Photo pairing run after uploads; dashboard reports task progress/errors and failed-task retries.
Selected photos can be reindexed, location names rebuilt after language changes and Live Photo pairing retried without claiming a full user-data reset.
Dashboard exposes task errors/retries, live logs and activity; logs are not documented as a crash-recovery file operation journal.

Update guide requires stopping container and backing up complete data, Compose, legacy environment and separately stored local/remote media. Rollback restores pre-upgrade database and files, not just an older image.
Migrations run automatically; current runtime image has no shell/package manager, and older manual in-container migration instructions no longer apply.
Dashboard accepts custom tracking scripts in head/body; operators control the added privacy implications.
Runs on a home/server host and exposes a browser interface to authenticated devices; Docker Compose is the recommended setup.
Prebuilt application image is configured with PostgreSQL/Redis and mounted photos; data persists outside containers.
Web-based filtering and full-screen viewing work from logged-in desktop/tablet/mobile devices.
Official site links a Google Play client providing access to an existing server; it is not a standalone gallery or currently documented backup client.
Official site links an App Store client requiring a Photonix server.
Mount existing photo storage instead of copying into a proprietary container; database/thumbnails remain separate from originals.
Recursive inotify watches respond to completed writes, added files, directory additions, moves/renames and deletions. Per-LibraryPath watch_for_changes settings enable/disable watches.
Multiple libraries coexist in one installation and users switch through the account menu; CLI assigns accounts to libraries.
Separate usernames/passwords support private user libraries and administrator-configured shared libraries.
create_library and create_user management commands provision additional accounts/library access; initial setup may use createsuperuser.
Viewer exposes camera/time metadata and analysis results by scrolling, including colors, objects and map location.
Uses aperture, shutter speed, GPS and capture date/time as searchable information; source adds camera, lens, ISO and focal-length constraints.
User-assigned concepts coexist with camera-derived and automatically classified tags; multiple tags per photo enable combined filtering.
Queries resolve tag IDs or case-insensitive tag-name substrings; multiple filters are applied to the photo queryset.
Supports camera/lens IDs, aperture/ISO/focal-length ranges, exposure values, flash and metering/drive/shooting modes.
rating filters apply an inclusive star-rating range; this proves filtering, not the location or format of rating writes.
Parses month names/abbreviations, day ordinals and years into capture-date constraints; when a month lacks a year, selects the current or most recent applicable year.
A fixed color palette is compared with a 32x32 resampled image using weighted HSV distance; results retain sufficiently significant color proportions.
Object classifier runs within Photonix, stores bounding boxes and uses detected area as a significance signal; models are not a hosted Google API.
Classifies style labels such as geometric, minimalist and noir, distinct from literal object labels.
Object/face/style/color and location analysis run inside the deployment; configuration enables/disables individual classifiers to manage CPU/RAM.
MTCNN detects face boxes and landmarks, creating initially unknown location-specific face tags.
Aligned face crops generate 128-value FaceNet embeddings; Euclidean similarity thresholds match identities across images.

Unmatched faces form conservatively grouped Unknown person tags during import. Annoy nearest-neighbor indexes rebuild at five-minute intervals when needed, with direct comparison for newly added faces.
Users label automatically grouped unknown people with names, allowing personalized recognition without training a full new face model.
UI shows bounding boxes and supports approval, rejection and editing automatic face tags; documentation describes merging groups as the preferred correction path.
Uses World Borders polygons and GeoNames top-1000 cities locally with no API calls; returns nearest city only within 10 km. Coarse coastlines may miss beach locations.
Official feature overview documents viewing geographic location on a map; no offline tile-cache guarantee is inferred from offline geocoding.

Compares timestamps and other metadata to group camera RAW, camera JPEG and edited versions; latest inferred edit becomes the preview while other versions remain accessible. This is not exact hash deduplication.
Disabling an analysis type stops processing but newly imported photos remain queued and are analyzed when it is re-enabled.
Thumbnails and cache data are outside the originals' directory; v0.24.0 addresses corrupt-image thumbnail crashes.
Mounted originals and local classifiers avoid mandatory third-party image upload; operating a remotely accessible server remains the user's responsibility.
Official mobile-app section explicitly says automatic camera-roll uploading is a feature to come; present apps provide server access.
Sharing-online section asks users to wait until the feature is fully ready; it must not be counted as existing public-link sharing.
Official site describes phone-controlled TV/client presentations as future work, not an available feature.
Official site explicitly says limited video-file support is intended soon; current documented scope focuses on photography.
Current grouping chooses the inferred latest edit; manually preferring an older edit is described as upcoming.
User/library guide states management UI is yet to be developed and directs administrators to CLI provisioning.
Website discusses read-only/read-write roles and invitations in future tense; inspected current user guide establishes membership but not all UI/permission workflows.
Central server/library can be used from several devices without copying catalogue databases onto each client.
Web-based photo browsing, search, tagging and export UI with selectable themes.
Recommended supported deployment mounts pictures, config/database and thumbnails separately; default port is 6363.
README/FAQ document Windows standalone server and desktop client distributions; non-Docker server builds are not published for every release.
Universal macOS desktop client plus standalone server packages are documented, subject to release availability and dependency setup.
Linux standalone client/server packages supplement Docker; 64-bit OS is required.
At startup scans the configured photo tree and extracts metadata from existing originals; files need not be imported into a proprietary store.
Server scans one top-level tree; documented Docker workaround mounts several shares/volumes as distinct subfolders beneath /pictures.
Preserves server folder organization; desktop Save Locally copies basket images under the matching client-relative folder tree.
Creates OS-level watchers per folder, automatically indexing added/updated images after the initial metadata pass.
After initial indexing, changes are processed without manually rebuilding the whole catalogue; initial metadata pass prioritizes recently modified files.
A .nomedia file in a folder causes that folder to be skipped by indexing; this is scan exclusion, not an encrypted vault.
Move or copy images between folders through the application.
README specifies image deletion through a trashcan folder; automatic retention duration and restoration guarantees are not documented in inspected manuals.
Thumbnail browser supports selection for keyword edits or basket addition, while individual images show properties and AI tags.
README identifies browsing grouped by date and release 4.5.3 updates advanced date-range UI.
README explicitly supports full-text multi-phrase, partial-word retrieval; exact filename/path tokenization is not specified in the inspected feature section.
Find by keyword tags and explicitly filter images with no keyword tags.
Advanced search filters camera/lens make/model and orientation.
Advanced search includes date ranges, with a redesigned date-range selector in release 4.5.3.
Advanced search explicitly lists file-size criteria.
Search objects, detected faces and identified faces; anonymous face detection and named-person matching are distinct.
README explicitly lists visual-similarity search. It does not establish exact hashes or duplicate-removal support.
Indexer extracts resolution, capture timestamp and EXIF metadata into the searchable catalogue.
MetadataExtractor-based IPTC keyword indexing supports the documented tagging/search workflow.
Add keywords to selected images, an entire basket or the current photo in the properties screen.
Selected images and basket contents can receive keyword operations together; pending additions/removals are combined in the background queue.
ExifTool applies queued keyword and other metadata operations to underlying originals without re-encoding JPEG image pixels. Originals are modified, so this is not read-only storage.
Pending metadata operations survive restart and are processed later; batching coalesces updates to reduce disk work.
Runs face detection after thumbnails are generated, using lower-resolution derived images for analysis.
Creates unknown people from distinctive face traits and matches future faces to the existing person; latest README says this now runs locally/offline.
Click a detected face to name its associated person; same-named different people need disambiguating names.
Assigning an existing name to another unknown person prompts a merge of face data, handling differences such as pose; split/reject workflows are not established here.
Recognized objects/faces appear as special icon-marked tags beside ordinary keywords; README also lists image-colour classification.
Current README explicitly replaces formerly used Microsoft Azure Face API with local/offline detection and recognition; older Azure lineage must not be treated as a current requirement.
Set a processing time window and CPU throttling to limit intensive face/object jobs on shared NAS hardware.
Generates browsing previews separately after metadata indexing and analyzes those thumbnails rather than originals.
SYNO_THUMBS uses Synology @eaDir layout so existing DSM thumbnails are reused and newly created ones can be used by Photo Station.
README lists DNG, CR2, ORF and NEF alongside JPG/PNG/TIFF/WebP/BMP; decoder support beyond these examples is not enumerated.
HEIC is explicitly included in supported formats and indexing description.
Displays locations when image metadata provides them; offline basemap/geocoding or location-write support is not established.
Collect images from search results into reusable baskets for keywording, download/export or WordPress publication.
With authentication enabled users get a private My Basket and can expose a shared basket to all users. Without auth, anyone can alter any basket.
Enable authentication in system settings and restart to obtain registered accounts, persistent user-associated baskets and user-tag operation attribution.
ReadOnly cannot modify keywords or download high-resolution images; User can; Admin manages settings/accounts. First user becomes admin and last admin cannot be demoted.
Download/export basket images, including ZIP, or Save Locally in the desktop client to mirror server paths for external editing.
Basket export can generate files at different resolutions for publication/email; this is export processing, not a general in-place editor.
Exports optionally add watermarks for social/email use; standalone installation requires fonts for watermark rendering.
Basket images upload directly to a configured WordPress site; requires a separate WordPress JWT Authentication plugin and site/server credential setup.
README places cropping and colour adjustments in planned/in-progress enhancements, separate from existing lossless metadata and export processing.
README explicitly lists image de-duplication as in progress; existing visual-similarity search is not counted as duplicate cleanup.
Roadmap says additional formats and possibly video; no current playback claim is made.
Current workflow requires manually copying/rclone-syncing edits back; automatic return synchronization is explicitly future work.
README roadmap names selection/upload to Alamy; not established as available.
User IDs are associated with some operations, but the roles manual explicitly says audit reporting will come in a future release.
Host the site on a PHP server using SQLite 3 rather than the separate Pro edition's MySQL option.
Browser upload, image detail, discovery and authenticated management pages are built in.
README lists multi-image selection and drag-and-drop as current features.
Ctrl+V workflow sends base64 image content; parse endpoint validates MIME before storing it.
Logged-in users can fetch supported image URLs; URL handler checks an image extension and rejects an already known digest-derived ID.
Original and thumbnail paths are created below imgs/YYYY/MM using generated digest-derived filenames.
Uses a truncated MD5 as image ID. URL/paste duplicates are rejected; multipart upload reuses the known record ID after writing/renaming the upload, so this is not guaranteed disk-level deduplication.
Multipart allowlist includes GIF, JPG/JPEG, PNG, BMP and WebP. This evidence does not establish RAW or video playback.
Admin settings enable/disable visitor uploads; uploads distinguish administrator versus visitor records.
Configure guest daily upload count and backend file-size limit; upload constructor checks visitor IP quota. v2.31 fixes the size-setting bug.
UI/API can return URL, HTML, Markdown and BBCode; detail view exposes copy controls and direct download.
Multipart upload returns IDs, paths, URL, thumbnail, dimensions and for newly inserted files a deletion URL; discovery API serializes gallery records.
Upload creates a 290×175 thumbnail where appropriate; small images can use the original URL instead.
README explicitly lists image cropping alongside automatic thumbnail generation; crop variants and metadata preservation are not specified there.

README lists batch compression; configured TinyPNG processing accepts JPEG/PNG, skips previously compressed records and overwrites the local original with downloaded output. Multiple configured API keys can be selected.

ModerateContent classifies a public image URL and stores the rating; already classified images are skipped, and batch helper selects up to five unknown entries. This is not local inference or face recognition.
Discovery controller provides all, GIF, views and large-image categories; category query semantics beyond those labels are not inferred.
Uses 16-image pages; public discovery caps the pagination count at 160 entries, while management has its own filters and count.
Management accepts a start/end date and applies it to upload timestamps, separately for all, administrator or visitor records—not EXIF capture dates.
Management can query numeric ID, 16-character image ID or uploading IP, and filter suspicious/adult-classified records.
Image page lists dimensions, MIME, extension, upload time, file size and view count; EXIF capture metadata editing is not established.
Detail page displays stored view count and discovery offers a views category.
Stores uploader IP, user agent, date, admin/visitor type, original client filename and moderation status.
A valid deletion token authorizes removal without logging in; separate ID-based deletion requires login and both remove original, thumbnail and database entries.
Image view includes a comment.html file if present; this is an integration hook, not evidence of a built-in comment database.
Free README leaves external storage unchecked and free navigation only activates localhost. Pro's advertised support is separately classified.
README advertises multiple external storage backends, MySQL, no advertising and professional support in separate ImgURL Pro; these are not verified free-source features.
README marks online update unfinished, but source navigation exposes a version-upgrade page. Its completeness was not established; not counted as present.

Slink provides its upload, collections, share management and administrative interface through its SvelteKit web frontend backed by Symfony; Docker hosts the service and does not imply native desktop/mobile application builds.
README explicitly supports uploading multiple image files in parallel, with progress tracking and error handling for each file.

README and introduction explicitly list English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Polish, Ukrainian and Chinese user interfaces. This is interface localization, not a claim about search-language or model support.
Symfony/SvelteKit server with browser upload, management and sharing; container settings and persistent mounts are documented.
Environment variables configure Docker/Compose deployments; local images require a host mount at /app/slink/images for persistence.
Programmatically created shares start unpublished; UI Copy Link creates/reuses and publishes atomically. Unpublishing returns 404; holding a URL alone is insufficient if its share is revoked.
Each share can set/change/remove a password; stored password is hashed and successful unlock creates a short-lived cookie.
Expiry timestamp can be set or cleared; passing it auto-revokes access.
/shares lists owned image and collection shares; filters type, expired/has/no-expiry and password protection, with free-text underlying-name search.
Shortening is enabled by default; generated code length defaults to 8 and is clamped between 4 and 32 characters.
Group images into a collection and share via one link; collection shares auto-publish upon creation, unlike API-created image shares.
Instance settings separately require sign-in for media shares or collection shares; anonymous access to public routes is independently configurable.
Explore shows images users have made publicly visible; admin may disallow unauthenticated public-route access or force uploads public.
Parallel multi-file upload tracks progress and per-file errors; maximum image size is configurable and chunk size defaults to 2 MB within a 1–25 MB range.
Disabled by default and admin-enabled; guests use drag/drop or file selection, uploads are public, and guests cannot edit/delete submitted images.
Detects duplicate images during upload and notifies the user; enabled by default. Inspected docs do not specify hash/perceptual algorithm or a batch cleanup tool.
JPEG compression quality is configurable from 1 to 100, default 80.
Optional setting converts all uploads to WebP, AVIF or JPEG; animated conversion is separately opt-in and disabled by default.
IMAGE_STRIP_EXIF_METADATA defaults true; administrators can override at runtime. No preservation of untouched original metadata is implied.
HEIC and TIFF are accepted but converted to JPG before saving for compatibility.
AVIF is a supported upload format and configurable conversion target.
Supported list includes SVG, BMP, ICO, PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF; broad image support is not evidence of video support.
Hierarchical tag management has a dedicated management page and tag search capabilities.
README explicitly couples nested tags with search; arbitrary boolean/saved-query semantics are not documented.
Upload history offers list/grid views of the user's uploads.
Users save public images for later access; distinguished from changing ownership or copying originals.
Users can leave comments on publicly visible images.
Notifies users of interactions with their images; specific delivery channels are not established.
README explicitly supports both light and dark application modes; interface translation is inventoried separately under deployment.localization.
Email/password registration and login with configurable signup and admin approval; default environment reference requires approval before sign-in.
Google/Authentik/Keycloak/Authelia/Pocket ID presets or custom OIDC; matches sub then verified email, uses S256 PKCE, and stores client configuration encrypted.
OIDC providers can inherit/allow/block registration and inherit/require/auto-approve new accounts independently of global signup policy; existing users are unaffected.
Bearer-authenticated POST /api/external/upload accepts multipart images and returns URL/metadata; login-protected endpoint exports ShareX config.
Keys have optional expiry, are displayed once and can be revoked; docs warn they permit uploads on the user's behalf.
Slink generates a .sxcu configuration for the separately installed ShareX client to automate screenshot uploads with an API key.
Configured network share credentials store originals and transformed caches in automatically created slink/images and slink/cache directories.
Supports AWS or custom endpoint/path-style S3 storage; AWS can use instance IAM role instead of static keys, but role mode is ignored for custom providers.
Storage layouts separate uploaded images from transformed/cache objects locally, on SMB and under the S3 cache prefix.
Admin dashboard provides statistics/analytics and storage-consumption metrics; documentation does not substantiate throughput benchmarks.
Administrators manage image content/visibility, users, storage and settings; stored settings override corresponding environment variables.
Security guide explicitly says built-in rate limiting and brute-force protection are absent and recommends a reverse proxy for them.
Commands import, update, generate-db, verify and batch operate on explicit files/directories with debug output.
Import accepts one/multiple source files/directories and a destination, preserving source placement by default and using embedded metadata to choose paths.
Configurable folder placeholders include strftime date parts, city/state/country, camera make/model and album, with compound variables and ordered fallback choices.
Filename templates combine capture timestamp, original name, title/album and extension, remove missing placeholders and allow lowercase/default or uppercase output.
Prefers DateTimeOriginal/CreateDate/ModifyDate then filesystem times; GPS and camera metadata drive folder naming. Missing location goes to a configurable fallback.
Uses XMP title/album/GPS and QuickTime/H264 timestamps for video/audio; README distinguishes photo Title from video/audio DisplayName and read-only Composite GPS.
update changes album, title, capture time or location through ExifTool and recalculates filenames/folders; it changes real files rather than only catalogue fields.
Import/update accept date or date-time overrides; import override replaces existing timestamp data, not merely fills missing values.
Import/update location names are resolved to coordinates and written into supported media metadata; supplied import location overwrites existing location.
'--album-from-folder derives album metadata from input folders and template fallbacks can prioritize album over place; this is file organization, not virtual shared albums.

With ExifTool 13.13+ geolocation database, current default derives city/region/country from coordinates and resolves names without a MapQuest key. Availability is tested against installed ExifTool database.
When a MapQuest key exists, name/coordinate lookups still call its API; README marks this deprecated and intended for removal, with optional English names.
Location lookup caches results in JSON and reuses a nearby cached location within a requested 3 km radius, reducing repeated lookups but potentially coarsening naming.
Computes SHA-256 and skips an existing matching stored path; if cache says a match but that file is missing, import proceeds. --allow-duplicates overrides normal skipping.
Reads complete files in 64 KiB blocks into SHA-256 and maps hash to stored path; no perceptual similarity or byte-by-byte postverification is established.
hash.json retains signatures and locations between runs; a hash maps to one recorded path rather than a full duplicate group catalogue.
Repeated --exclude-regex switches and named config exclusions skip matching file/folder paths, including examples for NAS artifacts and thumbnails.

'--dry-run reports file/metadata/plugin actions instead of media mutation; code guards hash/location writes. It is not a completely no-write process because directory/cache initialization can still occur.

'--trash calls send2trash on original sources. Important source caveat: this call is not conditional on process_file returning a successful destination, so a skipped import can still trigger source trash.
verify iterates hash/path records, reports missing files and recomputes content hashes to flag mismatches; it detects problems but does not repair corrupted files.
generate-db --source rebuilds hash.json for an existing library; resetting a baseline differs from verifying the old baseline.
Storage implementation provides timestamped copies of existing hash.json; this is backup of small integrity metadata, not copies of all media.
Configured plugins expose before/after/batch hooks, JSON state and logging; a failing before-hook can prevent import.

Bundled optional plugin queues imported photos for Google upload via batch, requiring a Google API project, OAuth client and stored credentials. Guide is legacy and current Google API compatibility was not independently established.
README explicitly relies on external inotify/cron/Automator/Hazel to invoke CLI when media arrives; Elodie itself is not documented as a persistent watcher.
README requires ExifTool 11.50+ for HEIC support; this proves organization/metadata handling, not image decoding or playback.
README explicitly includes DNG/NEF and common video/audio alongside JPEG, with media-specific metadata precedence; no built-in playback is implied.
GUI guide describes dragging Finder photos to create an album that writes EXIF and moves files, but calls the GUI unfinished and uses obsolete build tooling; manifest has no current release.
Browser frontend accesses the microservices via hypermedia APIs; intended for organizational/editorial image workflows.
Runs separately deployable services with Elasticsearch and AWS infrastructure; local setup provisions LocalStack resources.
Requires S3 buckets and DynamoDB resources; originals and derivative images are server-managed rather than a local folder browser.
APIs cover image ingestion/search, metadata, exports, collections, usage and auth; internal, readonly and syndication machine keys have distinct scopes.
Upload service prepares presigned uploads, accepts images with uploader/identifiers/timestamps/filename and exposes per-image/per-user upload status.
Loader exposes enqueueDerivativeImage with derivativeOfMediaIds, preserving an explicit relationship to source assets.
Media API supplies original-file download and width-specific crop-export downloads; crop links are configurable.
Structured fields include title, description, copyright, credit, supplier reference, source, photographer/byline, category, subject, people-in-image, photoshoot and cropper identity.
Query parser explicitly supports filename; this is managed-asset metadata search rather than browsing filesystem paths.
Supports field:value, quoted phrases, leading '-' negation, has:/is: conditions, # labels, collection: hierarchy terms and nested usages@field filters.
Distinguishes taken, uploaded/date and added dates; supports comparison operators, today/yesterday, multiple date formats and API since/until relative durations.
fileType parser normalizes jpg/jpeg and tif/tiff plus png to MIME constraints.
Searches location/city/state/country; the in alias expands across these descriptive fields. This is not a map or reverse-geocoding claim.
person query aliases peopleInImage metadata; no automatic facial recognition is implied.
Nested usages constraints include status, platform, section, publication, orderedBy and content references; request filters also cover usage and syndication status.
Search provides offset/length and configurable orderBy; documented defaults are ten results ordered newest upload first.

useAISearch plus enabled server configuration embeds query text through Bedrock and combines vector/text ranking; default vector weight is 0.85 and metadata/usage filters constrain the candidate pool.

AI similar:imageId uses the accessible source image's Cohere Embed v4 image vector for filtered nearest-neighbor retrieval. Missing vectors yield no results; combining image and text ranking signals is rejected.
Lambda sends images to real Bedrock and stores vectors in S3 Vectors even in LocalStack development; query embedding calls are likewise remote.
AI-search controller caches normalized query embeddings/futures so simultaneous equivalent queries share a remote call; zero-length polling skips Bedrock/KNN work.
SQS-fed embedding work supports retries/dead-letter behavior; documented backfill selects unembedded, non-soft-deleted assets.
Ingestion extracts IPTC into source metadata and maps key fields into editable/searchable primary metadata.
Ingestion preserves source XMP metadata in the database before configurable classification/cleaning.
Configuration defines collapsible domain sections with string/integer/datetime/select fields, controlled vocabularies, validation and searchable aliases without modifying application code.
Selected images show common values or Multiple values; saving applies per-image updates. Opt-in string edit modes support overwrite, prefix or suffix against each existing value.
Displays/edits usage categories, agency suppliers, publications/creators and required restriction text; unknown rights are explicit and some categories force restrictions.
Configured UI can show payable, all-use, news/sport eligibility and supplier markers, based on deployment-specific rights rules rather than generic image availability.
Configured templates preview their replacement usage-rights category in a locked editor and allow applying or cancelling without prematurely changing existing rights.

ImageProcessor/MetadataCleaner interfaces enable configured Scala pipelines for agency detection, license assignment, credits and house-style normalization; custom implementations require integration, not a generic AI model.
Includes Guardian hardcoded and runtime-configured providers for photographer/illustrator lists and Creative Commons options; additional sources can implement the provider trait.
Collections have root/child/grandchild hierarchy. Root creation currently requires the API, not Kahuna UI.
Cropper verifies source ownership URI, image validity and bounds using oriented dimensions, then generates/stores crop exports separately from originals.
Crop creation yields master/additional sizings; optimized download API accepts width, height and quality parameters.
Crop exports refer to a source image, have separate asset/download records and can be removed via crop permissions without a source rewrite in the inspected controller.
Each generated crop records authenticated identity, request time and specification. This is derivative provenance, not a durable crash-recovery file-action journal.

Uploads original TIFF and creates mandatory JPEG thumbnails plus optional optimized PNG; layered TIFF handling picks the extracted first image/layer for the preview rather than providing a complete multipage viewer.
Usage records connect images to articles/editorial systems or print issue/page/layout/publication details, with pending/published/removed state resolution.
Current API exposes supplier usage, image usage and quota-count/quota-for-image endpoints for contractual accounting.
Aggregation endpoint computes a date histogram for a chosen field and optional query.
Rights tests specify edit permission or ownership; crop deletion uses a dedicated permission. Machine API tiers are internal, readonly or syndication-specific.
Media API exposes per-partner image syndication and search can filter syndication status; downstream commercial integrations are deployment-specific.
Current routes distinguish soft-deleted metadata, ordinary delete, explicit hard-delete and undelete. Retention period and complete recovery semantics are not documented by these routes.
Loader exposes images/restore calling restoreFromReplica; exact operator workflow/backup completeness remains unverified.

Administrator script consumes image IDs and Internal API credentials, records last processed ID and separate success/error lists. Documentation explicitly says no mass-deletion UI; logs are not an atomic pre-operation journal.
Separate frontend/backend application for personal photo storage, team image sharing and web/blog image hosting.
Runtime requirements list JDK 1.8, MySQL 5.7+ and Redis; README recommends compiled integrated packages for deployment.
README provides app/database services, persistent data volumes and separate public frontend/backend addresses.

README explicitly offers a Windows desktop client downloadable from the project website and usable with both open-source and paid Core servers. This is a separate companion distribution, not the Java server's web UI or proof of its packaged source availability.

README explicitly offers a Mac desktop client usable with both editions. This records the separately distributed client, not native execution of the Java server as a gallery; current companion compatibility was not tested.
README explicitly limits the mini-program to paid Core and says it cannot currently connect to the open-source edition.
Open-source list includes Alibaba OSS, UpYun USS, Qiniu KODO, Tencent COS, NetEase NOS and AWS S3 protocol, alongside local storage and FTP.
FTP is explicitly listed among the open-source edition's storage sources; transport encryption is not specified.
Branch source implements authenticated PUT, MKCOL, DELETE and proxy GET for a configured WebDAV provider, but README/release do not establish packaged open-source availability.
Upload images by drag/drop or pasting screenshots with Ctrl+V; supports multiple images and guest/user management.
Newline-separated URLs are processed server-side, with a configurable referer, per-guest/user count limit and counts for failures/excess URLs.
Source exposes uploadChunkFile and processFile/merge endpoints for web and client routes; this establishes branch support, not guaranteed 20240319 package parity or restart-resume semantics.

README lists account-level duplicate checking on upload; upload endpoint accepts optional MD5. Full comparison/verification semantics are not established, so this is not claimed as byte-verified library cleanup.
README advertises timed temporary image storage and upload methods accept a day value; cleanup timing, provider removal and cache expiry are not established.
README documents personal album browsing and image-information cards.
Album and image queries accept page number/size and return total counts with selected rows.
Gallery controller creates a titled set of image references, supports editing membership/title and lists/deletes galleries by user/admin context.
Gallery membership stores per-image notes along with URL/name references; embedded original-file metadata is not modified by the inspected controller.
Rename action changes the recorded idname for a stored image identifier; physical object-key renaming is not established.
selectPhoto passes a nonempty searchname into the image query; ordinary users are constrained to their own user ID.
Query accepts start/stop times and rejects reversed ranges; whether dates are capture EXIF or upload timestamps is not established here.
Admins can filter by storage source, username/user type, own-versus-all and violation flag, with ascending/descending order selection.
README explicitly lists SVG among accepted image formats; this does not establish raster editing or thumbnail rendering of SVG.
README explicitly names WebP and ICO in addition to common image formats.
README offers direct image links and batch gallery sharing; controller returns generated gallery keys for created collections.
Gallery create/update accepts an optional password of at least three non-space characters and gallery listing checks it; not an E2EE or security-audit claim.
One-click copy of image embed links with user-defined code format.
README lists generating a QR code from an image's direct link.
Multiple registered users and visitors have separately configurable upload management; registration/password recovery integrate email service.
Guest uploads can be enabled/disabled and have a shared capacity budget; URL upload count limits distinguish unauthenticated from registered users.
Set available user capacity and bulk-generate account-expansion codes; redeeming a valid code increases the account allocation.
Distribution groups associate group name, storage-key ID, user type and compression flag; default group cannot be deleted.
README describes real-time multithreaded review; configuration requires service API credentials and can enable a selected review provider. No on-device or air-gapped guarantee.
Administrator-configurable IP blacklist is explicitly documented.
README documents site-controlled upload APIs and source exposes web/client routes; account token can be regenerated with immediate effect.
Dashboard totals cover own images/galleries/quota usage and, for privileged users, global image/user counts, review and guest-capacity state.
Controller builds twelve monthly counts for a selected year, restricted to current user unless admin requests global data; not a capture-time photo timeline guarantee.
